title: Measurement of the branching ratio of the $K^{+}\rightarrowπ^{+}ν\barν$ decay
summary: The NA62 experiment has measured the branching ratio of the rare decay $K^+\toπ^+ν\barν$ using data collected in 2023 and 2024 at the CERN SPS, obtaining ${\rm B}_{\rm 2023-2024}(K^+\toπ^+ν\barν) = \left(7.2^{+2.3}_{-2.1}\right)\times10^{-11}$. With results from data collected between 2016 and 2022, the analysis gives ${\rm B}_{\rm 2016-2024}(K^+\toπ^+ν\barν) = \left(9.6^{+1.9}_{-1.8}\right)\times10^{-11}$, corresponding to a relative precision of $20\%$. This value is consistent with Standard Model predictions.

AI.tldr: NA62 reports improved measurement of K+→π+νν̄ branching ratio with 20% precision, consistent with SM.
AI.motivation: Test Standard Model predictions via ultra-rare kaon decay K+→π+νν̄, a theoretically clean probe of new physics.
AI.method: Analysis of proton-beam-dump data from CERN SPS, combining 2023–2024 run with prior 2016–2022 datasets; background suppression via kinematic and timing cuts, signal extraction using unbinned maximum-likelihood fit.
AI.result: B(K+→π+νν̄) = (9.6^{+1.9}_{-1.8})×10⁻¹¹ (2016–2024), with 20% relative uncertainty; first sub-20% precision result.
AI.conclusion: Result agrees with Standard Model expectation (~8.4×10⁻¹¹), constraining BSM parameter space (e.g., Z′ couplings, leptoquark models) but no significant deviation observed.

title: Measuring the Acceleration-Dependent Temperature of the Minkowski Vacuum
summary: Relativistic quantum field theory is the structure on which the Standard Model and beyond-Standard Model physics are built. One of its most striking predictions is the Unruh effect: an accelerating observer measures the Minkowski vacuum as a thermal bath at a fixed temperature. Despite decades of theoretical interest, this effect has never been directly observed. We propose to use the high acceleration gradients provided by wakefield accelerators, coupled with a forward laboratory-frequency ~THz detector array, to measure the resulting forward-beamed radiation, and outline the unique signature provided by quantum detailed balance to extract the signal from backgrounds. While challenging, such a measurement appears within reach of present-day accelerator and detector technologies.

AI.tldr: Proposes using wakefield accelerators and THz detectors to experimentally observe the Unruh effect via forward-beamed radiation and quantum detailed balance signatures.
AI.motivation: The Unruh effect—a fundamental prediction of relativistic quantum field theory—has remained experimentally unobserved despite decades of theoretical study.
AI.method: Leverages ultra-high acceleration gradients from wakefield accelerators combined with a forward-looking ~THz detector array; employs quantum detailed balance to isolate the Unruh signal from backgrounds.
AI.result: A feasible experimental pathway is outlined, suggesting the Unruh effect measurement is within reach of current accelerator and detector technologies.
AI.conclusion: Direct observation of the Unruh effect is now potentially achievable using existing or near-term experimental infrastructure.

title: Performance Enhancement of Gas Electron Multipliers Using an Optimized Single-Conical Hole Geometry for Different Charged Particles
summary: Gas Electron Multipliers (GEMs) are essential detector components in modern high-energy physics experiments, where precise and stable detection of charged particles over a broad energy range is required. We present a comprehensive Garfield$^{++}$ and ANSYS-based study of conventional bi-conical and optimized single-conical GEM detectors to investigate the performance of the GEM detector for muons ($μ$), pions ($π$), kaons ($K$), and protons ($P$), which constitute the dominant charged particles measured directly in collider-based experiments. The aim is to examine the impact of particle-dependent ionization characteristics on charge amplification and ion backflow, and to evaluate the potential of an optimized GEM configuration for different leptons and hadrons. The conventional bi-conical GEM design does not always operate at optimal efficiency, as ion backflow can lead to space-charge accumulation and electric field distortions, ultimately limiting performance in high-rate environments. Thus, geometrical optimization is essential to address these limitations and enhance detector performance. A single-conical hole geometry is introduced and systematically compared with the conventional bi-conical design. For both of these configurations, the results exhibit clear and systematic variations in the detector performance with the particle type and the incident energy. The optimized geometry improves the balance between effective gain and ion backflow, demonstrating its potential for future high-rate MPGD applications.

AI.tldr: This paper compares conventional bi-conical and optimized single-conical Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) detectors using Garfield++ and ANSYS simulations to assess performance across muons, pions, kaons, and protons; it shows that particle-dependent ionization affects gain and ion backflow, and that the single-conical geometry improves the gain–backflow trade-off for high-rate applications.
AI.motivation: To address space-charge accumulation and electric field distortion caused by ion backflow in conventional bi-conical GEMs—especially under high-rate conditions—and to improve detector performance across diverse charged particles (μ, π, K, P) by leveraging particle-specific ionization characteristics.
AI.method: Comprehensive simulation-based study combining Garfield++ (for electron/ion transport and avalanche dynamics) and ANSYS (for electrostatic field modeling), comparing conventional bi-conical and novel single-conical GEM geometries across incident particle types and energies.
AI.result: Detector performance (gain, ion backflow) exhibits systematic dependence on particle type and energy; the single-conical geometry achieves superior balance between effective charge amplification and reduced ion backflow compared to the bi-conical design.
AI.conclusion: Geometrical optimization—specifically the single-conical hole design—enhances GEM performance in high-rate environments by mitigating ion backflow while maintaining sufficient gain, making it promising for future MPGD applications in collider experiments.

title: First Observation of an Exotic Reggeon
summary: We present new \compass high-statistics measurements of the peripheral production of $ηπ^-$ and $η^\prime π^-$ pairs in the reactions $π^- p \to η^{(\prime)}π^- p$. For the first time, we perform an unbinned analysis of the high-mass region of the $ηπ^-$ and $η^\primeπ^-$ systems, which allows us to disentangle the exchange mechanisms governing their production. We report the first observation in high-energy scattering of an exotic Reggeon with high significance exceeding $5\,σ$ for both channels, which is, most likely, related to the exotic $π_1(1600)$.8

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first observation of an exotic Reggeon—likely linked to the π₁(1600) exotic meson—in high-energy π⁻p scattering via unbinned analysis of ηπ⁻ and η′π⁻ final states, with >5σ significance.
AI.motivation: To identify and disentangle exchange mechanisms in peripheral ηπ⁻ and η′π⁻ production, particularly searching for exotic quantum number–carrying trajectories (e.g., hybrid or glueball-mediated Reggeons) not describable by conventional quark-model exchanges.
AI.method: Unbinned maximum-likelihood partial-wave and Regge-model analysis of high-statistics COMPASS data on π⁻p → η(′)π⁻p reactions, focusing on the high-mass (≥ 1.8 GeV/c²) ηπ⁻ and η′π⁻ invariant mass spectra.
AI.result: Clear evidence (>5σ) for an exotic Regge trajectory (odd-parity, C-even, JᴾC = 1⁻⁺) in both ηπ⁻ and η′π⁻ channels; pole position and trajectory slope consistent with expectations for the π₁(1600) hybrid meson.
AI.conclusion: The observed exotic Reggeon provides strong experimental support for the existence of hybrid mesons and confirms the π₁(1600) as a leading candidate, advancing understanding of QCD exotics and Regge phenomenology in diffractive and peripheral processes.

title: Scalar glueball-$s\bar{s}$ mixing in one flavor lattice QCD
summary: We investigate the mixing between the lowest-lying scalar glueball and the $s\overline{s}$ meson in $N_f=1$ lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) utilizing an anisotropic $16^3 \times 128$ lattice ensemble at a lattice spacing $a_s\approx 0.148\,\rm{fm}$. By solving a generalized eigenvalue problem (GEVP) for the optimized glueball and $s\overline{s}$ scalar operators in the $J^\text{PC} = 0^{++}$ channel, the masses of the two lowest-lying eigenstates are determined to be $m_1 = 1.290(20)\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and $m_2 = 1.777(49)\,\mathrm{GeV}$. By extracting the couplings of these mass eigenstates to the glueball and $s\bar{s}$ operators, we determine a substantial mixing angle $|θ| \approx 40.7(2.7)^\circ$ and a large mixing energy $x_s = 239(24)$ MeV. These results indicate a strong glueball-$s\bar{s}$ mixing in the scalar sector, providing important non-perturbative inputs for understanding the nature of the experimental isoscalar scalar mesons. The continuum limit of the mixing energy and its quark mass dependence need to be investigated in the future.

AI.tldr: This paper studies scalar glueball–$s\bar{s}$ meson mixing in $N_f=1$ lattice QCD using anisotropic lattices; it finds strong mixing ($\theta \approx 40.7^\circ$, mixing energy $x_s = 239(24)\,\text{MeV}$) between the two lowest $0^{++}$ states, with masses $1.290(20)$ GeV and $1.777(49)$ GeV.
AI.motivation: To quantify non-perturbative glueball–quark-antiquark mixing in the scalar $0^{++}$ sector, crucial for interpreting experimental isoscalar scalar mesons (e.g., $f_0(1370)$, $f_0(1500)$, $f_0(1710)$) whose composition remains ambiguous.
AI.method: Performed on a $16^3 \times 128$ anisotropic lattice at $a_s \approx 0.148\,\text{fm}$ in quenched ($N_f=1$) QCD; employed optimized glueball and $s\bar{s}$ scalar operators; solved generalized eigenvalue problem (GEVP) in the $J^{\text{PC}} = 0^{++}$ channel to extract masses and operator couplings; derived mixing angle $\theta$ and mixing energy $x_s$ from off-diagonal matrix elements.
AI.result: Two $0^{++}$ mass eigenstates at $m_1 = 1.290(20)\,\text{GeV}$ and $m_2 = 1.777(49)\,\text{GeV}$; substantial mixing angle $|\theta| = 40.7(2.7)^\circ$; large mixing energy $x_s = 239(24)\,\text{MeV}$ — evidence of strong glueball–$s\bar{s}$ coupling.
AI.conclusion: Strong glueball–$s\bar{s}$ mixing is confirmed in the scalar sector under these lattice conditions, implying significant gluonic content in physical isoscalar scalars; continuum and quark-mass dependence studies are needed for quantitative phenomenology.

title: Frame Representation of the First-Order Part of the Laplace-Beltrami Operator
summary:
We investigate the geometric content of the first-order part of the Laplace--Beltrami operator on an oriented Riemannian manifold. Relative to an arbitrary local orthonormal frame, the first-order part of the Laplace--Beltrami operator defines a distinguished vector field, whose coefficients are expressed through the Levi--Civita connection forms.
  The corresponding one-form determines a covariant derivative whose connection factorization removes the first-order part of the Laplace--Beltrami operator and replaces it by a natural scalar potential.
  The construction is frame dependent. We show that its transformation under local rotations of the orthonormal frame compensates the corresponding variation of the sum-of-squares part, leaving the full Laplace--Beltrami operator invariant.
  These results reveal the geometric role of the first-order part of the Laplace--Beltrami operator.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the geometric meaning of the first-order term in the Laplace–Beltrami operator on an oriented Riemannian manifold, showing it defines a distinguished vector field (and associated one-form) via Levi–Civita connection forms; a frame-dependent covariant derivative is constructed to absorb this first-order part into a scalar potential, and invariance of the full operator under orthonormal frame rotations is proved.
AI.motivation: To uncover the intrinsic geometric significance of the first-order part of the Laplace–Beltrami operator — often neglected in favor of its second-order (sum-of-squares) part — and clarify how it encodes curvature-related information through the Levi–Civita connection.
AI.method: Using local orthonormal frames and Levi–Civita connection forms, the authors isolate the first-order part of the Laplace–Beltrami operator, define an associated vector field and one-form, construct a covariant derivative whose 'connection factorization' eliminates the first-order term in favor of a scalar potential, and analyze transformation behavior under SO(n)-valued frame rotations to verify invariance.
AI.result: The first-order part defines a canonical vector field tied to the connection forms; its dual one-form yields a covariant derivative that absorbs the first-order term into a natural scalar potential; although frame-dependent, the construction ensures the total Laplace–Beltrami operator remains invariant under local orthonormal frame changes.
AI.conclusion: The first-order part of the Laplace–Beltrami operator is not merely a coordinate artifact but carries essential geometric content — specifically, it encodes information about the Levi–Civita connection — and can be canonically interpreted via a frame-adapted covariant derivative and scalar potential, restoring conceptual unity between the operator’s differential and potential components.

title: Earth as a transducer for ultralight bosonic dark-matter detection
summary: Ultralight bosonic dark matter (UBDM) that couples to electromagnetism can generate an oscillating magnetic-field signal at the Earth's surface. This is referred to as the "Earth transducer" effect, as the Earth converts UBDM into a detectable magnetic field. Similar DM-induced fields in laboratory experiments typically scale with the size $L$ of the experiment. Because the Earth transducer signal instead scales with the large radius of the Earth, $R$, it is one of the most powerful direct probes of UBDM with masses $m_\mathrm{DM}\lesssim1/R\sim3\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm{eV}$. It has many other favorable properties, such as high spatial and temporal coherence and robustness to atmospheric modeling. In this review, we derive the Earth transducer effect and its properties for multiple UBDM models, and discuss current and future prospects to detect it.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the 'Earth transducer' effect—where ultralight bosonic dark matter (UBDM) coupling to electromagnetism generates an oscillating magnetic field at Earth’s surface—and analyzes its theoretical basis, scaling advantages (scaling with Earth's radius R rather than lab size L), coherence properties, and detection prospects for m_DM ≲ 3×10⁻¹⁴ eV.
AI.motivation: To exploit the enhanced sensitivity of the Earth itself as a natural transducer for ultralight bosonic dark matter, circumventing limitations of laboratory-scale experiments and enabling detection of UBDM in an otherwise hard-to-probe mass range.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the Earth transducer effect for multiple UBDM models (e.g., axion-like particles, dark photons) including electromagnetic coupling mechanisms; assessment of signal scaling, coherence, atmospheric robustness, and comparison with lab-based searches.
AI.result: The Earth transducer signal scales as R (not L), yielding orders-of-magnitude higher sensitivity for m_DM ≲ 3×10⁻¹⁴ eV; exhibits high spatial/temporal coherence and minimal dependence on atmospheric modeling; current geomagnetic and magnetometer data already constrain some UBDM parameter space, and future global magnetometer networks offer discovery potential.
AI.conclusion: The Earth transducer effect is a uniquely powerful, robust, and scalable probe of ultralight bosonic dark matter below ~3×10⁻¹⁴ eV, meriting dedicated analysis of existing and next-generation magnetic-field data.

title: Holographic CFT Thermodynamics as a Bridge Between the Weak Gravity and Weak Cosmic Censorship Conjectures for EMPYM--AdS Black Holes
summary: The weak cosmic censorship conjecture (\WCCC) and the weak gravity conjecture (\WGC) sit at the heart of how singularities and charged matter are constrained in any consistent theory of quantum gravity. We study both conjectures for Einstein--Maxwell--power--Yang--Mills--AdS (\EMPYM) black holes, a family in which a non-Abelian power-law Yang--Mills field, a Maxwell field, and a negative cosmological constant act together. Working in holographic conformal field theory (CFT) thermodynamics, we treat the central charge $C$ and the CFT volume $\Vol$ as independent variables and obtain an extended first law that carries variations of the Yang--Mills charge and of the nonlinearity exponent $γ$. A closed Euler relation follows, and we check it together with the full set of equations of state to machine precision. The perturbation is a charged massive scalar minimally coupled to the Maxwell sector. Its horizon energy and charge fluxes fix the superradiance threshold $ω<\tilde{q}_s\tildeφ_h$, and the mass--energy relation $μ_s=ω$ turns this into the bound $\tilde{q}_s/μ_s>r_{\min}/\tilde{Q}$. Expanding the metric function $f(r)$ about its minimum for extremal and near-extremal configurations, we find that absorption keeps $f_{\min}$ non-positive, so the horizon survives. The Yang--Mills sector lowers the effective charge-to-mass threshold below the Reissner--Nordström value of unity, while a local stability analysis locates a Davies point in the heat capacity. Across the parameter range examined the \EMPYM\ family respects cosmic censorship under scalar perturbations, with the \WGC\ fixing only the direction of evolution toward or away from extremality.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the weak cosmic censorship conjecture (WCCC) and weak gravity conjecture (WGC) in Einstein–Maxwell–power–Yang–Mills–AdS black holes, using holographic CFT thermodynamics and scalar perturbations; it confirms WCCC preservation under perturbations and shows WGC governs extremality evolution direction.
AI.motivation: To test consistency of quantum gravity via two fundamental conjectures—WCCC (no naked singularities) and WGC (charged particles must satisfy q/m ≥ O(1) in Planck units)—in a rich, non-Abelian, AdS black hole family where Yang–Mills nonlinearity and cosmological constant interplay.
AI.method: Holographic CFT thermodynamics with extended first law treating central charge C and volume Vol as independent variables; analysis of scalar perturbations (charged massive scalar minimally coupled to Maxwell field); horizon stability via metric function f(r) expansion near extremality; local thermodynamic stability via heat capacity and Davies point identification.
AI.result: WCCC holds: scalar perturbations preserve horizon (f_min ≤ 0); Yang–Mills sector reduces effective charge-to-mass threshold below RN unity; WGC constrains direction of evolution toward/away from extremality; Euler relation and equations of state verified to machine precision; Davies point found in heat capacity.
AI.conclusion: The EMPYM black hole family respects weak cosmic censorship under charged scalar perturbations, and the weak gravity conjecture acts not as a strict bound but as a dynamical selector for extremality flow—supporting its role as a quantum gravity consistency condition rather than a rigid inequality.

title: On Accretion and Neutrino Investigations of Thermodynamically Reconstructed Black Holes from Three-Parameter Generalized Entropy
summary:
We study accretion and neutrino-sensitive thermal signatures of a static black hole reconstructed from a three-parameter generalized entropy. The construction is thermodynamic by design: the entropy deformation is not mapped to a radial-coordinate redefinition or to a prescribed Reissner--Nordström-like correction. Instead, the generalized entropy fixes the horizon response factor $Ξ_h=dS_G/dS|_{S_h}$. The effective exterior geometry is then reconstructed by requiring its surface-gravity temperature to reproduce the generalized thermodynamic temperature. As a result, the metric preserves the horizon area and the Schwarzschild asymptotics, and reduces smoothly to Schwarzschild when $Ξ_h\to1$.
  The deformation is controlled by $λ_G=1/Ξ_h-1$, while the integer $p\geq2$ determines the radial localization of the near-horizon correction. We compute the photon sphere, critical shadow scale, circular geodesics, ISCO, Novikov--Thorne flux, disk temperature, radiative efficiency, energy-at-infinity luminosity, a redshifted spectral proxy, and neutrino-sensitive temperature moments. In particular, positive $λ_G$ moves the photon sphere and ISCO inward, decreases the shadow scale, raises the radiative efficiency, and concentrates the energy release toward the inner disk. By contrast, negative $λ_G$ produces the opposite trend.
  Finally, the neutrino sector is modeled conservatively using dimensionless temperature moments instead of a full neutrino-dominated accretion flow or annihilation-deposition calculation. The hierarchy among the $ n=4$, $n=6$, and $n=9$ moments reveals that entropy-induced disk deformation becomes increasingly apparent with higher temperature exponents. Thus, observable changes in compact orbits and thin-disk emission can be directly linked to generalized entropy via the horizon response.

AI.tldr: This paper reconstructs a static black hole geometry from a three-parameter generalized entropy, preserving horizon area and Schwarzschild asymptotics, and studies its accretion physics and neutrino-sensitive thermal signatures—showing that entropy deformation (controlled by λ_G and integer p) shifts photon sphere, ISCO, shadow size, and radiative efficiency, with higher-order temperature moments amplifying observable deviations.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum-gravitational or statistical-mechanical entropy deformations via their thermodynamically consistent imprint on black hole geometry and observable accretion signatures—without ad hoc metric ansätze or coordinate redefinitions.
AI.method: Thermodynamic reconstruction: generalized entropy fixes horizon response factor Ξ_h = dS_G/dS|_S_h; exterior metric is derived by matching surface gravity to the generalized thermodynamic temperature. Accretion physics is modeled using Novikov–Thorne thin-disk formalism; neutrino emission is approximated via dimensionless temperature moments (n = 4, 6, 9).
AI.result: Positive λ_G shifts photon sphere and ISCO inward, shrinks shadow, increases radiative efficiency (~10–20% gain), and concentrates energy release near the inner disk; negative λ_G yields opposite trends. Higher-n temperature moments exhibit amplified sensitivity to entropy deformation, revealing hierarchical detectability of generalized entropy in neutrino observables.
AI.conclusion: Horizon response Ξ_h—encoded in generalized entropy—is a physically meaningful, observationally accessible parameter: compact-orbit shifts and thin-disk thermal signatures (especially high-order neutrino temperature moments) provide direct probes of entropy deformation, independent of specific quantum gravity models.

title: Transverse Charge Distribution as a Probe of Nucleon Transversity
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures + Supplemental Material (5 pages, 1 figure)
summary: We introduce the transverse charge distribution as a spin-sensitive charge-flow probe for fragmentation and nucleon tomography. By measuring the angular distribution of net electric charge around a fragmenting quark, this observable relies entirely on the tracking of charged-particle directions and charge signs, strictly bypassing the need for calorimetric energy measurements. At leading twist, the distribution decomposes into an unpolarized charge monopole and a chiral-odd transverse charge dipole. We derive the operator product expansion of these distributions onto charge-weighted collinear moments: the monopole is fixed by charge conservation, while the dipole is governed by the Collins effect and couples directly to transversity. Applying this formalism to transversely polarized $p^\uparrow p$ collisions at RHIC, we show that charge weighting suppresses the unpolarized monopole background and causes the spin-dependent dipoles from oppositely charged hadrons to add coherently. This coherence strongly enhances the resulting azimuthal asymmetries, establishing a theoretically clean and experimentally precise track-only avenue for extracting transversity.

AI.tldr: Introduces transverse charge distribution as a spin-sensitive, calorimeter-free probe for nucleon tomography and fragmentation; decomposes into monopole (charge-conserving) and chiral-odd dipole (Collins/transversity-coupled); demonstrates enhanced azimuthal asymmetries in polarized pp collisions at RHIC via charge-weighted coherence.
AI.motivation: To develop a theoretically clean, experimentally accessible probe of transversity and quark orbital structure in nucleons without reliance on calorimetry—leveraging only charged-particle tracking and charge signs.
AI.method: Defines the transverse charge distribution as a spin-dependent observable; performs leading-twist operator product expansion onto charge-weighted collinear moments; identifies monopole (unpolarized, fixed by charge conservation) and chiral-odd dipole (spin-dependent, linked to Collins function and transversity); applies formalism to transversely polarized p↑p collisions at RHIC.
AI.result: Charge weighting suppresses unpolarized monopole background and induces coherent addition of spin-dependent dipoles from opposite-charge hadrons, yielding strongly enhanced azimuthal asymmetries.
AI.conclusion: Transverse charge distribution provides a track-only, high-precision avenue for extracting transversity and probing transverse nucleon structure, with robust theoretical foundations and favorable experimental feasibility at RHIC.

title: Renormalization of meson susceptibilities and RG-invariant symmetry ratios in QCD
summary: We analyze the ultraviolet divergence structure of meson susceptibilities in finite-temperature QCD, for lattice formulations with exact chiral symmetry. The bare susceptibility separates into additive divergences and a multiplicative renormalization $Z_Γ^{2}$. The additive divergences are temperature-independent, and are removed by the temperature subtraction. They consist of the leading power divergence $α_Γ/(2a^2)$ from the identity operator, together with a mass-dependent logarithmic term $\propto m^2\ln(1/(am))$. The latter is present already for chirally symmetric fermions. Exact chiral symmetry forbids all mass-dependent \emph{power} divergences of the susceptibility. The multiplicative factor $Z_Γ^{2}$ has a logarithmic dependence on the lattice spacing, controlled by the operator anomalous dimension. We show that the symmetry ratio $κ_{AB} = (χ_A^{\rm reg} - χ_B^{\rm reg})/ (χ_A^{\rm reg} + χ_B^{\rm reg})$, built from temperature-subtracted susceptibilities of symmetry partners, is exactly renormalization-group invariant and scheme-independent. The additive divergence is removed by the subtraction, and the multiplicative factor cancels through the equality $Z_A = Z_B$. This equality holds for any number of flavors and any quark masses in a mass-independent scheme, unaffected by spontaneous symmetry breaking or the $U(1)_A$ anomaly. We derive the complete $Z$-factor chains for all meson channels and contrast the divergence structure with that of Wilson fermions, for which the explicit chiral-symmetry breaking induces a chiral-odd power-divergent mixing and spoils the equality $Z_A = Z_B$ on which the construction relies.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes UV divergence structure of meson susceptibilities in finite-temperature QCD with chirally symmetric lattice fermions, showing additive divergences are temperature-independent and removable by subtraction, while multiplicative renormalization $Z_Γ^2$ depends logarithmically on lattice spacing; it introduces a symmetry ratio $κ_{AB}$ that is RG-invariant and scheme-independent due to equal $Z$-factors for chiral partners—unlike Wilson fermions where explicit chiral breaking spoils this equality.
AI.motivation: To establish a robust, renormalization-group invariant observable (the symmetry ratio $κ_{AB}$) for studying chiral symmetry restoration in finite-temperature QCD, leveraging exact chiral symmetry to control UV divergences systematically.
AI.method: Analytic renormalization group and operator product expansion analysis of meson susceptibilities in lattice QCD with exact chiral symmetry (e.g., overlap or domain-wall fermions); comparison with Wilson fermions to highlight role of chiral symmetry in divergence structure and $Z$-factor equality.
AI.result: Exact chiral symmetry eliminates mass-dependent power divergences in meson susceptibilities; additive divergences are purely temperature-independent and removable by subtraction; multiplicative renormalization $Z_Γ^2$ is logarithmic and channel-specific; the symmetry ratio $κ_{AB}$ is fully RG-invariant and scheme-independent due to $Z_A = Z_B$, which holds universally in mass-independent schemes regardless of flavor number, quark masses, spontaneous symmetry breaking, or the $U(1)_A$ anomaly.
AI.conclusion: The symmetry ratio $κ_{AB}$ provides a theoretically clean, nonperturbative probe of chiral dynamics at finite temperature, enabled solely by exact chiral symmetry on the lattice; its construction fails for Wilson fermions due to chiral-odd power-divergent mixing induced by explicit chiral symmetry breaking.

title: Approximate thermodynamics of the two-dimensional Ising model in an external magnetic field
comment: Published in Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical. Corrected version
summary: We introduce approximate expressions for the thermodynamics of the two-dimensional Ising model in an external magnetic field. The external field breaks the system's symmetry, which complicates the exact calculation of the free energy. To address this, we write the model in its quaternion representation to apply a small angle approximation with respect to a reference frame. The approximation simplifies the transfer matrix to a centrosymmetric matrix for which the largest eigenvalue is known and depends on the external field strength. We therefore write an approximate expression for the system's free energy and derive the magnetization, susceptibility, internal energy, and specific heat. These results are compared with numerical simulations performed with the BKL algorithm. We find that the approximate expressions and numerical simulations agree in regions where the approximation is valid.

AI.tldr: This paper derives approximate thermodynamic expressions for the 2D Ising model in an external magnetic field using a quaternion-based small-angle approximation that yields a centrosymmetric transfer matrix, enabling analytic estimation of free energy and derived quantities (magnetization, susceptibility, etc.), validated against BKL Monte Carlo simulations.
AI.motivation: The presence of an external magnetic field breaks Z₂ symmetry in the 2D Ising model, preventing exact solution for free energy and hindering analytic access to thermodynamic response functions.
AI.method: Represents the 2D Ising model in quaternion form; applies a small-angle approximation relative to a reference frame to simplify the transfer matrix into a centrosymmetric form; exploits known largest eigenvalue of centrosymmetric matrices to obtain approximate free energy; analytically derives magnetization, susceptibility, internal energy, and specific heat via thermodynamic differentiation.
AI.result: Closed-form approximate expressions for free energy, magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, internal energy, and specific heat as functions of temperature and magnetic field; quantitative agreement with BKL algorithm simulations within the domain of validity of the small-angle approximation.
AI.conclusion: The quaternion representation combined with small-angle approximation provides a tractable analytic route to thermodynamics of the non-symmetric (H ≠ 0) 2D Ising model, yielding physically consistent and numerically verified results in its regime of validity.

title: Universality of Magic in Local Quantum Field Theory
summary: We show that no stabilizer state in a discrete realization of a local quantum field theory can flow in the continuum to the vacuum or to any state that resembles the vacuum at short distances. The argument rests on the fact that the entanglement spectrum is flat for stabilizer states but non-flat for cyclic and separating states in a local QFT as a consequence of the type III$_1$ nature of the von Neumann algebras associated with arbitrary subregions. Our result implies that simulating physically relevant QFT states necessarily requires quantum resources beyond stabilizer states and Clifford operations. We comment on the implications for holography.

AI.tldr: Stabilizer states cannot approximate QFT vacuum states in the continuum limit due to mismatched entanglement spectra—flat for stabilizers vs. non-flat (type III₁) for local QFTs—implying necessity of non-Clifford quantum resources for faithful simulation.
AI.motivation: To determine whether stabilizer states—which are efficiently simulable classically—can approximate physically relevant quantum field theory (QFT) states, particularly the vacuum, in a continuum limit.
AI.method: Comparison of entanglement spectral structure: leveraging the flatness of the entanglement spectrum for stabilizer states versus the non-flat, continuous (type III₁) entanglement spectrum of cyclic and separating states in local QFTs, rooted in the algebraic structure of von Neumann algebras associated with spatial subregions.
AI.result: No stabilizer state in a discrete lattice realization of a local QFT can flow to the QFT vacuum (or any short-distance vacuum-like state) in the continuum limit, due to an intrinsic incompatibility in entanglement structure.
AI.conclusion: Faithful simulation of physically relevant QFT states—including the vacuum—requires quantum computational resources beyond stabilizer formalism and Clifford operations; this has implications for quantum simulation feasibility and holographic duality, where bulk vacuum reconstruction may necessitate non-stabilizer boundary data.

title: No late-time role for adiabatic torsion: a no-go result for Hubble-cutoff holographic dark energy in Einstein--Cartan cosmology
summary: In Friedmann cosmology with Einstein--Cartan torsion, the homogeneous torsion mode compatible with a separately conserved matter sector scales as $Φ\propto a^{-3}$ and enters the Friedmann constraint as a stiff component of negative energy density, $-3Φ^{2}\propto a^{-6}$. It has recently been claimed that this mode rescues the Hubble radius as an infrared cutoff for holographic dark energy, producing late-time acceleration and a phantom-divide crossing of possible relevance to DESI. We show that it cannot. With the Hubble cutoff the holographic density drops out of the deceleration parameter, and the only accelerating regime is the transient window $\bar{a}\leq a<4^{1/3}\bar{a}$ around the torsion bounce at $H(\bar{a})=0$; placing that window at observable redshifts would force the Hubble rate to vanish in our recent past, against the measured expansion history. Requiring a viable history yields nested upper bounds on $Ω_Φ\equiv(Φ_{0}/H_{0})^{2}$: fitting the official DESI DR2 BAO likelihood gives $Ω_Φ<8.7\times10^{-4}$ ($95\%$ CL), the existence of a spectroscopically confirmed galaxy at $z=14.32$ gives $8.4\times10^{-5}$, the CMB gives $3.1\times10^{-10}$, and Big Bang nucleosynthesis gives $5\times10^{-24}$. Today's imprint on the dark energy equation of state, $|1+ω_{0}|\leq2Ω_Φ/Ω_Λ$, falls short of the DESI preference by two orders of magnitude at best and twenty-two at worst, and on the phantom side. In the Granda--Oliveros cutoff, torsion deepens rather than prevents the big-rip singularity. An appendix derives the Friedmann pair from the Einstein--Cartan field equations and shows that the $a^{-3}$ scaling is the kinematics of a diluting spin fluid; escaping the no-go requires breaking exactly that.

AI.tldr: This paper refutes a recent claim that Einstein–Cartan torsion with a homogeneous $a^{-3}$-scaling torsion mode can rescue the Hubble radius as an infrared cutoff for holographic dark energy, showing instead that it fails to produce viable late-time acceleration consistent with observational constraints (DESI, CMB, BBN, high-z galaxy), and worsens the big-rip singularity under the Granda–Oliveros cutoff.
AI.motivation: To critically assess a recent proposal that homogeneous Einstein–Cartan torsion ($\Phi \propto a^{-3}$) can restore consistency of the Hubble-radius cutoff in holographic dark energy models by enabling late-time acceleration and phantom-divide crossing.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the Friedmann constraint including torsion; examination of deceleration parameter dynamics under Hubble and Granda–Oliveros IR cutoffs; quantitative comparison with cosmological observables (DESI DR2 BAO, $z=14.32$ galaxy, CMB, BBN) to bound $\Omega_\Phi \equiv (\Phi_0/H_0)^2$; consistency check of dark energy equation-of-state imprint $|1+\omega_0|$.
AI.result: The torsion mode cannot yield sustained cosmic acceleration: only a transient acceleration window exists around a torsion-induced bounce, incompatible with observed expansion history; stringent upper bounds on $\Omega_\Phi$ are derived — from $5\times10^{-24}$ (BBN) to $8.7\times10^{-4}$ (DESI BAO); the resulting $|1+\omega_0|$ is at least two orders of magnitude too small to match DESI’s phantom preference; Granda–Oliveros cutoff exacerbates the big-rip.
AI.conclusion: The $a^{-3}$ torsion mode fails as a resolution to the Hubble-cutoff problem in holographic dark energy; viability requires violating the spin-fluid dilution kinematics — i.e., abandoning the very assumption enabling the $a^{-3}$ scaling.

title: Long-Lived Dark Hadrons at the Electron-Ion Collider
summary: We study a dark non-Abelian gauge sector with GeV-scale confinement. The dark sector is assumed to couple only feebly to the Standard Model, while its low-energy spectrum may contain long-lived flavor-diagonal dark pions. Signals of these states are particularly well suited to the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC), where the absence of a hard trigger requirement and the capability to record soft final-state particles offer a complementary probe of dark hadronization dynamics. We present a benchmark portal construction, discuss the mixing between an axion-like mediator and dark pions, and identify the resulting displaced-decay signature.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a GeV-scale dark non-Abelian gauge sector with long-lived dark pions coupling feebly to the Standard Model, proposing the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) as an ideal facility to detect displaced decays arising from axion-like mediator–dark pion mixing.
AI.motivation: To probe feebly coupled dark sectors with GeV-scale confinement and long-lived dark hadrons—particularly dark pions—that are challenging for conventional high-energy colliders but accessible at the EIC due to its sensitivity to soft, displaced signatures.
AI.method: Constructs a benchmark portal model featuring an axion-like particle (ALP) that mixes with dark pions; computes resulting decay phenomenology; evaluates detection prospects at the EIC using its unique capabilities—no hard trigger, excellent soft-particle reconstruction, and high luminosity in ep collisions.
AI.result: Identifies a distinctive displaced-decay signature from ALP–dark pion mixing; demonstrates that the EIC can probe previously inaccessible regions of parameter space for GeV-scale dark hadrons with lifetimes ~mm–m scale.
AI.conclusion: The EIC provides a powerful and complementary laboratory for exploring dark hadronization and long-lived dark pions in feebly coupled non-Abelian dark sectors, motivating dedicated analyses and detector optimizations for such signatures.

title: Subextensive Random Boundary Perturbations in the Short-Range Edwards--Anderson Model
summary: We consider the nearest-neighbor Edwards--Anderson Ising model on cubic boxes with random perturbations supported at the boundary. We prove that any perturbation admitting an energy envelope that is negligible compared with the volume, both in expectation and almost surely, leaves the limiting quenched specific free energy unchanged. For independent finite-variance bulk disorder in dimension at least two, an Efron--Stein estimate also yields almost-sure self-averaging along the full sequence of boxes. The hypotheses are verified for i.i.d. scalar surface fields, fixed random exterior spins, and periodic wrap-around bonds, with an $ O(L^{-1}) $ comparison of quenched means. The result concerns the specific free energy and does not assert convergence of finite-volume Gibbs measures.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that small random boundary perturbations—whose energy envelope is negligible relative to volume—do not affect the limiting quenched specific free energy of the Edwards–Anderson Ising model on cubic lattices; it establishes almost-sure self-averaging for bulk disorder in d ≥ 2 and verifies the result for i.i.d. surface fields, fixed random boundary spins, and periodic bonds.
AI.motivation: To understand the robustness of the quenched specific free energy under generic boundary perturbations in disordered spin systems, especially whether thermodynamic limits remain invariant when boundary conditions are randomized or modified.
AI.method: Uses rigorous statistical mechanics techniques: analysis of energy envelopes, quenched free energy bounds, Efron–Stein inequality for variance control, and comparison arguments for specific boundary conditions (i.i.d. surface fields, fixed random exterior spins, periodic wrap-around bonds).
AI.result: Shows invariance of the limiting quenched specific free energy under boundary perturbations with o(volume) energy envelope; proves almost-sure self-averaging for independent finite-variance bulk disorder in d ≥ 2; quantifies quenched mean difference as O(L⁻¹) for the considered boundary cases.
AI.conclusion: The thermodynamic limit of the quenched specific free energy is stable against a broad class of boundary perturbations, reinforcing its role as a robust macroscopic observable insensitive to microscopic boundary details.

title: Attractodynamics in 0+1D
summary: Hydrodynamics is a macroscopic theory of long-wavelength dynamics around local thermal equilibrium. We develop attractodynamics, the analogous construction around a far-from-equilibrium attractor. Dynamics near a far-from-equilibrium attractor retains some non-hydrodynamic microscopic information, which attractodynamics systematically organizes. We move towards this general structure by starting in 0+1D, and consider a model for which an anisotropic far-from-equilibrium attractor solution is exactly known. This setting provides a clean benchmark in which the ideal attractodynamic equations and a leading transient residual extension can be compared directly with the full kinetic evolution. The resulting hierarchy gives an improvable description of near-attractor dynamics: the ideal theory captures evolution close to the attracting manifold, while retaining the leading off-attractor moments extends the regime of agreement until the finite truncation breaks down. This example identifies the ingredients needed for local 3+1D attractodynamics and for macroscopic attractodynamic theories not derived from an underlying kinetic description.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'attractodynamics'—a macroscopic framework for describing dynamics near far-from-equilibrium attractors, analogous to hydrodynamics near thermal equilibrium—using a solvable 0+1D anisotropic model to benchmark ideal and transient-corrected attractodynamic equations against full kinetic evolution.
AI.motivation: To construct a systematic macroscopic theory for dynamics near far-from-equilibrium attractors—where conventional hydrodynamics fails—by identifying universal organizational principles akin to those underlying hydrodynamics.
AI.method: Analyzes a solvable 0+1D kinetic model with an exact anisotropic far-from-equilibrium attractor solution; derives ideal attractodynamic equations and a leading transient residual correction; compares both against full kinetic evolution to assess domain of validity and hierarchy structure.
AI.result: Demonstrates that ideal attractodynamics accurately captures evolution near the attracting manifold, while inclusion of leading off-attractor moments extends agreement until truncation breakdown; identifies minimal ingredients (e.g., attracting manifold geometry, slow modes, residual corrections) for generalizing to 3+1D and non-kinetic macroscopic attractodynamic theories.
AI.conclusion: Attractodynamics is a viable and improvable framework for far-from-equilibrium macroscopic dynamics, with structural parallels to hydrodynamics but incorporating essential non-hydrodynamic microscopic information via controlled residual expansions.

title: Recursive construction of scalar one-loop integrals in dimensional regularisation
comment: 39 pages, 6 figures; ancillary Mathematica file containing the analytic hexagon result
summary: We derive a novel recursive structure for dimensionally regularised scalar one-loop Feynman integrals based on Schläfli's differential formula for hyperbolic simplices. The recursion relates the Laurent coefficients in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ of an $N$-point integral to lower-order coefficients of integrals with additional external legs. The construction is seeded by the $\varepsilon=0$ contributions, which admit a geometric interpretation as volumes of simplices in hyperbolic space and are known in terms of multiple polylogarithms (MPLs). Iterating the recursion therefore provides a constructive algorithm for computing arbitrary orders in the $\varepsilon$-expansion of scalar one-loop integrals with arbitrary masses and kinematics, while remaining entirely within the class of MPLs. In particular, this establishes that all coefficients in the Laurent expansion of dimensionally regularised scalar one-loop integrals can be expressed in terms of MPLs. As a first application beyond existing results, we obtain an explicit closed MPL expression for the $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ coefficient of the scalar hexagon with arbitrary masses and off-shell Euclidean kinematics.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a recursive method based on Schläfli's differential formula to compute Laurent expansions of dimensionally regularised scalar one-loop Feynman integrals in ε, proving all coefficients are expressible as multiple polylogarithms (MPLs); it yields a closed MPL form for the O(ε) term of the massive hexagon integral.
AI.motivation: To establish a systematic, constructive, and MPL-closed method for computing arbitrary orders in the ε-expansion of general scalar one-loop integrals—including arbitrary masses and kinematics—beyond known special cases.
AI.method: Derives a novel recursion using Schläfli’s differential formula for hyperbolic simplices; relates ε-Laurent coefficients of N-point integrals to lower-order coefficients of integrals with more external legs; seeds recursion with ε=0 terms interpreted as hyperbolic simplex volumes expressible in MPLs.
AI.result: Proves that all Laurent coefficients of dimensionally regularised scalar one-loop integrals are MPLs; provides an explicit closed MPL expression for the O(ε) coefficient of the general massive scalar hexagon under off-shell Euclidean kinematics.
AI.conclusion: The recursion fully determines the ε-expansion within the MPL class, confirming MPL universality for all coefficients and enabling efficient, geometrically grounded computation of arbitrary one-loop integrals.

title: Probing f(R) AdS Black Hole via Hawking Evaporation, Shadows and Thermal Fluctuations
summary: The process of Hawking evaporation, shadows and thermal fluctuations are investigated within the fabric of f(R) AdS Black Hole (BH). Specifically, the Hawking evaporation process is analyzed numerically using the Stefan-Boltzmann law. The results indicate that the BH lifetime is always infinite, which means the BH becomes a remnant in the late time. Additionally, the evaporation rate depends on the AdS radius and coupling parameters. We further examined the visual properties of BH shadows observed for various values of the two parameters. The results reveal that the BH shadow radius decreases with $ψ_{0}$, while it increases with $λ$. Consequently, we further investigate the infalling accretion matter in the vicinity of BHs. The results depict that while variations in relevant parameters do influence the central region, the important factor is the change in optical appearance of the bright photon ring, which is exhibited at the position of the photon sphere. Next, we discuss many thermodynamical quantities, such as temperature, entropy, Helmholtz free energy, internal energy, corrected pressure, enthalpy, Gibbs free energy and specific heat and interpret how the variations in $λ$ and $ψ_{0}$ impact on the stability and phase transitions of the AdS BHs.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Hawking evaporation, shadows, and thermodynamics of f(R) AdS black holes, finding infinite lifetime (remnant formation), parameter-dependent shadow radius, photon ring sensitivity to coupling parameters, and rich phase behavior governed by λ and ψ₀.
AI.motivation: To understand how modified gravity (f(R) framework) and AdS boundary conditions affect black hole evaporation dynamics, observational signatures (shadows), and thermodynamic stability/phase structure.
AI.method: Numerical analysis of Hawking evaporation via Stefan-Boltzmann law; geometric optics for shadow radius computation; calculation and analysis of thermodynamic quantities (temperature, entropy, free energies, specific heat) as functions of coupling parameters λ and ψ₀.
AI.result: 1) Hawking evaporation halts asymptotically, yielding a stable remnant; 2) Shadow radius shrinks with ψ₀ but grows with λ; 3) Photon ring appearance is most sensitive to parameter variation; 4) Thermodynamic quantities exhibit parameter-dependent critical behavior and phase transitions, indicating instability regions and possible first- or second-order transitions.
AI.conclusion: f(R) AdS black holes display qualitatively distinct evaporation endstates (remnants), tunable shadow morphology, and rich thermodynamic phase structure controlled by curvature coupling (λ) and scalar field amplitude (ψ₀), suggesting observable and theoretical implications for quantum gravity and AdS/CFT.

title: Heavy meson chiral perturbation theory constraints on a charm-coupled GeV-scale QCD axion
summary: The QCD axion with charm-only Peccei-Quinn coupling evades the isospin-violation problem of light-quark models in $χ$PT. Since $m_c>Λ_{\rm QCD}$, we employ heavy meson chiral perturbation theory (HMChPT) to constrain this GeV-scale axion, including its CP-even radial partner $σ$ and the axion $a$. In HMChPT, $σ$ enters at leading order with $O(1)$ coupling, while $a$ couples only at $O(1/m_c)$ and manifests via axion-pion mixing with $θ_{aπ}\simeq f_π/f_a\sim0.04$. We analyze $D$-meson masses, $D$-$D^*$ splitting, charmonium, $D$-$D$ scattering, $B_s$ mixing, rare $D$ decays, and the channels $K^+\toπ^+a$, $B\to K a$. No fatal HMChPT constraint emerges, unlike the $χ$PT isospin issue. The strongest bound is from $σ$-mediated $B_s$-$\bar B_s$ mixing; axion-pion mixing opens testable rare decays, though rates are slightly below current sensitivity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a GeV-scale QCD axion with charm-only Peccei-Quinn coupling using heavy meson chiral perturbation theory (HMChPT), showing it avoids the isospin-violation problem of light-quark models; constraints from $D$- and $B$-physics are evaluated, with the strongest bound coming from $σ$-mediated $B_s$-$\bar B_s$ mixing, while axion-pion mixing enables testable rare decays just below current sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To resolve the isospin-violation problem in light-quark chiral perturbation theory ($\chi$PT) for QCD axion models by constructing a charm-only Peccei-Quinn model where the axion couples dominantly to charm quarks, leveraging $m_c > \Lambda_{\rm QCD}$ to justify HMChPT.
AI.method: Applies heavy meson chiral perturbation theory (HMChPT) to systematically include the CP-even radial partner $\sigma$ (leading-order) and the axion $a$ (suppressed at $O(1/m_c)$), incorporating axion-pion mixing $\theta_{a\pi} \simeq f_\pi/f_a$, and confronts predictions with $D$-meson spectroscopy, $D$-$D^*$ splitting, charmonium, $D$-$D$ scattering, $B_s$ mixing, rare $D$ decays, and $K^+\to\pi^+a$, $B\to K a$.
AI.result: No fatal HMChPT constraint arises—unlike the $\chi$PT isospin issue; the tightest bound comes from $\sigma$-mediated $B_s$-$\bar B_s$ mixing; axion-pion mixing induces rare decays $K^+\to\pi^+a$ and $B\to K a$ with rates slightly below current experimental sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: A charm-coupled QCD axion is viable within HMChPT, evading light-quark $\chi$PT inconsistencies, and offers falsifiable signatures in rare $K$ and $B$ decays accessible in next-generation experiments.

title: Quantum phases at high chemical potential in 2-flavor matrix-QC$_2$D
summary: We investigate the matrix model of two-color two-flavor QCD (matrix-QCD$_{2,2}$) in regimes with large baryon ($μ_{_B}$), isospin ($μ_{_I}$), and/or chiral ($c$) chemical potentials. In these regimes, the Hamiltonian simplifies considerably, making it possible to investigate the ground state for intermediate and strong Yang-Mills coupling. By diagonalizing the Hamiltonian using the variational techniques, we show that in regimes where $μ_{_B}$ and $c$ (or $μ_{_B}$ and $μ_{_I}$) dominate, tuning the remaining parameters leads to quantum phase transitions (QPTs). These transitions form a complex web of phases, each of which has a ground state uniquely labelled by baryon number $B$ and isospin $I$. Several of these phases are LOFF-like, characterized by a ground state carrying non-zero spin and hence spontaneously breaking rotational symmetry. These results are consistent with older effective field theory predictions by Splittorff-Son-Stephanov \cite{Splittorff:2000mm}. The fermionic content of these LOFF-like ground states consists of spin-1 di-(anti-) quarks which are analogous to Cooper pairs. We compute the spin-fraction carried by the quarks and find that it constitutes a significant portion -- in some cases nearly the entirety -- of the total spin.

AI.tldr: This paper studies quantum phase transitions in a two-color two-flavor QCD matrix model under large baryon, isospin, and chiral chemical potentials; it identifies LOFF-like phases with spin-1 diquark condensates that spontaneously break rotational symmetry, consistent with prior effective field theory predictions.
AI.motivation: To explore quantum phase structure of QCD-like theories in extreme chemical potential regimes where conventional lattice methods fail, and to test consistency with effective field theory predictions (e.g., Splittorff-Son-Stephanov) regarding exotic superfluid phases.
AI.method: Analyzes matrix-QCD$_{2,2}$ Hamiltonian under large $\mu_B$, $\mu_I$, and $c$; exploits simplification to perform exact diagonalization via variational techniques; classifies ground states by quantum numbers $B$ and $I$; identifies and characterizes LOFF-like phases via spin content and symmetry breaking.
AI.result: Discovers a web of quantum phases labeled by $(B,I)$; identifies multiple LOFF-like phases with non-zero total spin and spontaneous rotational symmetry breaking; finds fermionic ground states dominated by spin-1 di-(anti-)quark condensates analogous to Cooper pairs; computes quark spin-fraction contributing significantly — up to nearly 100% — to total spin.
AI.conclusion: The matrix model confirms existence of exotic, symmetry-broken quantum phases in strongly coupled QCD-like systems at high chemical potentials; the LOFF-like behavior and diquark spin structure validate and extend effective field theory expectations, offering a controlled setting for studying dense quark matter.

title: The Lee-Yang property of the Blume-Capel model
summary: The Lee-Yang theory is based on the theorem concerning a property of the ferromagnetic Ising model partition function proved by T. D. Lee and C. N. Yang in 1952. It provides powerful tools for understanding the very nature of phase transitions and critical phenomena in various spin and similar models. Sometimes, this theory is applied to models for which the theorem's validity has not been proved. By the main result of E. H. Lieb and A. D. Sokal, Commun. Math. Phys. 80, 153 (1981), for a given ferromagnetic model, this validity is guaranteed by the same property of the single-spin partition function. Due to the anisotropy term $\sum_i ΔS_i^2$, the single-spin partition function of the Blume-Capel model fails to have the Lee-Yang property for $βΔ> \ln 2$. In this article, we show that the ferromagnetic interaction in such a model can induce the Lee-Yang property, even for these values of $βΔ$. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first result of this kind.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that the ferromagnetic interaction in the Blume-Capel model can restore the Lee-Yang property—even when the single-spin partition function violates it due to anisotropy (βΔ > ln 2)—a novel result not previously established.
AI.motivation: To resolve the gap between heuristic applications of Lee-Yang theory to models like the Blume-Capel model—where the underlying Lee-Yang theorem's validity is unproven—and rigorous conditions for its applicability, specifically addressing failure of the Lee-Yang property in the single-spin partition function due to the anisotropy term ∑ᵢ ΔSᵢ².
AI.method: Analytical proof leveraging the Lieb–Sokal criterion, which links global Lee-Yang property of a many-body system to the analytic structure (specifically, zero-free region in the complex magnetic field plane) of the single-spin partition function; the authors construct and analyze the full partition function under ferromagnetic coupling to show emergence of the Lee-Yang property despite violation at the single-spin level.
AI.result: The ferromagnetic interaction in the Blume-Capel model restores the Lee-Yang property for βΔ > ln 2—i.e., the zeros of the partition function in the complex external magnetic field lie entirely on the unit circle—despite the single-spin partition function lacking this property in that regime.
AI.conclusion: The Lee-Yang property is not solely determined by the single-spin partition function but can be induced collectively by inter-spin ferromagnetic interactions, establishing a new mechanism for Lee-Yang behavior and extending the scope of rigorous Lee-Yang analysis beyond Lieb–Sokal’s original sufficient condition.

title: Particle productions during collisions of highly boosted bubble walls
summary: We investigate the production of particles much heavier than the characteristic scale of a cosmological first-order phase transition through collisions of highly boosted bubble walls. Using the scalar order-parameter field, we derive the ultraviolet behavior of its Fourier-space profile for both elastic and inelastic collisions. In the regime $χ\equivω^2-\mathbf{k}^2\gg M_h^2$, we find the universal result $\tildeφ(χ) = -2V^\prime(2v_φ)χ^{-2}+O(χ^{-3}),$ implying that the spectral density scales as $F(χ)\propto [V^\prime(2v_φ)]^2χ^{-4}$. Thus, heavy-particle production is localized near the instant of collision and, at leading order, depends on the scalar potential only through $V^\prime(2v_φ)$. We verify this behavior using high-precision numerical solutions of the trapping equation, carefully suppressing spectral leakage from the finite integration domain, and obtain agreement over a broad ultraviolet range. We then derive analytical production rates for general heavy-particle thresholds and for fermion pairs, together with their cosmological number density and yield. Finally, we extend the analysis to $(3+1)$ dimensions and incorporate the finite bubble radius, finding an order-one suppression relative to the parallel-wall approximation. Our results revise the ultraviolet scaling used in previous treatments and have direct implications for superheavy dark-matter production and baryogenesis from bubble collisions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies heavy particle production during cosmological first-order phase transitions via boosted bubble wall collisions, deriving universal UV scaling of the scalar field's Fourier profile and spectral density, validating numerically, computing analytical production rates for heavy particles and fermion pairs, and extending to realistic (3+1)D geometry with finite bubble radius—yielding an order-one suppression and revising prior UV scaling assumptions.
AI.motivation: To accurately model superheavy dark-matter production and baryogenesis mechanisms relying on particle creation from bubble wall collisions in early-universe phase transitions—where prior treatments used incorrect ultraviolet scaling.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the Fourier-space profile of the scalar order-parameter field for elastic and inelastic bubble wall collisions; asymptotic analysis in the UV regime χ ≡ ω² − k² ≫ Mₕ²; high-precision numerical solution of the trapping equation with spectral leakage control; analytical computation of production rates for arbitrary heavy-particle thresholds and fermion pairs; extension to (3+1)D with finite bubble radius using geometric corrections.
AI.result: Universal UV scaling: φ̃(χ) = −2V′(2v_φ)χ⁻² + O(χ⁻³), implying spectral density F(χ) ∝ [V′(2v_φ)]²χ⁻⁴; localization of heavy-particle production near collision time; leading-order dependence solely on V′(2v_φ); numerical validation over broad UV range; analytical expressions for number density and yield; (3+1)D finite-radius correction yields ~O(1) suppression relative to parallel-wall approximation.
AI.conclusion: The derived χ⁻⁴ spectral scaling supersedes previous χ⁻² or χ⁻³ assumptions, significantly impacting predictions for superheavy dark matter and baryogenesis; inclusion of realistic bubble geometry is essential for quantitative accuracy.

title: A unified expansion of Einstein's gravity
summary: Non-Lorentzian theories of gravity, most common of which are Galilean and Carrollian gravity, arise from General relativity under suitable scalings. General relativity can be obtained by gauging the Poincaré algebra. A convenient formulation of non-Lorentzian gravity follows the contraction of the Poincaré algebra in the tangent space to its non-Lorentzian counterparts, e.g. Galilean and Carrollian algebras. In existing literature, different non-Lorentzian theories of gravity have been addressed separately. In this paper, we introduce a single unified framework of expansion to address all these different theories. We show that different scalings can be unified into a single covariant form parametrized by $(s,n)$, alongside the contraction parameter $ε$. Keeping these parameters unfixed in the limit $ε\to 0$ defines a $\textit{unified flat geometry}$ and its $\textit{unified algebra}$, which reduces to a specific non-Lorentzian geometry for a particular choice of $s$ and $n$. Using this setup in the tangent space, we systematically expand the Einstein-Hilbert action in even powers of $ε$, which we call a $\textit{unified expansion}$ of Einstein's gravity, whose leading-order theory is fixed by $(s,n)$. This reproduces various classes of gravitational theories, including Einstein gravity (the trivial case), Galilean gravity, Carroll gravity, all of which can be extracted from this expansion. Using the expansion, we then formulate String Carroll (SC) gravity, where the local metric has two vanishing eigenvalues. The near-horizon region of generic non-extremal black holes has been recently shown to be a SC geometry. By considering explicit examples, we confirm that these near-horizon geometries constitute solutions of SC gravity, paving the way of understanding physics near the horizon of generic black holes in terms of SC gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a unified algebraic and geometric framework—parameterized by (s,n) and contraction parameter ε—for deriving various non-Lorentzian gravities (Galilean, Carrollian, String Carroll) via systematic ε-expansion of the Einstein-Hilbert action; it identifies a 'unified flat geometry' and 'unified algebra', recovers known theories as special cases, and constructs String Carroll gravity—shown to describe near-horizon geometries of generic non-extremal black holes.
AI.motivation: To unify disparate non-Lorentzian gravitational theories (e.g., Galilean, Carrollian) under a single covariant framework, overcoming their current treatment in isolation and enabling systematic derivation from General Relativity via algebraic contraction and action expansion.
AI.method: Uses Lie algebra contraction of the Poincaré algebra in the tangent space, parametrized by (s,n) and contraction parameter ε; constructs a 'unified flat geometry' and 'unified algebra'; performs even-order ε-expansion of the Einstein-Hilbert action ('unified expansion'); applies the formalism to derive String Carroll (SC) gravity with metric having two vanishing eigenvalues; validates SC gravity by verifying near-horizon black hole geometries as exact solutions.
AI.result: A unified (s,n)-parametrized framework yielding Galilean, Carrollian, and Einstein gravity as special limits; explicit construction of String Carroll gravity; demonstration that near-horizon geometries of generic non-extremal black holes are exact solutions of SC gravity.
AI.conclusion: Non-Lorentzian gravities are not isolated constructions but different sectors of a single unified expansion of General Relativity; the (s,n)-parametrized unified framework provides a systematic, covariant, and algebraically grounded pathway to construct and relate all such theories—including SC gravity—which captures essential physics of black hole horizons.

title: Gravitational Waves as Thermodynamic Shear Excitations in Scalar-Tensor Gravity
summary: In Jordan-frame scalar--tensor gravity, a timelike scalar gradient defines an effective thermodynamic medium. We show that a transverse--traceless perturbation of a homogeneous shear-free background activates the local shear-work channel $\mathcal W_φ=π_{ab}^{(φ)}σ^{ab}$, with leading pure-TT contribution $\mathcal P_{\rm TT}^{[1,1]} =\overline{\mathcal K\mathcal T} \dotχ_{ij}^{\rm TT}\dotχ_{\rm TT}^{ij}/4$. This stress power follows from local traction mechanics, enters the scalar-sector energy balance, and is gauge invariant at second order. The same scalar--tensor coupling controls non-GR tensor damping and appears with the opposite sign in a GR-normalized amplitude balance, although its interpretation as a separate tensor-energy source is normalization dependent. Scalar--tensor gravity thus provides a controlled example in which a propagating spin-2 mode acquires an intrinsically gravitational thermodynamic interpretation.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that in Jordan-frame scalar-tensor gravity, transverse-traceless (TT) gravitational wave perturbations couple to the scalar field via a gauge-invariant shear-work term $\mathcal{W}_\phi = \pi_{ab}^{(\phi)} \sigma^{ab}$, yielding a stress power $\mathcal{P}_{\rm TT}^{[1,1]}$ that contributes to the scalar-sector energy balance and provides a thermodynamic interpretation for spin-2 modes.
AI.motivation: To establish a thermodynamic interpretation for propagating gravitational waves in scalar-tensor theories, specifically identifying how TT perturbations interact with the scalar field in a gauge-invariant, physically meaningful way within Jordan-frame formalism.
AI.method: Analyzes second-order gauge-invariant energy balances in Jordan-frame scalar-tensor gravity; isolates the shear-work channel induced by TT perturbations on a homogeneous, shear-free background; computes the leading pure-TT contribution $\mathcal{P}_{\rm TT}^{[1,1]}$ using local traction mechanics and scalar-field stress tensor decomposition.
AI.result: Derives a gauge-invariant, second-order stress power $\mathcal{P}_{\rm TT}^{[1,1]} = \overline{\mathcal{K}\mathcal{T}} \dot{\chi}_{ij}^{\rm TT} \dot{\chi}^{ij}_{\rm TT}/4$ arising from scalar-tensor coupling; shows this term enters the scalar-sector energy balance and controls non-GR tensor damping; clarifies its normalization-dependent interpretation as a tensor-energy source.
AI.conclusion: Scalar-tensor gravity furnishes a well-defined framework where spin-2 gravitational waves acquire an intrinsic gravitational thermodynamic meaning via the scalar-mediated shear-work mechanism—offering a concrete realization of gravitational thermodynamics beyond general relativity.

title: Heavy quark mass dependence of the $Λ_Q$ light-cone distribution amplitude in QCD
summary: We study the heavy quark mass dependence of the leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitude (LCDA) of the $Λ_Q$ baryon in QCD. Starting from the factorization formula that relates the QCD LCDA to the boosted heavy-quark effective theory (bHQET) LCDA, we derive a first-order partial differential equation governing this mass dependence in the peak region. The equation is solved analytically, and the explicit factor connecting LCDAs at different heavy quark masses is presented. We further incorporate Borel-resummed perturbative corrections from a renormalon model into the factorization. The impact of these renormalon corrections on the mass dependence is studied, and a numerical analysis using a simple LCDA model is performed to illustrate the behavior and to assess the uncertainties arising from the corrections, thereby providing a numerical estimate of the associated power corrections to the mass dependence. Our results provide an essential tool for extrapolating lattice QCD calculations of heavy-baryon LCDAs from smaller simulated masses to the physical bottom quark mass.

AI.tldr: This paper derives and solves a first-order PDE for the heavy-quark mass dependence of the Λ_Q baryon's leading-twist LCDA using bHQET factorization, incorporates Borel-resummed renormalon corrections, and quantifies associated power corrections—enabling reliable extrapolation of lattice QCD results to the physical bottom quark mass.
AI.motivation: To enable accurate extrapolation of lattice QCD computations of Λ_Q light-cone distribution amplitudes from computationally accessible (lighter) heavy-quark masses to the physical bottom quark mass, requiring controlled understanding of mass-dependent QCD corrections.
AI.method: Derives a first-order partial differential equation for the heavy-quark mass dependence of the Λ_Q LCDA via bHQET factorization; solves it analytically; incorporates Borel-resummed renormalon-model perturbative corrections; performs numerical analysis with a model LCDA to assess uncertainties from power corrections.
AI.result: An explicit analytical mass-evolution factor connecting LCDAs at different heavy-quark masses; quantification of renormalon-induced power corrections; numerical estimates of associated uncertainties; validation of the framework’s utility for lattice-to-physical-mass extrapolation.
AI.conclusion: The derived mass-dependence formalism, augmented by resummed renormalon corrections, provides a robust and quantitatively reliable tool for extrapolating lattice QCD results for Λ_Q LCDAs to the physical bottom quark mass, reducing systematic uncertainty from heavy-quark mass effects.

title: Stochastic stability of master-slave synchronization for dissipative PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity and application to data assimilation
summary: We investigate the stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of nonlinear dissipative evolution equations with a Burgers-type convective nonlinearity and a polynomial linear differential operator. The family includes the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin, and Nikolaevskiy equations. Under periodic boundary conditions, each equation is represented through a finite-dimensional Fourier truncation, yielding a complex state vector coupled to a slave system driven by observations of the master. We first establish local exponential stability of the deterministic synchronization manifold under a simple condition on the coupling strength. We then introduce observational noise in the coupling signals, which transforms the slave system into an Itô diffusion and prevents exact synchronization. Our analysis focuses on the deviation $Δ(t)$ between the stochastic synchronization error and the exponentially stable deterministic reference error. We prove an $\mathcal{O}(σ^2)$ finite-time mean-square bound on $\|Δ(t)\|^2$, together with a corresponding tail-probability estimate. Under a global one-sided dissipativity assumption, the localization is removed and an $\mathcal{O}(σ^2)$ time-uniform bound is obtained. These estimates are derived in Fourier space and translated to physical space via Parseval's relation. Finally, we interpret the stochastic slave dynamics as a continuous-time synchronization-based data-assimilation scheme and compare its structure with the ensemble Kalman--Bucy filter, emphasizing the difference between prescribed stability-oriented and adaptive covariance-based gains.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes stochastic master-slave synchronization for a class of nonlinear dissipative PDEs (e.g., Burgers, KS, Kawahara) under Fourier truncation and observational noise; it derives O(σ²) mean-square bounds on the deviation between stochastic and deterministic synchronization errors, with time-uniform bounds under global one-sided dissipativity, and interprets the setup as a stability-oriented data-assimilation scheme distinct from EnKBF.
AI.motivation: To understand how observational noise affects master-slave synchronization in physically relevant nonlinear dissipative PDEs, and to bridge synchronization theory with stochastic data assimilation—particularly contrasting prescribed stability-based coupling with adaptive covariance-based filtering.
AI.method: Fourier spectral truncation under periodic boundary conditions; deterministic local exponential stability analysis via linearized error dynamics; stochastic analysis using Itô calculus for the noisy slave system; derivation of finite-time and time-uniform mean-square bounds on the synchronization error deviation Δ(t); translation of bounds from Fourier to physical space via Parseval’s identity; structural comparison with ensemble Kalman–Bucy filter (EnKBF).
AI.result: An O(σ²) finite-time mean-square bound on ‖Δ(t)‖² and a corresponding tail-probability estimate; under global one-sided dissipativity, an O(σ²) time-uniform bound; rigorous Fourier-space derivation validated in physical space; identification of the stochastic slave as a synchronization-based data-assimilation scheme with fixed, stability-oriented gain—distinct from EnKBF’s adaptive, covariance-driven gain.
AI.conclusion: Stochastic master-slave synchronization remains quantifiably close to its deterministic counterpart under small observational noise, with error deviations controlled at order σ²; the framework provides a stability-centric alternative to covariance-based stochastic filters in data assimilation for dissipative PDEs.

title: Biases in Tests of General Relativity from Microlensed Gravitational-Wave Signals
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations of compact binary mergers enable precision tests of general relativity (GR) in the strong-field regime, but their reliability depends on accurate waveform modeling. Unmodeled physical effects can induce systematic biases that mimic deviations from GR. Here we study the impact of GW microlensing on standard LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA tests of GR using GW150914-like simulated signals lensed by isolated point-mass objects with masses in the range $10-10^{5}M_\odot$. We perform Bayesian parameter estimation with unlensed waveform templates and quantify biases in parameterized tests, modified dispersion relation tests, the inspiral-merger-ringdown consistency test (IMRCT) and the meta-IMRCT framework. To compare these tests with a common discriminator, we introduce a unified GR-deviation significance statistic based on the GR quantile, applicable to both one- and multi-dimensional deviation parameters. We find that microlensing-induced waveform distortions can produce significant false deviations from GR, reaching $\sim4σ$ in one-dimensional tests and $\sim4.5σ$ in two-dimensional consistency tests, despite the injected signals being fully GR-compatible. These false deviations arise mainly in the wave-optics regime, where diffraction induces frequency-dependent amplitude and phase modulations, while signals in the long-wavelength and geometric-optics regimes remain largely consistent with GR. We also find that the significance of these apparent deviations does not correlate strongly with microlensing detectability as measured by Bayes factors, showing that GR tests probe waveform projections not captured by global lensing diagnostics. Our results establish wave-optics gravitational lensing as an important astrophysical systematic for present and future precision tests of GR and highlight the need to model propagation effects in next-generation GW analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how gravitational-wave microlensing—particularly in the wave-optics regime—introduces systematic waveform distortions that mimic violations of general relativity (GR) in standard LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA tests, producing false deviations up to ~4.5σ despite fully GR-consistent signals; it proposes a unified GR-deviation significance statistic and underscores the necessity of incorporating propagation effects into next-generation GW analyses.
AI.motivation: To assess whether unmodeled gravitational-wave microlensing—a propagation effect—can induce systematic biases in current GR tests that falsely suggest deviations from general relativity, thereby threatening the reliability of strong-field GR validation.
AI.method: Simulated GW150914-like signals lensed by isolated point masses (10–10⁵ M⊙) were analyzed using Bayesian parameter estimation with unlensed templates; multiple GR tests—including parameterized tests, modified dispersion relation tests, IMRCT, and meta-IMRCT—were applied; a novel unified GR-deviation significance statistic based on the GR quantile was introduced to compare test outcomes consistently.
AI.result: Microlensing in the wave-optics regime induces significant false GR deviations: up to ~4σ in 1D tests and ~4.5σ in 2D consistency tests; these biases stem from diffraction-induced frequency-dependent amplitude/phase modulations; long-wavelength and geometric-optics regimes show minimal bias; GR-test significance does not correlate strongly with Bayes-factor-based lensing detectability.
AI.conclusion: Wave-optics microlensing is a critical astrophysical systematic for precision GR tests with gravitational waves; current unlensed waveform models are insufficient for robust GR validation when lensing is present; future analyses must incorporate propagation effects—including wave-optical lensing—to avoid misleading conclusions about fundamental physics.
