title: The $Υ(nS) \to B_{(c)}$ transition form factors and their applications to semileptonic and nonleptonic weak decays
summary: The semileptonic and nonleptonic decays of the $Υ(nS)$ with $n=1,2,3,4$ are investigated within the covariant light-front quark model (CLFQM). Using the form factors of the transitions $Υ(nS) \to B_{(c)}$ obtained from the CLFQM, we calculate the branching ratios of the decays $Υ(nS)\to B_{(c)}\ellν_\ell$ and $Υ(nS)\to B_{(c)}M$ with $\ell=e,μ,τ$ and $M$ referring to $π(ρ),K^{(*)},D^{(*)},D^{(*)}_s$. One can find that the branching ratios of the decays $Υ(3S)\to B_c\ellν_\ell$ are the largest among those of considered semileptonic decays and can amount to $10^{-9}$; As to the nonleptonic decays, $Υ(3S)\to B_cρ$ and $Υ(3S)\to B_cD^{(*)}_s$ have the largest branching ratios, which reach up to $10^{-10}$. Given the identification and detection efficiency of final states, searching for these weak decay modes should be fairly challenging in future experiments. The forward-backward asymmetry $A_{FB}$ and the longitudinal polarization fraction $f_L$ are also calculated for those semileptonic decays.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates semileptonic and nonleptonic decay branching ratios of Υ(nS) (n=1–4) to B_(c) mesons using the covariant light-front quark model; Υ(3S) decays dominate, with BRs up to 10⁻⁹ (semileptonic) and 10⁻¹⁰ (nonleptonic); A_FB and f_L are also computed.
AI.motivation: To systematically evaluate weak decays of bottomonium states Υ(nS) (n=1–4) into B_(c) mesons—both semileptonic and nonleptonic—which are highly suppressed but theoretically accessible via heavy-quark transitions, and to assess their experimental detectability.
AI.method: Uses the covariant light-front quark model (CLFQM) to compute transition form factors for Υ(nS) → B_(c), then applies them to calculate decay widths and branching ratios for Υ(nS) → B_(c)ℓν_ℓ (ℓ=e,μ,τ) and Υ(nS) → B_(c)M (M = π,ρ,K,K*,D,D*,D_s,D_s*); also computes angular observables A_FB and f_L for semileptonic channels.
AI.result: Υ(3S) exhibits largest semileptonic BRs: BR[Υ(3S)→B_cℓν_ℓ] ~ 10⁻⁹; largest nonleptonic BRs: BR[Υ(3S)→B_cρ] and BR[Υ(3S)→B_cD_s^(*)] ~ 10⁻¹⁰; A_FB and f_L are quantified for all semileptonic modes.
AI.conclusion: Weak decays of Υ(nS) to B_(c) are dominated by Υ(3S); though theoretically predicted, their small branching ratios (~10⁻⁹–10⁻¹⁰) make experimental observation extremely challenging with current or near-future detectors due to low statistics and final-state identification inefficiencies.

title: The de Sitter Scalar Discrete Series: Gupta-Bleuler Structure and Holography
summary: We show that scalar discrete-series unitary irreducible representations (UIRs) $Π_{p,0}$ ($p=1,2,\cdots$) of the de Sitter (dS) group $\mathrm{SO}_0(1,4)$ admit a dS-covariant Krein realization on the dS hyperboloid, endowed with a dS-invariant non-degenerate Klein-Gordon (KG) sesquilinear form, in which the group action is indecomposable and organizes naturally into a Gupta-Bleuler triplet. The positive- and negative-norm sectors are already present in the underlying Krein space, whereas a null sector emerges only at an intermediate stage, where the induced KG form becomes degenerate and its radical leads canonically to the physical quotient carrying the UIR $Π_{p,0}$. We further show that suitable limits of the bulk theory at the ``future'' and ``past'' conformal boundaries ${\mathcal{I}}^\pm$ give rise to dS-invariant boundary realizations endowed with induced kernel inner products. While the bulk negative-norm sector admits no independent boundary counterpart, the boundary realization retains the physical and gauge structures inherited from the bulk. The resulting boundary module nevertheless remains indecomposable, with its physical quotient carrying the discrete-series representation $Π_{p,0}$. The antipodal symmetry provides a natural relation between the realizations on ${\mathcal{I}}^+$ and ${\mathcal{I}}^-$, ensuring the consistency of the boundary construction and its geometric interpretation. At the heart of the analysis lies a Fourier-type bulk-boundary transform that provides a dS-covariant identification of the bulk and boundary physical sectors, establishing a one-to-one intertwining correspondence between the bulk and boundary realizations of $Π_{p,0}$ while preserving reflection positivity.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a Krein-space realization of discrete-series UIRs of the de Sitter group SO₀(1,4), organizes it into a Gupta-Bleuler triplet (positive/negative/null norms), and establishes a dS-covariant bulk-to-boundary correspondence via a Fourier-type transform that preserves reflection positivity and intertwines the physical quotients.
AI.motivation: To rigorously realize scalar discrete-series unitary irreducible representations of the de Sitter group in a covariant, physically interpretable framework—specifically addressing the tension between unitarity, covariance, and the indefinite inner product inherent in field-theoretic realizations on curved spacetime.
AI.method: Constructs a dS-covariant Krein-space realization of Π_{p,0} on the dS hyperboloid using a non-degenerate Klein-Gordon sesquilinear form; identifies the Gupta-Bleuler triplet structure via degeneration of the induced KG form and quotienting by its radical; derives boundary realizations at conformal infinity I± via limiting procedures; introduces a dS-covariant Fourier-type bulk-boundary transform to establish intertwining isomorphisms preserving reflection positivity.
AI.result: A fully dS-covariant Krein realization of Π_{p,0} exhibiting an intrinsic Gupta-Bleuler structure; well-defined boundary realizations on I± carrying induced kernel inner products and retaining gauge/physical decomposition; a canonical bulk-boundary transform yielding a one-to-one, reflection-positive, intertwining correspondence between the physical sectors of bulk and boundary.
AI.conclusion: The discrete-series representations Π_{p,0} admit consistent, geometrically grounded, and physically meaningful realizations both in the dS bulk and at its conformal boundaries, unified by a dS-covariant, reflection-positive bulk-boundary duality—resolving structural ambiguities in quantum field theory on de Sitter space.

title: Light-front diagnostics in the 't Hooft model: II. Boundary cancellations, ERBL spectral sums, and analyticity of the EMT form factor
summary: A diagonal light-front overlap contains near-forward energy-momentum-tensor (EMT) information but is not itself a local matrix element. In the large-$N_c$ 't Hooft model we complete the second GPD moment with its ERBL contribution and follow how the two support regions combine. Boundary exponents generate fractional powers and, at $β=1/2$, resonant logarithms in the separate terms. We show that these structures cancel, including the interference of the leading and next indicial families. At the resonance, cancellation of the double and single logarithms also yields an inverse-mass-squared residue sum rule; above it, the two regions combine into a finite fourth-order coefficient. The complete EMT form factor is therefore analytic through curvature order. The ERBL sector leaves the slope unchanged but is essential for curvature and higher derivatives. We extract stable canonical and heavy curvatures, estimates with systematic envelopes for the second and third light excitations, and the longitudinal trace radius. The intermediate-state decomposition further shows how constituent mass and excitation redistribute pole strength and generate removable poles and interference zeros.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the energy-momentum tensor (EMT) form factor in the large-N_c 't Hooft model using light-front diagonal overlaps and GPD moments, demonstrating analyticity up to curvature order via cancellation of singularities between DGLAP and ERBL sectors; it extracts curvature parameters, trace radius, and reveals pole/zero structures from constituent mass and excitations.
AI.motivation: To resolve analytic structure and renormalization-group consistency of the EMT form factor by reconciling near-forward EMT information from diagonal light-front overlaps with full GPD moment evolution, particularly addressing singularities arising from boundary exponents and resonant logarithms at β = 1/2.
AI.method: Uses the large-N_c 't Hooft model to compute the second GPD moment by combining DGLAP and ERBL contributions; employs conformal mapping and indicial analysis to handle fractional-power singularities and resonant logarithms; performs intermediate-state decomposition to isolate pole/zero contributions from constituent mass and excitations.
AI.result: Demonstrates complete cancellation of double and single logarithms at β = 1/2, yielding an inverse-mass-squared residue sum rule; establishes analyticity of the EMT form factor through curvature order; extracts stable canonical and heavy curvatures, systematic estimates for second and third excited states, and the longitudinal trace radius; identifies removable poles and interference zeros from excitation-dependent pole strength redistribution.
AI.conclusion: The ERBL sector is indispensable for curvature and higher derivatives of the EMT form factor—even though it leaves the slope unchanged—ensuring full analyticity; the interplay between DGLAP and ERBL support regions, governed by boundary exponents and resonance conditions, underpins the physical consistency of EMT matrix elements in light-front QCD-inspired models.

title: Kibble-Zurek Mechanism and Current-Phase Relation in a Holographic Josephson Junction
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the current-phase relation of the Josephson junction in a holographic superfluid ring, realized from the stochastic and non-equilibrium dynamics according to the Kibble-Zurek mechanism. By employing a spatially modulated charge density to engineer a weak link, the current-phase relation is investigated in a range of geometric and thermodynamic parameters. The seminal sinusoidal relation between the current and the phase emerges periodically due to the compact shape of the geometry. We also identify the relations between the critical current and the geometric parameters of the junction: the width, steepness and depth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the critical current exhibits a characteristic exponential decaying against the final temperature, reflecting the thermal degradation of the order parameter in a strong-coupling regime. Our results establish a robust framework for holographic Josephson devices, offering experimentally testable predictions for the non-equilibrium dynamics of high-$T_c$ superconductors.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the current-phase relation of a Josephson junction in a holographic superfluid ring using non-equilibrium dynamics inspired by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism; it finds a periodic sinusoidal current-phase relation due to compact geometry, quantifies critical current dependence on junction geometry (width, steepness, depth), and shows exponential decay of critical current with final temperature—indicating thermal suppression of the order parameter in strong coupling—thereby providing testable predictions for high-Tc superconductors.
AI.motivation: To understand non-equilibrium dynamics and current-phase relations in holographic models of superconductivity, particularly for Josephson junctions in strongly coupled regimes relevant to high-Tc superconductors.
AI.method: Holographic construction of a superfluid ring with a spatially modulated charge density engineering a weak link; numerical simulation of stochastic and non-equilibrium dynamics governed by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism; systematic variation of geometric (junction width, steepness, depth) and thermodynamic (final temperature) parameters.
AI.result: Emergence of a periodic sinusoidal current-phase relation due to compact ring geometry; quantitative scaling laws linking critical current to junction geometry; exponential decay of critical current with final temperature, consistent with thermal degradation of the holographic order parameter.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes a robust holographic framework for Josephson devices, yielding experimentally accessible signatures of non-equilibrium superconducting dynamics in strongly coupled systems.

title: Separating the linearized Einstein equations in Kerr
comment: 9 pages, 5 supplemental Mathematica files in the source package
summary: A direct separation of the linearized Einstein equations in Kerr is presented. The trace of the perturbed metric is found to obey the spin-0 perturbation equation and so is irrelevant for the spin-2 perturbations. By combining the traceless condition, the Killing-Yano symmetry, a parity requirement, and the de Donder gauge condition, it has been found possible to reduce the linearized Einstein equations in Kerr to a manageable level, thereby enabling the direct separation of the equations and the derivation of a unique set of decoupled mode functions for the spin-2 perturbation of the Kerr black hole.

AI.tldr: This paper achieves direct separation of linearized Einstein equations for spin-2 perturbations of the Kerr black hole by leveraging traceless condition, Killing-Yano symmetry, parity, and de Donder gauge, yielding a unique set of decoupled mode functions.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing challenge of separating spin-2 gravitational perturbations on the Kerr background, which is essential for stability analysis and gravitational wave modeling.
AI.method: Uses the traceless condition, Killing-Yano tensor symmetry, parity decomposition, and de Donder gauge to reduce and separate the linearized Einstein equations; identifies that the metric trace satisfies spin-0 equation and thus decouples from spin-2 dynamics.
AI.result: Derives a unique, fully decoupled set of mode functions for spin-2 perturbations of Kerr spacetime, enabling direct separation of the linearized Einstein equations.
AI.conclusion: The combination of geometric symmetries and gauge conditions allows complete decoupling and separation of spin-2 perturbations—resolving a fundamental problem in black hole perturbation theory.

title: Moving Collinear Cracks in a Prestressed Dry Sandy Medium Fracture Response under Traveling Punch Loads
summary: The dynamic fracture behaviour of two moving collinear Griffith cracks in an initially stressed dry sandy medium subjected to concentrated crack-face loading and moving punch pressure is investigated. A moving coordinate system transforms the transient problem into a steady state formulation, while the effects of initial stress and sandiness are incorporated into the governing equations. Fourier integral transforms are employed to obtain the characteristic equation and the transformed traction displacement relations. The crack face, symmetry, and outer surface conditions reduce the problem to coupled Cauchy type singular integral equations. For a sufficiently thick strip, an asymptotic kernel reduction is developed, and the resulting equations are solved analytically using the finite Hilbert transform. Closed form expressions are derived for the crack density functions, Mode I stress intensity factors at the inner and outer crack tips, and the crack opening displacement. Several limiting cases are recovered from the general formulation, providing analytical consistency checks. The results demonstrate the combined influence of crack speed, crack geometry, initial stress, sandiness, and moving punch loading on crack tip intensification and crack opening. The proposed analytical framework provides useful insights for fracture assessment and the design of transportation infrastructure, geotechnical systems, underground excavations, and other engineering structures involving dry sandy media subjected to moving loads.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically investigates dynamic fracture behavior of two moving collinear Griffith cracks in an initially stressed dry sandy medium under concentrated crack-face and moving punch loading, deriving closed-form expressions for stress intensity factors and crack opening displacement via singular integral equations and finite Hilbert transform.
AI.motivation: To understand how combined effects of initial stress, sandiness, crack geometry, crack speed, and moving punch loading influence fracture mechanics in dry sandy media—critical for geotechnical and transportation infrastructure design.
AI.method: Uses a moving coordinate system to convert transient dynamics into steady-state formulation; incorporates initial stress and sandiness into governing equations; applies Fourier integral transforms to derive characteristic equations and traction-displacement relations; reduces problem to coupled Cauchy-type singular integral equations; employs asymptotic kernel reduction for thick strip and solves analytically via finite Hilbert transform.
AI.result: Derives closed-form expressions for crack density functions, Mode I stress intensity factors at inner/outer crack tips, and crack opening displacement; recovers several limiting cases for analytical validation; quantifies parametric influence of crack speed, geometry, initial stress, sandiness, and punch loading on crack tip intensification and opening.
AI.conclusion: The analytical framework provides physically consistent, parametrically rich insights for fracture assessment and design of engineering systems in dry sandy media under moving loads.

title: Exact constraints on family-separated seesaw relations and their phenomenological consequences
summary: Working at tree level and at a common renormalization scale, we examine the family-separated seesaw ansatz of Z.-z.~Xing, arXiv:2605.27049v2. For a fixed light-heavy pairing, imposing $m_iU_{αi}U_{βi}+M_iR_{αi}R_{βi}=0$ together with $UU^\dagger+RR^\dagger=\mathbf{1}$ yields the general exact solution $U=VD^{-1/2}$ and $R=iVE\,\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\sqrt{r_i/(1+r_i)}\right)$, where $r_i=m_i/M_i$, $D=\operatorname{diag}(1+r_i)$, $V$ is unitary, and $E=\operatorname{diag}(η_i)$ with $η_i=\pm1$. Consequently, $U^\dagger U$ and $R^\dagger R$ are diagonal, and distinct columns are exactly orthogonal. An exact unitary completion gives, in a convenient sterile basis, $M_R=D_N-D_ν$ and $Y_ν=(i/v)VE(D_νD_N)^{1/2}$, so that $Y_ν^\dagger Y_ν=D_νD_N/v^2$ is diagonal. In the canonical domain $M_i>m_i$, the singlet masses relevant to the unbroken-phase decay description are $\widehat{M}_i=M_i-m_i>0$, distinct from the broken-phase heavy eigenvalues $M_i$. Hence, at the scale of exact alignment, all standard unflavored and flavored nonresonant one-loop decay asymmetries vanish in the nondegenerate perturbative regime. For $m_i=0$, the paired Yukawa column and decay width vanish instead. The flavor-summed rephasing-invariant combination used in the proposed asymmetry also cancels identically, although individual CP-odd invariants may remain nonzero. Thus the proposed correlation between low-energy CP violation and these decay asymmetries does not follow from exact family separation. This result does not address radiative misalignment, resonant or coherent dynamics, or thermal and higher-loop sources. We also correct the proposed heavy-mass reconstruction formulas and clarify the implications for neutrinoless double-beta decay, Yukawa scaling, parameter counting, and light-heavy mass orderings.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the family-separated seesaw ansatz at tree level, deriving exact solutions for mixing matrices U and R under constraints; it shows that standard nonresonant one-loop CP asymmetries vanish under exact alignment, invalidating a proposed correlation between low-energy CP violation and leptogenesis in this regime.
AI.motivation: To assess the validity of a proposed correlation between low-energy CP violation and leptogenesis-driven decay asymmetries within the family-separated seesaw framework, and to clarify theoretical inconsistencies in mass reconstruction and phenomenological implications.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of exact solutions for the light (U) and heavy (R) neutrino mixing matrices under unitarity and orthogonality constraints; computation of CP-violating decay asymmetries, evaluation of flavor-summed rephasing-invariant quantities, and correction of heavy-mass reconstruction formulas.
AI.result: Exact alignment implies vanishing nonresonant one-loop decay asymmetries in the nondegenerate perturbative regime; the proposed low-energy CP–leptogenesis correlation fails; corrected heavy-mass formulas and clarified implications for 0νββ, Yukawa scaling, parameter counting, and mass ordering are provided.
AI.conclusion: Exact family separation suppresses standard flavored/unflavored CP asymmetries, undermining the claimed link to low-energy CP violation; the result is limited to tree-level, nonresonant, perturbative dynamics and does not cover radiative misalignment, resonance, coherence, or thermal effects.

title: Electric field fluctuations and renormalization group flows in a self-interacting scalar field theory
summary: We consider a self interacting charged scalar field represented by the complex λφ4 model, embedded in a background electric field exhibiting classical stochastic fluctuations. We studied the effects of the classical stochastic noise on the physical parameters of the scalar field theory, for both weak and ultra strong electric field regimes. The stochastic background electric field is included in the Schwinger propagator through the covariant derivative, and the generating functional of the theory is found by means of the replica trick in order to compute the statistical average over electric fluctuations. As a result of the averaging process, an effective interaction between charged currents emerges, with a coupling constant proportional to the magnitude of the auto-correlation function of the electric field fluctuations. We obtained the dressed propagators, the interaction vertices, and the renormalization group equations of the theory, along with the corresponding streamplots in the manifold of interaction couplings.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how classical stochastic fluctuations in a background electric field affect a self-interacting charged scalar field (λφ⁴ model), deriving an effective current-current interaction, dressed propagators, vertices, and RG flow via replica trick–averaged Schwinger propagator.
AI.motivation: To understand how classical stochastic noise in external electric fields modifies quantum field-theoretic structure—specifically vacuum polarization, effective interactions, and RG evolution—in both weak and ultra-strong field regimes.
AI.method: Incorporates stochastic electric field into the covariant derivative of the Schwinger propagator; employs the replica trick to compute statistical averages over electric field fluctuations; derives generating functional, effective action, dressed Green’s functions, Feynman rules, and renormalization group equations; visualizes RG flow via streamplots in coupling space.
AI.result: Emergence of an effective current-current interaction with coupling strength ∝ autocorrelation amplitude of electric noise; full set of noise-modified propagators and vertices; beta functions and RG equations for all couplings; qualitative and quantitative changes in RG flow topology under stochastic background.
AI.conclusion: Classical stochastic electric fluctuations induce nontrivial effective interactions and alter renormalization group trajectories in charged scalar QFT—demonstrating that environmental noise can fundamentally reshape quantum field dynamics even at the level of perturbative renormalizability and coupling evolution.

title: Regular Black Hole Formation and Gamma-Ray Burst from Matter Conversion
summary: During the gravitational collapse of a massive star into a regular black hole, a new form of matter must be produced in order to prevent the formation of a central singularity. Since such matter is not present in the initial stellar configuration, it must emerge dynamically during the collapse. This formation process is expected to be accompanied by a strong release of energy in the form of electromagnetic radiation, which may be observable. Here we investigate the gravitational collapse of baryonic matter into Dymnikova-Hayward-Bardeen regular black holes. We estimate the radiation density and the corresponding bolometric luminosity generated by the formation of the matter sector responsible for singularity avoidance. We show that such processes provide a possible mechanism for gamma-ray bursts. Moreover, compatibility with gamma-ray burst requires small regularization effects. As a result, the corresponding regular black holes differ weakly from the Schwarzschild black hole.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates gravitational collapse into regular black holes (Dymnikova-Hayward-Bardeen type), showing that singularity-avoiding matter generation during collapse emits electromagnetic radiation potentially explaining gamma-ray bursts (GRBs); compatibility with observed GRBs implies weak regularization—i.e., the resulting black holes are nearly Schwarzschild.
AI.motivation: To explain how regular black holes avoid central singularities via dynamically generated matter during stellar collapse, and whether associated electromagnetic radiation could account for observed gamma-ray bursts.
AI.method: Analytical modeling of gravitational collapse of baryonic matter into Dymnikova-Hayward-Bardeen regular black holes; estimation of radiation energy density and bolometric luminosity from the emergent matter sector responsible for singularity regularization.
AI.result: The collapse-induced formation of singularity-avoiding matter produces significant electromagnetic radiation; luminosity estimates are compatible with gamma-ray burst energetics under small regularization (i.e., near-Schwarzschild metrics).
AI.conclusion: Gravitational collapse into regular black holes can produce observable gamma-ray bursts via radiation from dynamically generated matter; observational consistency with GRBs constrains regularization scale, implying minimal deviation from Schwarzschild geometry.

title: Fouling maps and polynomial first integrals from symmetric tensor fields
summary: Under the framework of time-independent Hamiltonian mechanics on the cotangent bundles $T^*Q$ of the configuration spaces $Q$ of mechanical systems, we introduce the concept of fouling map as a non-invertible generalization of the so-called fouling transformations --canonoid transformations preserving configuration coordinates--. We develop a tensorial method for constructing polynomial fouling maps. We show that each such map induces a $(1,1)$-tensor field invariant under the Hamiltonian flow, whose traces of its powers are polynomial constants of motion. For mechanical Hamiltonian functions --the kinetic energy plus the potential energy on a semi-Riemannian configuration space $(Q,g)$--, we completely characterize polynomial bundle maps arising from symmetric $(k+1,0)$-tensor fields and derive the conditions ensuring their fouling nature. Several explicit examples on the Euclidean plane and on the 2-sphere illustrate the method.

AI.tldr: Introduces 'fouling maps'—non-invertible generalizations of canonoid transformations—on cotangent bundles; develops a tensorial method to construct polynomial fouling maps; shows they induce flow-invariant (1,1)-tensor fields whose trace powers yield polynomial constants of motion; fully characterizes such maps for mechanical Hamiltonians via symmetric tensor fields; illustrates with examples on ℝ² and S².
AI.motivation: To extend the notion of canonoid transformations—coordinate-preserving, structure-preserving maps—to non-invertible settings ('fouling maps') and systematically generate polynomial constants of motion for mechanical systems within time-independent Hamiltonian mechanics.
AI.method: Uses tensor calculus on cotangent bundles T*Q; constructs polynomial fouling maps via symmetric (k+1,0)-tensor fields on semi-Riemannian configuration spaces; derives invariance conditions under Hamiltonian flow; analyzes traces of induced (1,1)-tensor fields as conserved quantities.
AI.result: Each polynomial fouling map yields a Hamiltonian-flow-invariant (1,1)-tensor field; traces of its powers are polynomial first integrals; full characterization is given for mechanical Hamiltonians; explicit constructions provided for Euclidean plane and 2-sphere.
AI.conclusion: Fouling maps provide a geometrically natural, tensor-based framework for generating polynomial constants of motion beyond canonical symmetry methods; the approach unifies and generalizes known canonoid constructions while accommodating non-invertibility and broader geometric settings.

title: The semileptonic decays of $\mathcal{B}_{Q_{1}Q_{2}}(\frac{1}{2}^{+})\rightarrow\mathcal{B}_{Q_{1}}^{*}(\frac{3}{2}^{+})$ in QCD sum rules
summary: In the framework of QCD sum rules, we systematically analyze the weak transition process $\mathcal{B}_{Q_{1}Q_{2}}(\frac{1}{2}^{+})\rightarrow\mathcal{B}_{Q_{1}}^{*}(\frac{3}{2}^{+})$. When doing the operator product expansion in the QCD side, we consider the contributions of perturbative part and vacuum condensate terms up to dimension 6. In the phenomenological side, we eliminate the interferences of the low spin states and negative parity states by employing 16 different dirac structures. As an application, these form factors are finally used to analyze the semileptonic decays of $\mathcal{B}_{Q_{1}Q_{2}}(\frac{1}{2}^{+})\rightarrow\mathcal{B}_{Q_{1}}^{*}(\frac{3}{2}^{+})lν$, where these decays are driven by the transition processes $c\rightarrow d/s+l^{+}+ν_{l}$ and $b\rightarrow u+l^{-}+\overlineν_{l}$. The predicted physical quantities include not only the partial widths, ratios of $Γ_{L}/Γ_{T}$ and the branching fractions, but also some observables such as the forward-backward asymmetry parameter $A_{FB}^{l}$ of lepton, the $P_z^{F}$ component of the polarization vector for daughter baryon and the longitudinal polarization of the lepton $P_z^{l}$. We hope all of these theoretical predictions about the weak decays will be helpful for studying the properties of doubly heavy baryons in experiments in the future.
