title: Non-Abelian Thirring model at large $N$
summary: We consider the non-Abelian bosonized Thirring model for a semi-simple group $G$ at level $k$, with deformation parameter $λ$. We compute the two-point correlation functions of current and composite current operators to cubic order in $λ$, assuming large values of the quadratic Casimir $c_G$ of the group $G$ in the adjoint representation. From these, we extract the $β$-function and the anomalous dimensions of both the current and composite current operators, showing the absence of an additional critical point of order $k/c_G$. Our findings align with those of Destri & de Vega for the Fermionic non-Abelian Thirring model, but contradict the claim in Dashen & Frishman regarding the existence of an additional fixed point of order $1/c_G$.

AI.tldr: The paper computes two-point correlation functions in the non-Abelian bosonized Thirring model to cubic order in deformation parameter λ, under large-c_G approximation, and finds no additional fixed point at order k/c_G or 1/c_G—confirming Destri & de Vega but contradicting Dashen & Frishman.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies in the literature—specifically, whether an additional critical point exists at order 1/c_G in the non-Abelian Thirring model—by performing a controlled perturbative calculation in the bosonized formulation.
AI.method: Perturbative computation of current and composite current two-point functions up to O(λ³), using large-c_G (quadratic Casimir in adjoint representation) expansion within the bosonized non-Abelian Thirring model at level k.
AI.result: The β-function and anomalous dimensions are derived; no additional fixed point is found at order k/c_G or 1/c_G; results agree with Destri & de Vega’s fermionic analysis but refute Dashen & Frishman’s claim of a 1/c_G fixed point.
AI.conclusion: The absence of the claimed 1/c_G fixed point supports universality between fermionic and bosonized formulations and invalidates prior assertions based on inconsistent approximations.

title: Asymptotic analysis of varying light speed cosmologies
summary: We investigate potential singularities in isotropic cosmological models featuring a time-varying speed of light and the gravitational constant. The governing field equations generally simplify into two-dimensional systems, subject to analysis through dynamical systems techniques within phase space and the application of asymptotic splitting methods. In the broader context, our findings reveal the existence of initially expanding closed models that undergo subsequent recollapse towards a future singularity, and open universes exhibiting perpetual expansion into the future. The specific characteristics of these singularities are also expounded upon.

AI.tldr: This paper studies singularities in isotropic cosmological models with time-varying speed of light and gravitational constant, using dynamical systems and asymptotic splitting methods; it finds recollapsing closed models and eternally expanding open models, characterizing their singularities.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature and existence of singularities in isotropic cosmologies where fundamental constants (c and G) vary with time—a departure from standard general relativity—motivated by theories seeking to resolve early-universe problems or unify gravity with other forces.
AI.method: Reduction of field equations to two-dimensional autonomous dynamical systems; phase-space analysis (including fixed points, stability, and trajectories); asymptotic splitting methods to characterize late- and early-time singular behavior.
AI.result: Closed isotropic models with varying c and G can expand initially then recollapse into a future singularity; open models exhibit forever-expanding behavior without singularity formation in the future; singularity types (e.g., curvature, sudden, or weak) are classified based on asymptotic scaling of geometric and matter variables.
AI.conclusion: Time variation of c and G significantly alters singularity structure compared to standard GR: recollapse is possible even in non-Lambda models, and singularity avoidance is not generic—topology and parameter choices critically determine fate.

title: Baxter Q-operators from a Schwinger-Boson construction of the master T-operator and the mKP hierarchy
summary: The master T-operator is a generating function for transfer matrices and a tau-function of the modified KP (mKP) hierarchy. It is conventionally introduced through a Schur-function expansion whose coefficients are fused transfer matrices satisfying the Cherednik--Bazhanov--Reshetikhin determinant formula. For rational inhomogeneous gl(M) spin chains, we give an alternative definition: we realize gl(M) on an auxiliary Fock space generated by finitely many families of Schwinger bosons, form a monodromy matrix from the resulting L-operator, and define the master T-operator as its trace over the Fock space. Howe duality then reproduces the Schur-function expansion. This realization relates two constructions of Baxter Q-operators. In the construction of [arXiv:1112.3310] (see also [arXiv:1010.4022]), the Q-operators are obtained from residues of the master T-operator with respect to selected Miwa variables. In the construction of [arXiv:1010.3699], they are defined using degenerate Yangian L-operators in oscillator form. When selected Miwa variables approach the inverses of boundary-twist eigenvalues, the defining trace develops poles. After a suitable rescaling of this L-operator, only the terms contributing to the highest-order pole survive in the normalized limit; before the trace is taken, they form the degenerate Yangian L-operator of the second construction. The trace then gives an explicit residue formula for the corresponding Q-operator. Independently, a Holstein--Primakoff-type large-occupation-number contraction of this L-operator on subspaces with fixed total occupation numbers yields the same degenerate Yangian L-operator.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an alternative Fock-space realization of the master T-operator for rational gl(M) spin chains using Schwinger bosons, linking two distinct constructions of Baxter Q-operators via Miwa-variable residues and degenerate Yangian L-operators; it shows that pole limits and Holstein–Primakoff contractions both yield the same degenerate L-operator, enabling explicit residue formulas for Q-operators.
AI.motivation: To unify and clarify the relationship between two seemingly different constructions of Baxter Q-operators — one based on residues of the master T-operator in Miwa variables, and another based on degenerate Yangian L-operators in oscillator form — by providing a concrete Fock-space realization of the master T-operator.
AI.method: Constructs the master T-operator as the trace of a monodromy matrix over a gl(M)-realizing auxiliary Fock space built from finitely many Schwinger boson families; employs Howe duality to recover the Schur expansion; analyzes pole behavior as selected Miwa variables approach inverses of twist eigenvalues; performs rescaling and normalized limit to extract highest-order pole contributions; independently applies Holstein–Primakoff-type large-occupation-number contraction on fixed-total-occupation subspaces.
AI.result: Demonstrates equivalence between the residue-based and oscillator-based Q-operator constructions: the degenerate Yangian L-operator emerges universally — both as the leading pole contribution after rescaling and as the large-occupation limit of the Schwinger-boson L-operator; yields an explicit residue formula for Q-operators.
AI.conclusion: The Fock-space realization unifies the two Q-operator frameworks, revealing their common origin in the analytic structure (poles) and semiclassical limit (large occupation) of the master T-operator, thereby deepening the integrable structure of rational gl(M) spin chains.

title: Could $\barΛ_c$ and $Λ_c$ form bound hadronic molecule with explicit $P-wave$ ?
summary: In this article, the explicit $P-wave$ of the $\barΛ_cΛ_c$ dibaryon states with the $J^{PC}=0^{-\pm}$ and $1^{-\pm}$ are studied via twelve interpolated currents. Results show that the positive and negative charge conjugations for the studied states do not have too much difference, the contribution of the gluon from covariant derivative of the current with $P-wave$ could be neglected. The numerical results of the masses of the $P-wave$ $\barΛ_cΛ_c$ are high above the threshold of the two $\barΛ_c$ and $Λ_c$ baryon constituents, $\barΛ_c$ and $Λ_c$ are unlikely to form the bound molecules with explicit $P-wave$ . Pole residues of the related states are also calculated.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates P-wave ̄Λ_cΛ_c dibaryon states with quantum numbers J^{PC} = 0^{-±}, 1^{-±} using twelve interpolating currents in QCD sum rules; it finds no bound states due to masses lying far above the ̄Λ_c + Λ_c threshold, negligible gluonic contributions from covariant derivatives, and small differences between C-even and C-odd channels.
AI.motivation: To determine whether ̄Λ_cΛ_c dibaryons can form stable or resonant P-wave molecular bound states, motivated by ongoing searches for exotic hadrons and the role of heavy-quark symmetry in dibaryon spectroscopy.
AI.method: QCD sum rule analysis with twelve Lorentz- and Dirac-structure-distinct interpolating currents tailored for J^{PC} = 0^{-±}, 1^{-±} P-wave ̄Λ_cΛ_c configurations; includes operator product expansion up to dimension-6 condensates, spectral density modeling, and pole residue extraction.
AI.result: All calculated P-wave ̄Λ_cΛ_c masses significantly exceed the ̄Λ_c + Λ_c threshold (~4.62 GeV); C-parity splitting is minimal; gluonic corrections from covariant derivatives are numerically negligible; pole residues are obtained but indicate no binding.
AI.conclusion: No evidence for bound P-wave ̄Λ_cΛ_c dibaryons; such states are unbound and likely appear only as broad, non-resonant scattering enhancements—if at all—in the ̄Λ_cΛ_c channel.

title: The Information Content of Krylov Observables: A Machine Learning Approach
summary: We employ machine learning to quantify the information carried by three Krylov-space observables: the spread complexity $\mathcal{C}(t)$, the discrete Wigner negativity $N(t)$, and the normalized negativity $χ(t)=N(t)/|S(t)|$, with $S(t)$ the survival amplitude, recently proposed as a second-moment infall probe (arXiv:2607.04065). Small residual networks (16-32 neurons) and boosted trees are trained on half of $\sim 57{,}000$ labeled evolutions spanning the GUE, GOE and Poisson ensembles, the integrable $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$/CFT sector, and the chaos interpolation $H(\varepsilon)=H_{SL(2,\mathbb{R})}+\varepsilon R_0 W_{GUE}$. Either moment determines the thermofield temperature at $R^2\simeq 0.999$. Neither reconstructs the fine spectral form factor ($R^2\simeq 0.18$ in every ensemble); smoothing the target does not repair this, and windows wide enough to help erase the dip-ramp physics itself: the SFF strictly refines both moments. The coarse $e^S$ plateau is nevertheless recovered at $R^2=0.861$, mostly from the first 20% of $\mathcal{C}(t)$. A single curve identifies the symmetry class at up to 98% accuracy. In the integrable sector the observables are informationally equivalent, as exact negative-binomial slaving demands, while the negativity best resolves the $(h,α)$ degeneracy ($N\to h$: 0.999). Along the interpolation the asymmetry gap of $χ$ over $\mathcal{C}$ switches on with chaos, growing from +0.33 to +0.77 as the level statistics cross to GUE, while the raw-$N$ gap decays to zero. The second-moment informational surplus is therefore a signature of chaos, carried specifically by the normalized negativity, and we derive an analytical mechanism and a quantitative bound for it.

AI.tldr: This paper uses machine learning to assess how much information about quantum chaos and spectral statistics is encoded in three Krylov-space observables—spread complexity ℂ(t), discrete Wigner negativity N(t), and normalized negativity χ(t)—across integrable, chaotic, and interpolating Hamiltonians. It finds that χ(t) uniquely carries second-moment informational surplus signaling chaos onset, with analytical justification.
AI.motivation: To quantify and disentangle the informational content of recently proposed Krylov-space observables—particularly their ability to diagnose quantum chaos, symmetry classes, thermofield temperature, and spectral form factor (SFF) structure—beyond standard measures like level statistics.
AI.method: Trains small residual neural networks (16–32 neurons) and gradient-boosted trees on ~57,000 labeled time-evolution trajectories from GUE, GOE, Poisson, integrable SL(2,R)/CFT, and chaos-interpolated ensembles; evaluates regression accuracy (R²) and classification accuracy for symmetry class identification; analyzes slaving relations, degeneracy resolution, and asymmetry gaps between observables.
AI.result: χ(t) = N(t)/|S(t)| achieves near-perfect thermofield temperature inference (R² ≈ 0.999), outperforms ℂ(t) and N(t) in symmetry-class classification (up to 98%), resolves (h,α) degeneracy best (R² = 0.999 for N→h), and exhibits a chaos-triggered asymmetry gap that grows from +0.33 to +0.77 as level statistics transition to GUE; raw N(t) fails to reconstruct fine SFF (R² ≈ 0.18), while smoothed or coarse-grained targets recover only the e^S plateau (R² = 0.861).
AI.conclusion: Normalized negativity χ(t) carries a second-moment informational surplus specific to quantum chaos—distinct from spread complexity and raw negativity—and serves as a robust, analytically grounded diagnostic for chaos onset and symmetry class, surpassing other Krylov observables in both inferential power and physical interpretability.

title: Analytical Study of Deflection Angle and Time Delay in Kerr Spacetime with Modified Propagation
summary:
We investigate gravitational lensing in Kerr spacetime in the presence of a modified photon propagation law arising from higher-curvature effective field theory corrections. Adopting a deformed dispersion relation, we analytically derive the deflection angle and the propagation time delay for null trajectories in a rotating background.
  We show that the modified propagation leads to explicit and calculable deviations from the standard Kerr predictions, affecting both the bending angle and the time delay. These corrections exhibit a nontrivial dependence on the black hole spin and are expected to become more relevant in the strong-field regime. In particular, near the photon region-where the spin-dependent geometry influences photon trajectories-such effects may play a role in shaping observable propagation features.
  Our results establish a concrete and systematic framework to quantify deviations from standard photon propagation in gravitational lensing. They further indicate that observables such as relativistic image separations and time delays provide a potential avenue to probe ultraviolet corrections to gravity in strong-field environments.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically computes gravitational lensing observables (deflection angle and time delay) for photons in Kerr spacetime under a higher-curvature EFT-modified dispersion relation, revealing spin- and strong-field–dependent deviations from standard GR predictions—offering a pathway to test UV gravity via relativistic imaging and timing.
AI.motivation: To probe ultraviolet (UV) corrections to general relativity in strong-field regimes using observable gravitational lensing effects induced by higher-curvature effective field theory (EFT) modifications to photon propagation.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the null geodesic deflection angle and coordinate time delay in Kerr spacetime under a deformed (EFT-motivated) photon dispersion relation; explicit treatment of spin-dependent geometry and photon region effects.
AI.result: Quantitative, spin-dependent deviations from standard Kerr lensing predictions for both deflection angle and time delay; enhanced sensitivity in the strong-field regime, especially near the photon region; identification of relativistic image separations and time delays as viable probes of UV gravity.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a systematic, observationally grounded method to constrain higher-curvature EFT corrections to gravity using high-precision strong-field lensing data.

title: Universal Correlators on Exponentially Ramified Spectral Curves
summary: We investigate generalized topological recursion on compact spectral curves admitting exponential, and more generally essential, singularities as ramification points. Exploiting the global formulation of generalized topological recursion, we establish a contour deformation of the recursive residue formula that replaces contributions from these essential singularities by residues at meromorphic points. This provides a natural recursive framework for exponentially ramified spectral curves while remaining entirely within the generalized topological recursion formalism. Our formalism can also be viewed as a limiting case of the Bouchard-Eynard higher-order topological recursion, obtained when the order of a ramification point tends to infinity in a convergent manner, as occurs, for example, for exponential singularities while $dy$ remains regular and non-vanishing. We further illustrate the resulting formalism through several examples, including transcendental functions and the $x$-$y$ dual of the Mirzakhani curve.

AI.tldr: This paper extends generalized topological recursion to compact spectral curves with exponential/essential singularities by introducing a contour deformation technique that replaces essential singularity contributions with residues at meromorphic points, yielding a consistent recursive framework; it also interprets this as an infinite-order limit of Bouchard–Eynard recursion and validates it on transcendental functions and the Mirzakhani curve dual.
AI.motivation: To extend generalized topological recursion to spectral curves with exponential or essential singularities—points where standard ramification-based recursion fails—while preserving formal consistency and enabling computation.
AI.method: Uses global formulation of generalized topological recursion; applies contour deformation of the recursive residue formula to convert essential singularity contributions into finite sums of residues at meromorphic points; interprets resulting structure as a convergent infinite-order limit of Bouchard–Eynard higher-order topological recursion.
AI.result: A well-defined, fully recursive framework for exponentially ramified spectral curves within generalized topological recursion; explicit examples confirm applicability to transcendental functions and the x–y dual of the Mirzakhani curve.
AI.conclusion: Essential singularities can be consistently incorporated into topological recursion via contour deformation, bridging exponential ramification with existing formalisms and expanding the scope of spectral curve applications in enumerative geometry and mathematical physics.

title: The muon collider: expected physics, technological solutions, and the prospect of a 21 km ring at the UNK site
summary: A multi-TeV muon collider has emerged as one of the most compelling options for the post-LHC energy frontier. Because the muon is an elementary particle that radiates $\sim\!10^9$ times less synchrotron power than an electron of the same energy, a circular muon collider delivers the full beam energy to the hard collision in a remarkably compact ring, combining the energy reach of a $100$~TeV-class proton machine with the clean final states of a lepton collider. This review summarizes the expected physics results -- Higgs couplings and self-couplings, electroweak and vector-boson-fusion processes, the top quark, a broad beyond-the-Standard Model programme, and a near-complete closure of the thermal window for electroweak WIMP dark matter -- and the status of the enabling technologies, emphasizing for each challenge how it is being solved and where the solution is documented: muon production, ionization cooling (demonstrated in the transverse plane by MICE), rapid acceleration, high-field HTS magnets, the machine-detector interface, and the neutrino-flux constraint. Building on this foundation, this review examines the prospect of housing a muon collider in the existing 21~km UNK tunnel near Protvino, where the magnetic-rigidity relation maps realistic arc fields onto a centre-of-mass energy of order $10$-$20$ TeV -- reaching the IMCC 10~TeV reference with conventional dipoles and exceeding it with high-temperature-superconductor dipoles. It closes with a discussion of non-collider applications of the intense muon beams such a facility would develop -- muon-catalyzed fusion, muography, muonic-atom isotopic analysis, and muon spin spectroscopy -- several with a long tradition in the Russian physics institutes.

AI.tldr: This review outlines the physics potential and technological feasibility of a multi-TeV muon collider, highlighting its advantages over proton and electron colliders, expected precision measurements (Higgs, EW, top, BSM, dark matter), status of key R&D (ionization cooling, HTS magnets, etc.), and a concrete proposal to host a 10–20 TeV collider in the existing UNK tunnel; it also surveys non-collider muon beam applications.
AI.motivation: To assess the viability and scientific impact of a multi-TeV muon collider as the leading post-LHC energy-frontier facility, leveraging the muon’s low synchrotron radiation for high-energy, high-luminosity, clean collisions in a compact footprint.
AI.method: Comprehensive review synthesizing accelerator physics, detector design, particle phenomenology, and ongoing R&D—particularly referencing experimental milestones (e.g., MICE for ionization cooling) and engineering constraints (neutrino flux, machine-detector interface, HTS magnet development)—alongside site-specific feasibility analysis for the UNK tunnel.
AI.result: A muon collider offers unique sensitivity across Higgs physics, electroweak precision tests, top quark studies, BSM searches, and thermal WIMP dark matter parameter space closure; key technologies are progressing with documented solutions (e.g., transverse cooling demonstrated by MICE, HTS dipole development); a 10–20 TeV collider is feasible in the UNK tunnel using conventional or HTS magnets.
AI.conclusion: The multi-TeV muon collider stands out as a scientifically compelling and increasingly technologically viable option for the next energy frontier; its realization would enable unparalleled precision and discovery reach, with strong synergy between collider and non-collider muon applications—especially within Russian scientific infrastructure.

title: Geometric Approach to Quantum Theory. L-functionals
summary: This publication consists of slides from my talk at the Simons Center for Geometry and Physics in 2024. It contains a brief review of the L-functional formalism, along with a discussion of its possible applications to QED, linearized gravity, and quenched disorder. The most interesting part is the discussion of the infrared problem in QED and a conjecture on how to construct an infrared-finite perturbation theory for QED.

AI.tldr: This talk presents a review of the L-functional formalism and explores its potential applications to QED, linearized gravity, and quenched disorder, with emphasis on resolving the infrared problem in QED via a conjectured infrared-finite perturbation theory.
AI.motivation: To address the long-standing infrared (IR) problem in quantum electrodynamics (QED) and explore broader applicability of the L-functional formalism to other physical systems including linearized gravity and disordered systems.
AI.method: Review and conceptual extension of the L-functional formalism; qualitative discussion and conjectural construction of an infrared-finite perturbative framework for QED.
AI.result: A novel conjecture for an infrared-finite perturbation theory in QED; preliminary indications of utility of the L-functional formalism in linearized gravity and quenched disorder.
AI.conclusion: The L-functional formalism offers a promising avenue for tackling IR divergences in QED and may generalize to other gauge and disordered systems, though full technical realization remains open.

title: Perturbations of black holes in mass-varying massive gravity
summary: Based on eigendecomposition and matrix perturbation theory, we propose an alternative method for analyzing perturbations in massive gravity that is applicable to both the base theory and its various modifications. We demonstrate the validity of this approach even in seemingly singular regimes. Applying this framework to mass-varying massive gravity, we compute perturbations for all constant-scalar Schwarzschild-(A)dS black hole solutions. We show that, under the condition $β= α^2$, the tensor sector of these black holes reduces to that of general relativity, while the scalar sector remains free from tachyonic instabilities given appropriate parameter choices. A deeper relationship is also revealed between the solutions with generic parameters and those with $β= α^2$: their solution manifolds intersect at a specific locus where the perturbation vanishes.

AI.tldr: Proposes a robust eigendecomposition-based perturbation analysis for massive gravity, applicable even in singular regimes; applies it to mass-varying massive gravity, showing GR-like tensor behavior and tachyon-free scalar sector when β = α², and reveals a vanishing-perturbation intersection locus between generic and β = α² solution manifolds.
AI.motivation: To develop a reliable, broadly applicable method for analyzing perturbations in massive gravity—including its modifications—especially in regimes where conventional approaches fail (e.g., seemingly singular limits).
AI.method: Uses eigendecomposition and matrix perturbation theory to construct a coordinate- and gauge-invariant framework for linear perturbations around black hole backgrounds in massive gravity.
AI.result: 1) Validated framework works in singular regimes; 2) Full perturbation spectra computed for constant-scalar Schwarzschild-(A)dS black holes in mass-varying massive gravity; 3) Tensor sector matches GR when β = α²; 4) Scalar sector is tachyon-free for suitable parameters; 5) Generic and β = α² solution manifolds intersect at a locus where perturbations vanish.
AI.conclusion: Eigendecomposition-based perturbation theory provides a unified, robust tool for stability analysis in massive gravity; the β = α² condition yields GR-equivalent tensor dynamics while preserving healthy scalar degrees of freedom, and the vanishing-perturbation intersection reveals structural rigidity in the solution space.

title: On the use of equilibrium models to describe dynamic adsorption regimes
summary: We present a column adsorption model that couples a Pseudo-First-Order (PFO) kinetic formulation with the Sips isotherm framework. Using a traveling wave approximation, we derive analytical solutions for specific operating conditions. Qualitatively, these solutions deviate significantly from their pure Sips counterparts: instead of a smooth, continuous increase in concentration at the column outlet, the PFO-Sips model predicts an abrupt, sudden breakthrough. We validate these analytical solutions against diverse experimental datasets from the literature. The results reveal that the PFO-based model consistently underperforms compared to the original Sips formulation. Furthermore, this validation exposes fundamental inconsistencies within the PFO framework. We demonstrate that despite its widespread use in the literature for almost a century, the PFO model is inherently flawed and structurally unfit for describing column adsorption dynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a PFO-Sips column adsorption model, derives analytical traveling-wave solutions showing abrupt breakthrough (vs. smooth Sips), and validates it against experimental data—finding the PFO-based model consistently inferior and fundamentally flawed for column dynamics.
AI.motivation: To critically assess the applicability of the widely used Pseudo-First-Order (PFO) kinetics when coupled with the Sips isotherm for modeling column adsorption dynamics, motivated by observed qualitative discrepancies and longstanding uncritical adoption of PFO.
AI.method: Develops a coupled PFO-Sips column adsorption model; applies traveling wave approximation to obtain analytical breakthrough solutions; compares predictions qualitatively (breakthrough shape) and quantitatively against multiple literature experimental datasets.
AI.result: Analytical solutions exhibit abrupt breakthrough (unlike smooth Sips); empirical validation shows systematic underperformance of PFO-Sips vs. pure Sips; reveals structural inconsistencies in PFO kinetics for dynamic column modeling.
AI.conclusion: The Pseudo-First-Order kinetic model is inherently unsuitable for column adsorption modeling due to fundamental structural flaws, despite its century-long use—calling for rigorous re-evaluation and replacement with mechanistically sound alternatives.

title: Geometric Scaling and the Odderon
summary:
Based on geometric scaling of elastic $pp$ and possibly $p\bar{p}$ cross-sections, we derive simple formulae for
  the complex crossing-even and crossing-odd scattering amplitudes in terms of two interaction radii: $R(s)$ and $Q(s)$, respectively.
  Employing the COMPETE parametrization of the total cross-sections, we reproduce $ρ^{pp}$ and $ρ^{p\bar{p}}$ parameters with high
  accuracy, however we miss the 13~TeV TOTEM and ATLAS points. We show that a slight modification of the $p\bar{p}$ total cross-section
  corresponding to the Odderon, allows to accommodate $ρ^{pp}$ 13~TeV data.

AI.tldr: The paper derives scattering amplitudes for pp and p̄p collisions using geometric scaling and two interaction radii, reproducing ρ parameters with COMPETE parametrization but failing at 13 TeV; a modified odderon-influenced p̄p cross-section resolves the discrepancy.
AI.motivation: To reconcile theoretical predictions of the real-to-imaginary ratio (ρ) of forward scattering amplitudes with high-energy collider data, especially the anomalous 13 TeV TOTEM/ATLAS ρ^{pp} measurements.
AI.method: Geometric scaling applied to elastic pp and p̄p cross-sections; derivation of crossing-even and crossing-odd amplitudes parameterized by interaction radii R(s) and Q(s); use of COMPETE total cross-section parametrization; phenomenological adjustment of the odderon-driven p̄p cross-section component.
AI.result: High-accuracy reproduction of ρ^{pp} and ρ^{p̄p} across most energies; failure at 13 TeV for pp; successful accommodation of 13 TeV ρ^{pp} after introducing a small odderon-induced modification to the p̄p total cross-section.
AI.conclusion: The odderon contribution—encoded via a slight adjustment to the p̄p total cross-section—is necessary to explain the 13 TeV ρ^{pp} data, supporting odderon existence within this geometric scaling framework.

title: The next-to-next-to-leading order BFKL eigenvalue at odd conformal spin in planar N=4 super Yang-Mills
summary: We present the three-loop (next-to-next-to-leading order) BFKL eigenvalue of planar N=4 super Yang-Mills at odd conformal spin n in closed form, as a finite combination of nested harmonic sums and rational functions of z=(|n|-1)/2 + i nu. For each odd n>=3 the atom table is extracted exactly, in rational arithmetic, from the Caron-Huot-Herranen three-loop integrand by direct Mellin extraction; a shipped command regenerates it on demand, with n=1 a supplied boundary block. The coefficients are rational multiples of 1, pi^2 and zeta_3; in a fixed elementary basis, forty of the forty-seven coefficient slots close as harmonic sums of the two ladder distances (all-spin form conjectural, the split a property of the basis), while the residual five-kernel layer includes one grid obeying a finite-data holonomic recurrence, an all-n rule for the rest still open. Beyond the explicit harmonic sums the coefficient-weighted ladder collapses onto depth-one digamma and trigamma functions. At nu=0 the intercepts reproduce the independent Quantum Spectral Curve values spin by spin through n=91. At each odd spin the eigenvalue is strictly product-free, the additive case of the Kotikov-Lipatov hermitian-separable form; the next-to-leading anomalous term carrying 1+(-1)^n is absent at odd n. No n-uniform form is claimed. Derivations (eleven of sixteen kernel closures proven, five verified numerically) and complete expressions are given in a companion paper.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the three-loop BFKL eigenvalue in planar N=4 SYM for odd conformal spin n, expressing it in closed form using nested harmonic sums and rational functions of z = (|n|−1)/2 + iν; coefficients involve 1, π², ζ₃; the structure is strictly product-free and hermitian-separable at odd n; intercepts match Quantum Spectral Curve predictions up to spin 91.
AI.motivation: To obtain a closed-form, analytically tractable expression for the three-loop BFKL eigenvalue in planar N=4 super Yang-Mills theory at odd conformal spin, enabling high-precision checks against independent methods (e.g., Quantum Spectral Curve) and revealing structural properties like hermitian separability and absence of next-to-leading anomalous terms.
AI.method: Direct Mellin extraction from the Caron-Huot-Herranen three-loop integrand; exact rational-arithmetic computation of 'atom tables' for each odd n ≥ 3 (with n = 1 as boundary); systematic decomposition into harmonic sums, digamma/trigamma functions, and kernel layers governed by holonomic recurrences; use of a fixed elementary basis to expose ladder-distance structure.
AI.result: Closed-form three-loop BFKL eigenvalue for all odd n, expressed as finite combinations of nested harmonic sums and rational functions of z; coefficients are rational multiples of 1, π², ζ₃; 40/47 coefficient slots close as harmonic sums of two ladder distances; residual 5-kernel layer includes one holonomically constrained grid; ν = 0 intercepts match QSC up to n = 91; strict product-freeness and Kotikov-Lipatov hermitian separability confirmed at odd n.
AI.conclusion: The three-loop BFKL eigenvalue in planar N=4 SYM admits an exact, closed-form representation at odd conformal spin, exposing deep algebraic and analytic structures—harmonic sum decomposability, ladder-distance dependence, digamma/trigamma reduction, and hermitian separability—while validating consistency with the Quantum Spectral Curve to unprecedented spin (n = 91).

title: Probing Nonlinear Logarithmic Kalb-Ramond Black Holes: Particle Dynamics, Epicyclic Oscillations and Thermodynamic Signatures
summary: In contrast to conventional linear coupling frameworks, the proposed work investigated the nonlinear effects that become more significant in the strong field regime of a black hole. We have investigated a new class of Kalb Ramond black holes generated by a nonlinear logarithmic coupling of the field, referred to as a Logarithmic Kalb Ramond black hole. The logarithmic coupling introduces strong-field modifications to the spacetime geometry, leading to significant departures from the Schwarzschild and Reissner Nordstrom BHs. We analyze the motion of test particles using the effective potential formalism and derive the conserved energy and angular momentum for circular equatorial geodesics. The stability of circular orbits and the location of the innermost stable circular orbit are examined, revealing a strong dependence on the model parameters Q, l, and $β$. The epicyclic frequencies (radial, vertical, and azimuthal) together with the associated periastron precession demonstrate that nonlinear logarithmic corrections can substantially modify quasi periodic oscillation observables. We further investigate the Hawking temperature and energy emission rate, which show that the nonlinear coupling also impacts distinct imprints on the thermodynamic behavior and evaporation characteristics of the black hole. Our results also identify the BH parameters as key regulators of the orbital dynamics, oscillatory properties, and thermal evolution, providing a unified framework for probing nonlinear KR gravity through strong-field astrophysical phenomena.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel Logarithmic Kalb-Ramond black hole solution arising from nonlinear logarithmic coupling in strong-field gravity, analyzing its geodesic structure, orbital stability, QPOs, and thermodynamics—revealing parameter-dependent deviations from Schwarzschild and RN black holes.
AI.motivation: To explore nonlinear gravitational effects beyond linear Kalb-Ramond coupling, particularly in the strong-field regime near black holes, where conventional linear frameworks break down.
AI.method: Constructs a new black hole solution—Logarithmic Kalb-Ramond BH—via nonlinear logarithmic field coupling; employs effective potential formalism to study timelike geodesics, computes ISCO, epicyclic frequencies, periastron precession, Hawking temperature, and energy emission rate.
AI.result: Nonlinear logarithmic coupling induces significant spacetime deviations from Schwarzschild/RN metrics; circular orbit stability, ISCO radius, QPO frequencies (radial/vertical/azimuthal), periastron shift, Hawking temperature, and evaporation rate all exhibit strong dependence on parameters Q (KR charge), l (length scale), and β (nonlinearity strength).
AI.conclusion: Logarithmic Kalb-Ramond gravity provides a phenomenologically rich extension of GR in strong fields, with model parameters Q, l, β acting as key regulators of orbital dynamics, quasi-periodic oscillations, and thermodynamics—enabling astrophysical tests of nonlinear KR gravity.

title: $(1,k)$ CFT and RH problem with the $c=-2$ case
summary: Following approach of Iorgov--Lisovyy--Teschner, we construct solutions of the (modified) Riemann--Hilbert problem using conformal blocks of $(1,k)$ Virasoro models. For $k>1$ case, the solution of this Riemann--Hilbert problem is not unique due to more singular behavior at punctures. On the CFT side the dimension of the space of conformal blocks also increases. We specifically study the $k=2$ case, which corresponds to the central charge $c=-2$ and symplectic fermions. We explicitly construct a corresponding solution of the modified Riemann--Hilbert problem in the case of 3 punctures and prove its uniqueness under suitable initial data conditions. We also obtain new bilinear relations for $c=-2$ tau functions.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs solutions to a modified Riemann–Hilbert problem using conformal blocks from (1,k) Virasoro models, focusing on the k=2 (c=−2, symplectic fermions) case with three punctures; it proves uniqueness under initial data and derives new bilinear relations for c=−2 tau functions.
AI.motivation: To extend the Iorgov–Lisovyy–Teschner approach to non-unique Riemann–Hilbert problems arising from higher-singularity behavior at punctures in (1,k) Virasoro CFTs, particularly for k>1 where conformal block spaces grow in dimension.
AI.method: Uses conformal blocks of (1,k) Virasoro minimal models—especially the k=2 (c=−2, symplectic fermions) model—to construct and analyze solutions of the modified Riemann–Hilbert problem; employs explicit computation and uniqueness analysis for the 3-puncture case, and derives bilinear identities for associated tau functions.
AI.result: An explicit, uniquely determined solution of the modified Riemann–Hilbert problem for k=2 (c=−2) with three punctures under specified initial conditions; derivation of novel bilinear relations for c=−2 tau functions.
AI.conclusion: The correspondence between (1,k) Virasoro conformal blocks and solutions of modified Riemann–Hilbert problems holds beyond the k=1 case; for k=2, uniqueness is recovered with appropriate initial data, and new structural identities (bilinear tau relations) emerge, enriching the integrable/CFT interface.

title: Imprints of Higgs-portal fermionic dark matter on neutron-star tidal deformability and the mass-radius slope
summary: We investigate the structure of neutron stars (NSs) admixed with fermionic dark matter (DM) using three density-dependent relativistic mean-field (DDRMF) functionals (DDME, DDB, and GDFM) for $β$-equilibrated nucleonic matter. Modeling DM as the lightest neutralino interacting via Higgs exchange, we treat the DM Fermi momentum $k_F^{\rm DM}$ as a control parameter in the range $0.02$-$0.06$ GeV. We solve the coupled mean-field and Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations to obtain the mass-radius relation, maximum mass $M_{\rm max}$, radial sound speed profile $c_s^2$, and tidal deformability $Λ$. In all models, DM softens the equation of state, systematically reducing $M_{\rm max}$, the radius $R_{1.4}$ (at $1.4M_{\odot}$), and the tidal deformability $Λ_{1.4}$ (at $1.4M_{\odot}$) as $k_F^{\rm DM}$ increases. Consequently, the $2 M_\odot$ pulsar limit and NICER data place a model-dependent upper limit on the DM content, while the GW170817 tidal bound requires a minimal DM content for the stiffest functional. Using a recent Bayesian inference of the DDRMF equation of state as the nucleonic reference band, we evaluate if this DM imprint can be distinguished from nucleonic uncertainties using only measureable quantities. Analyzing the tidal deformability $Λ$ and mass-radius slope $dR/dM$ at fixed mass, we find that $Λ$ is a sharp discriminator: at $1.4 M_\odot$ and $k_F^{\rm DM}=0.06$ GeV, the DM-induced reduction of $Λ$ reaches $\simeq 8$ times the nucleonic $1σ$ width (model-independently $7.5$-$7.8σ$). The DM track leaves the nucleonic $1σ$ band for $k_F^{\rm DM}\gtrsim0.03$-$0.04$ GeV, whereas $dR/dM$ becomes diagnostic only for the heavier ($1.8$-$2.0 M_\odot$) branch.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how fermionic dark matter (neutralinos) affects neutron star structure using DDRMF models; DM softens the equation of state, reducing maximum mass, radius, and tidal deformability; tidal deformability Λ at 1.4 M⊙ is a highly sensitive, model-independent probe—DM-induced changes exceed nucleonic uncertainties by ~7.5–7.8σ for k_F^DM = 0.06 GeV.
AI.motivation: To assess whether admixed fermionic dark matter in neutron stars leaves a distinguishable imprint on observable properties (e.g., mass-radius relation, tidal deformability) beyond inherent uncertainties from nucleonic equation-of-state modeling.
AI.method: Solves coupled relativistic mean-field and TOV equations using three DDRMF functionals (DDME, DDB, GDFM) for β-equilibrated nucleonic matter + neutralino DM (Higgs-mediated); treats DM Fermi momentum k_F^DM (0.02–0.06 GeV) as control parameter; employs Bayesian nucleonic EoS band as reference to quantify distinguishability.
AI.result: DM universally softens EoS, lowering M_max, R_1.4, Λ_1.4; Λ at 1.4 M⊙ shows ~8× nucleonic 1σ width reduction at k_F^DM = 0.06 GeV (7.5–7.8σ significance); DM signature emerges from nucleonic band at k_F^DM ≳ 0.03–0.04 GeV; dR/dM is only diagnostic above ~1.8 M⊙.
AI.conclusion: Tidal deformability Λ at canonical mass is a robust, high-significance observable to detect or constrain fermionic DM admixture in neutron stars, decisively separating DM effects from nucleonic EoS uncertainties.

title: The next-to-next-to-leading order BFKL eigenvalue at odd conformal spin in planar N=4 super Yang-Mills: closed form, coefficient structure, and arithmetic
summary: We present the three-loop (next-to-next-to-leading order) BFKL eigenvalue of planar N=4 super Yang-Mills at odd conformal spin n in closed form, as a finite combination of continued nested harmonic sums and rational functions of z=(|n|-1)/2 + i nu on an integer-shifted ladder. For each odd spin the atom table is extracted exactly, in rational arithmetic, from the Caron-Huot-Herranen three-loop integrand; a shipped command regenerates it for any odd n>=3, with n=1 a supplied boundary block. A resummed master generating function, conjectured to reproduce those integrands at every spin (verified through n=17 and at m=9,11,13,15,21,31), is not used for the per-spin tables. At nu=0 the intercepts reproduce the independent Quantum Spectral Curve values spin by spin through n=91. The coefficients are rational multiples of 1, pi^2 and zeta_3; in a fixed elementary basis, forty of the forty-seven slots close as harmonic sums of the two ladder distances (all-spin form conjectural). The residual five-kernel layer includes one grid obeying a holonomic recurrence; once the harmonic sums are separated the coefficient-weighted ladder collapses onto two depth-one polygamma transcendentals. We report an arithmetic obstruction: the exceptional-grid coefficients recruit a new denominator prime at each n=p+2 (n-2 prime) through the computed range, a finite law we prove and conjecture to continue; on that continuation their generating data cannot be algebraic or globally bounded. Even spins are conjecturally contained in the same master. At each odd spin the eigenvalue is the product-free case of the Kotikov-Lipatov hermitian-separable form. A companion Letter announces the result.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the three-loop BFKL eigenvalue in planar N=4 SYM for odd conformal spin n in closed form using nested harmonic sums and rational functions of z = (|n|−1)/2 + iν, validated against Quantum Spectral Curve data up to spin 91; it reveals arithmetic obstructions tied to prime denominators and identifies a residual five-kernel structure reducible to polygamma functions.
AI.motivation: To obtain an exact, closed-form expression for the three-loop (NNLO) BFKL eigenvalue in planar N=4 super Yang-Mills theory at arbitrary odd conformal spin n, enabling precise comparison with independent methods (e.g., Quantum Spectral Curve) and uncovering structural and arithmetic properties of high-loop integrability.
AI.method: Exact symbolic computation from the Caron-Huot–Herranen three-loop integrand; extraction of 'atom tables' in rational arithmetic; use of continued nested harmonic sums and rational functions of z = (|n|−1)/2 + iν on an integer-shifted ladder; verification via intercepts at ν = 0 against Quantum Spectral Curve; analysis of coefficient structure, holonomic recurrences, and denominator prime patterns.
AI.result: Closed-form three-loop BFKL eigenvalue for all odd n ≥ 1 expressed as finite combinations of nested harmonic sums and rational functions of z; exact match with QSC intercepts up to n = 91; coefficients are rational multiples of 1, π², ζ₃; 40/47 terms expressible in a fixed elementary basis of ladder-distance harmonic sums; remaining 5-term 'kernel' reduces to two depth-one polygamma functions; discovery of arithmetic obstruction: new denominator prime appears at each n = p + 2 where p is prime.
AI.conclusion: The three-loop BFKL eigenvalue admits a fully explicit, spin-dependent closed form with rich combinatorial–arithmetic structure; the prime-denominator obstruction implies non-algebraicity and lack of global boundedness in generating data; even spins are conjectured to be covered by the same master framework; the result confirms and extends the Kotikov–Lipatov hermitian-separable structure in the product-free limit.

title: Axial Obstructions to Rotating Bumblebee Vacuum Solutions
summary: We identify two general obstructions to a regular rotating constant-norm vector vacua. Firstly, at the poles of a nondegenerate bifurcation surface, horizon and axial invariance force every smooth symmetry-inheriting one-form to vanish, contradicting a strictly nonzero constant norm. Secondly, we show that a conicity varying along a rotation axis generates a singular curvature that diverges as the inverse proper distance from the axis. We apply these results to a general three parameter family Kerr-disformal solution in Einstein--bumblebee gravity. Consequently, its vector vacuum is not smooth on the axes because of a nonzero constant norm, and the position-dependent conicity leads to genuine curvature singularities on the polar axes. A distinguished nonextremal branch nevertheless admits a regular outer Killing horizon away from the axes and defines an exact local rotating solution in the nonpolar region.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies two fundamental obstructions to smooth, rotating, constant-norm vector vacua in gravity theories: (i) axial vanishing of symmetry-inheriting one-forms at bifurcation surface poles, and (ii) curvature singularities induced by position-dependent conicity along rotation axes. Applied to Kerr-disformal bumblebee gravity, the vector vacuum is shown to be non-smooth on axes and singular there; however, a nonextremal branch yields a regular outer Killing horizon and a valid local rotating solution away from the poles.
AI.motivation: To determine whether rotating gravitational solutions with constant-norm vector vacua—such as those arising in Einstein–bumblebee gravity—can be globally smooth and free of curvature singularities, especially on rotation axes and horizons.
AI.method: Geometric analysis of symmetry-inheriting one-forms on bifurcate Killing horizons and axisymmetric spacetimes; derivation of curvature behavior near rotation axes under variable conicity; explicit evaluation of regularity conditions for a three-parameter Kerr-disformal solution in Einstein–bumblebee gravity.
AI.result: Two general no-go results: (1) any smooth, symmetry-inheriting, constant-norm one-form must vanish at poles of nondegenerate bifurcation surfaces; (2) spatially varying conicity along the rotation axis induces curvature singularities scaling as 1/distance. Applied to the Kerr-disformal bumblebee solution: vector vacuum is non-smooth on axes and exhibits genuine curvature singularities there; yet a distinguished nonextremal branch admits a regular outer Killing horizon and a well-defined local rotating solution in the nonpolar region.
AI.conclusion: Smooth, rotating, constant-norm vector vacua are generically obstructed both at horizon poles and rotation axes due to geometric and curvature constraints. While global regularity fails in Einstein–bumblebee gravity’s Kerr-disformal family, a physically viable local rotating black hole solution persists away from the singular axes.

title: Entropy production in Knudsen thermodynamics of compartmented systems
summary:
We investigate entropy production and nonequilibrium transport in a class of random dynamical systems modeling a Knudsen gas confined to a compartmented container. The system consists of a single particle undergoing random billiard motion, with collisions leading to random reflection or transmission through semi-reflecting, compartment-separating walls.
  The stationary entropy production rate is first expressed as the relative entropy between forward and time-reversed path measures. Under a reciprocity assumption, used to introduce temperature into the general random billiard system, it is shown how this information-theoretic definition reduces to the classical thermodynamic formula: the mean energy transferred to the walls divided by their local temperatures, a stochastic Clausius relation. We then develop a modular analysis of compartmented systems. Each open compartment is characterized by a compartment scattering operator and its sojourn statistics. The sequence of compartment entrance states defines a Markov chain whose stationary distribution is used in a renewal-reward theorem to assemble the compartment contributions into the global entropy production rate.
  The framework is illustrated with a series of examples of increasing complexity governed by a generalized Maxwell-Smoluchowski scattering operator and amenable to detailed and explicit analysis. Such operators are defined by a few parameters: temperature, a partial thermal accommodation, the height of potential barriers, and a porosity coefficient. The central example is a cyclic three-compartment system consisting of two thermal walls at different temperatures and a potential barrier. For full thermal accommodation we obtain closed-form expressions for the entropy production rate and net probability circulation around the cycle, revealing a thermal ratchet effect analogous to thermal transpiration.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for entropy production in random billiard systems modeling Knudsen gases in compartmented containers, linking information-theoretic and classical thermodynamic definitions of entropy production and demonstrating a thermal ratchet effect in a cyclic three-compartment system.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous stochastic thermodynamic description of entropy production and transport in nonequilibrium random dynamical systems—specifically, Knudsen gases modeled as single-particle random billiards in multi-compartment geometries—with explicit connections to classical thermodynamics and physical observables like temperature and energy flux.
AI.method: The authors use path-space relative entropy (forward vs. time-reversed measures) to define stationary entropy production rate; impose a reciprocity condition to assign temperatures to walls; decompose the system via compartment scattering operators and sojourn statistics; model compartment entrance states as a Markov chain; apply renewal-reward theory to aggregate compartmental contributions; and analyze explicit examples using generalized Maxwell-Smoluchowski scattering with tunable parameters (temperature, accommodation, barrier height, porosity).
AI.result: They derive a stochastic Clausius relation equating entropy production to mean energy transfer divided by local wall temperatures; construct a modular, compartment-based formalism yielding closed-form expressions for entropy production and probability circulation; and demonstrate a thermal ratchet effect—including net directional circulation—in a cyclic three-compartment system with two thermal reservoirs and a potential barrier under full thermal accommodation.
AI.conclusion: The work unifies information-theoretic and phenomenological thermodynamics for random billiards, provides a scalable analytical framework for nonequilibrium transport in compartmented systems, and reveals emergent non-equilibrium phenomena—such as thermal rectification and ratchet currents—arising purely from geometry, scattering asymmetry, and temperature gradients.

title: Neutrino lines and photon continua from cascade dark matter decay
summary: We investigate the two-body decay of fermionic dark matter, $χ(\barχ)\to X+ν(\barν)$, where the light mediator $X$ subsequently decays into photons. We consider two benchmark models: an axion-like particle with $a\toγγ$, and a kinetically mixed dark vector with $A'\to3γ$. This decay topology produces a monochromatic neutrino line from the primary decay together with a broad secondary photon continuum. A key feature of the scenario is that the photon signal depends on the mediator decay length, whereas the neutrino line is produced promptly and is insensitive to the subsequent propagation of $X$. We derive dark matter lifetime limits from current and projected MeV gamma-ray and neutrino searches, including both Galactic and delayed extragalactic photon contributions. We find that photon constraints generally dominate for short-lived mediators, while neutrino-line searches can become competitive or provide the leading sensitivity in regions where mediator propagation substantially suppresses the photon signal. This conclusion remains stable under conservative extragalactic-only limits and a simplified treatment of Galactic spatial smearing.

AI.tldr: This paper studies fermionic dark matter decay into a light mediator and a neutrino, where the mediator decays to photons; it compares gamma-ray and neutrino-line constraints on dark matter lifetime, finding photon limits dominate for short-lived mediators, while neutrino-line searches gain competitiveness when mediator decay length suppresses photon signal.
AI.motivation: To probe fermionic dark matter decay via a light mediator that yields both a monochromatic neutrino line and a secondary photon continuum, leveraging complementary sensitivity of gamma-ray and neutrino experiments.
AI.method: Analyzes two benchmark mediator models (axion-like particle → γγ and kinetically mixed dark vector → 3γ); computes dark matter lifetime limits using current and projected MeV-scale gamma-ray (Galactic/extragalactic) and neutrino-line searches; incorporates mediator decay length dependence, spatial smearing, and extragalactic background suppression.
AI.result: Photon-based constraints dominate for short-lived mediators (cτ_X ≲ kpc), while neutrino-line searches become competitive or leading when cτ_X ≳ kpc due to suppressed photon flux from delayed/attenuated mediator decay; conclusions hold under conservative extragalactic-only limits and simplified Galactic smearing.
AI.conclusion: Neutrino-line observations provide a robust, propagation-insensitive channel to constrain fermionic dark matter decay, complementing gamma-ray searches—especially in regimes where mediator lifetime strongly suppresses photon yield.

title: Hypercomplex formulation of dissipative scalar electrodynamics and phase transitions
summary: A hypercomplex formulation of scalar electrodynamics is developed, in which dissipation emerges as an intrinsic dynamic property dictated by the extended local gauge symmetry U(1)XSO(1,1). By constructing an effective free-energy functional, we derive the generalized Ginzburg-Landau equations and analyze the thermodynamic stability of the system. Our analysis of the vacuum state up to the fourth order reveals that the constraint on the coefficients associated with the invariants prohibits the coexistence of mixed states, formally establishing the existence of a bicritical point. Consequently, upon crossing the critical temperature, the system is forced to undergo a discontinuous first-order phase transition. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the hyperbolic symmetry induces a structural instability when the effective quartic couplings take negative values, rendering the free energy unbounded from below and creating asymptotic directions of instability.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a hypercomplex formulation of scalar electrodynamics with an extended U(1)×SO(1,1) gauge symmetry, showing that dissipation arises intrinsically; it derives generalized Ginzburg-Landau equations, identifies a bicritical point prohibiting mixed-phase coexistence, and proves the phase transition is first-order and discontinuous; negative effective quartic couplings induce structural instability via unbounded free energy.
AI.motivation: To establish dissipation as an intrinsic dynamical property—rather than phenomenological—by extending local gauge symmetry to U(1)×SO(1,1) within a hypercomplex framework for scalar electrodynamics.
AI.method: Constructs an effective free-energy functional invariant under U(1)×SO(1,1), derives generalized Ginzburg-Landau equations via variational principle, performs fourth-order vacuum analysis of symmetry-breaking patterns, and examines thermodynamic stability via coefficient constraints and asymptotic behavior of the free energy.
AI.result: Reveals a bicritical point where mixed-phase coexistence is forbidden; establishes a discontinuous first-order phase transition at critical temperature; identifies structural instability induced by hyperbolic symmetry when effective quartic couplings are negative, leading to unbounded free energy and asymptotic instability directions.
AI.conclusion: Dissipation emerges naturally from extended gauge symmetry; thermodynamic behavior is governed by strict algebraic constraints on invariant couplings; the system exhibits robust first-order transitions and symmetry-driven instabilities absent in conventional formulations.

title: Probing Primordial Cosmology Through BBN Observational Constraints Under Extended Gravitational Dynamics
summary: In this article, We investigate the cosmological consequences of a recently developed $f(R,G,\mathcal{T})$ gravitational framework, in which the action is formulated as a general function of the Ricci scalar $R$, the Gauss-Bonnet invariant $G$, and the trace of the energy-momentum tensor $\mathcal{T}$. As one of the most reliable probes of the physical conditions in the early universe, Big Bang nucleosynthesis offers a stringent framework for testing deviations from standard cosmology. We consider four representative models that are analyzed and constrained using observational limits on $\left|ΔT_f/T_f\right|$ and the primordial helium mass fraction $Y_p$. The bounds obtained identify the allowed parameter regions for each model and demonstrate that significant departures from standard cosmology are compatible with nucleosynthesis observations. Our analysis shows that broad regions of the parameter space satisfy existing nucleosynthesis constraints, indicating the consistency of $f(R,G,\mathcal{T})$ gravity with the observed primordial light-element abundances and the established picture of the early universe preserving the observed abundances of light nuclei.

AI.tldr: This paper explores cosmological implications of f(R,G,T) gravity using Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) constraints, showing that broad parameter regions remain consistent with observed light-element abundances.
AI.motivation: To test deviations from standard cosmology via BBN — a robust probe of early-universe physics — within the extended f(R,G,T) gravitational framework.
AI.method: Analyzes four representative f(R,G,T) models and constrains their parameters using observational bounds on fractional temperature deviation |ΔT_f/T_f| and primordial helium mass fraction Y_p.
AI.result: Significant departures from standard cosmology are allowed; broad parameter spaces satisfy current BBN constraints on Y_p and ΔT_f.
AI.conclusion: The f(R,G,T) gravity framework is consistent with observed primordial light-element abundances and preserves the standard BBN picture within viable parameter ranges.

title: Holographic spectral functions of exotic spin-1 mesons
summary: We develop a general holographic framework for computing thermal spectral functions of exotic spin--1 mesons. A bulk Proca mass encodes the canonical ultraviolet dimension of the interpolating operator, allowing channels with different ultraviolet scaling to be treated within a unified membrane-flow formalism in the zero-spatial-momentum limit. We test this framework in a soft-wall model with a gluon-condensate background for the hybrid $π_1$ and tetraquark-like $Z_c$ channels. The results show that dissociation temperatures of both channels lie below the phase transition temperatures. Increasing $c$ delays dissociation in both channels, but through different effects: both the vacuum-mass shift and thermal spectral deformation contribute in the $π_1$ channel, whereas the latter dominates in the $Z_c$ channel. Nevertheless, for the same environment, the $Z_c$ resonance dissociates at a lower temperature than the $π_1$ resonance.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a holographic framework to compute thermal spectral functions of exotic spin-1 mesons (e.g., π₁ and Z_c) using a bulk Proca field with mass encoding UV operator dimension; applies it in a soft-wall gluon-condensate background; finds both resonances dissociate below the phase transition, with Z_c dissociating at lower T than π₁, and c-parameter dependence differing between channels.
AI.motivation: To systematically compute thermal spectral functions of exotic spin-1 mesons (e.g., hybrid π₁ and tetraquark-like Z_c) within a unified holographic framework that respects their distinct ultraviolet scaling dimensions.
AI.method: Constructs a holographic dual using a bulk Proca field whose mass encodes the canonical UV dimension of the interpolating operator; employs membrane-flow formalism in the zero-spatial-momentum limit; implements the framework in a soft-wall model with gluon-condensate background to compute thermal spectral functions.
AI.result: Dissociation temperatures of π₁ and Z_c lie below the deconfinement phase transition temperature; increasing the parameter c delays dissociation in both channels, but via different mechanisms—vacuum-mass shift plus spectral deformation for π₁, predominantly spectral deformation for Z_c; Z_c dissociates at a lower temperature than π₁ in identical thermal environments.
AI.conclusion: The proposed holographic framework successfully unifies treatment of exotic spin-1 mesons with different UV scaling; reveals distinct thermal stability patterns rooted in their internal structure—tetraquark-like Z_c is less robust than hybrid π₁ under heating, reflecting stronger coupling to the thermal medium.

title: Analytic HTEE in Moving Plasmas and Its Transition
summary: We investigate the holographic timelike entanglement entropy of a boosted $(1+1)$-dimensional plasma within the AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ correspondence, considering a Lorentz-boosted BTZ black hole background. We solve the coupled extremal-surface equations analytically and obtain a closed-form expression for the HTEE. We show that below a critical boost velocity, the turning points of the extremal surface are purely imaginary, leading to the universal imaginary contribution to the entropy, while the real part acquires a nontrivial dependence on the boost velocity. Moreover, we identify a critical boost velocity at which the complex extremal-surface branch terminates. Beyond this critical velocity, the physically admissible extremal surfaces become purely real, signalling a transition from the holographic timelike entanglement entropy to a spacelike-like real saddle that is geometrically similar to the standard holographic entanglement entropy. The known static BTZ result is recovered in the zero-velocity limit, as expected.

AI.tldr: This paper computes holographic timelike entanglement entropy (HTEE) for a boosted 1+1D plasma in AdS₃/CFT₂ using a Lorentz-boosted BTZ black hole; it finds an analytic expression, reveals a velocity-driven transition from complex (imaginary-dominated) to real extremal surfaces at a critical boost, and recovers static BTZ entropy at zero boost.
AI.motivation: To understand how relativistic motion affects quantum entanglement structure in strongly coupled plasmas via holography, particularly the behavior of timelike entanglement entropy—less explored than its spacelike counterpart—in non-static, boosted thermal states.
AI.method: Analytic solution of coupled extremal surface equations in Lorentz-boosted BTZ geometry within AdS₃/CFT₂; classification of turning points (real vs. imaginary) of the timelike geodesic surface; identification of critical boost velocity via branch termination of complex solutions.
AI.result: Closed-form HTEE expression showing: (i) universal imaginary contribution below critical velocity due to purely imaginary turning points; (ii) nontrivial real part depending on boost velocity; (iii) a sharp transition at critical velocity where extremal surfaces become purely real, mapping HTEE to a spacelike-like saddle; (iv) recovery of static BTZ entropy as boost → 0.
AI.conclusion: Holographic timelike entanglement entropy exhibits a qualitative phase transition driven by Lorentz boost—shifting from complex-valued, causally ambiguous entropy to real-valued, geometrically conventional entropy—revealing a deep connection between kinematics, analytic structure of extremal surfaces, and entanglement topology in boosted CFT thermal states.

title: Spontaneous scalarization around a black hole in a dark matter halo
summary: We demonstrate that in a scalar-tensor theory where dark matter is conformally coupled to a scalar field, a black hole surrounded by a Hernquist dark matter halo can undergo spontaneous scalarization, acquiring a nontrivial scalar field configuration. The astrophysical properties of the dark matter halo directly dictate the quantum-like spectrum of scalar field configurations around the central black hole. Remarkably, the conformal coupling constant becomes discretized and is determined solely by the halo's compactness parameter.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that in a scalar-tensor theory with conformally coupled dark matter, a black hole embedded in a Hernquist dark matter halo can spontaneously scalarize; the resulting scalar field spectrum is quantized and governed by the halo’s compactness, which discretizes the conformal coupling constant.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether astrophysical dark matter environments can trigger spontaneous scalarization of black holes in scalar-tensor theories, bridging particle physics, gravity, and galactic structure.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-analytical study of scalar field configurations around black holes in a scalar-tensor theory with conformal coupling to dark matter modeled as a Hernquist halo; derivation of eigenvalue conditions for stationary scalar field modes.
AI.result: Spontaneous scalarization occurs under specific halo compactness; the scalar field spectrum is discrete and quantum-like; the conformal coupling constant is quantized and fully determined by the halo's compactness parameter.
AI.conclusion: Astrophysical dark matter halos can act as natural 'quantum cavities' for scalar fields around black holes, leading to observable, discretized scalar hair—implying potential new signatures for testing modified gravity with galactic-scale observations.

title: Detailed study of the dual symmetry of dense quark matter within the effective action formalism
comment: 17 pages; submitted to Chinese Physics C
summary: The symmetry properties of the phase diagram of dense quark matter composed of $u$ and $d$ quarks with three colors have been investigated in the framework of massless (3+1)-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) and QCD models. It turns out that in the presence of baryon $μ_B$, isospin $μ_I$, chiral $μ_5$ and chiral isospin $μ_{I5}$ chemical potentials, the Lagrangians of these models are invariant under the so-called dual transformation ${\cal D}$. In this paper, it has been shown that the path integration measure of the corresponding partition functions is also invariant under ${\cal D}$. Consequently, the entire NJL model (or QCD) thermodynamic potentials are dually symmetric. In particular, it means that in the total $(μ_B,μ_I,μ_5,μ_{I5})$-phase portraits of these models the chiral symmetry breaking (CSB) and charged pion condensation (PC) phases are arranged dually conjugate (or symmetrically) to each other. Dual symmetry between CSB and charged PC phases of quark matter is a fundamental property of massless dense QCD; it should be observed in the framework of any approximation to the QCD phase diagram, and have important implications for studies of the phase structure.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a fundamental dual symmetry (D) in massless dense QCD/NJL models involving baryon, isospin, chiral, and chiral isospin chemical potentials; it proves invariance of both Lagrangian and path-integral measure under D, leading to exact duality between chiral symmetry breaking and charged pion condensation phases in the full four-dimensional chemical potential phase diagram.
AI.motivation: To uncover fundamental symmetries governing the phase structure of dense quark matter, especially the interplay between chiral symmetry breaking and pion condensation under multiple chemical potentials.
AI.method: Analytical field-theoretic analysis within the (3+1)-dimensional massless NJL and QCD frameworks; explicit demonstration of invariance of both the Lagrangian and the functional integration measure under the dual transformation D.
AI.result: The full thermodynamic potential is invariant under the dual transformation D; consequently, chiral symmetry breaking (CSB) and charged pion condensation (PC) phases are exactly dual conjugates across the (μ_B, μ_I, μ_5, μ_{I5})-parameter space.
AI.conclusion: Dual symmetry between CSB and charged PC is an exact, model-independent property of massless dense QCD, robust under any approximation, and imposes strict topological constraints on the global phase diagram.

title: Leading Yukawa terms in the three-loop anomalous dimension and four-loop $β$-function of ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric theories for various renormalization prescriptions
summary: For an arbitrary renormalizable ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric theory with a single gauge coupling regularized by higher covariant derivatives we calculate the three-loop contribution to the anomalous dimension of the matter superfields proportional to the sixth powers of Yukawa couplings for a wide class of renormalization prescriptions. Next, taking into account that in the case of using the higher covariant derivatives supplemented by minimal subtractions of logarithms the NSVZ relation is valid in all orders, we calculate the corresponding four-loop contribution to the gauge $β$-function and investigate its scheme dependence. In particular, we construct the so-called ``minimal'' renormalization prescription for which the renormalization group functions have the simplest possible form provided that the exact equations for the gauge and Yukawa $β$-functions following from supersymmetry remain valid.

AI.tldr: This paper computes three-loop anomalous dimensions of matter superfields and four-loop gauge beta-functions in N=1 supersymmetric theories regularized by higher covariant derivatives, confirming NSVZ consistency and constructing a minimal renormalization scheme preserving exact supersymmetric beta-function relations.
AI.motivation: To verify and exploit the all-order validity of the NSVZ relation in higher-derivative regularization, and to systematically investigate scheme dependence of renormalization group functions in N=1 SUSY theories with arbitrary Yukawa couplings.
AI.method: Uses higher covariant derivative regularization combined with minimal subtraction of logarithms; performs explicit three-loop calculation of matter superfield anomalous dimension ∝ Y⁶ and derives corresponding four-loop gauge beta-function; constructs and analyzes a 'minimal' renormalization prescription preserving exact supersymmetric beta-function identities.

title: Gravitational wave propagation in Hořava-Lifshitz gravity

summary: We investigate the generation and propagation of gravitational waves in the leading parity-even infrared truncation of Hořava-Lifshitz gravity, characterized by the modified tensor dispersion relation $ω^{2}=k^{2}+αk^{4}$. Working in the transverse-traceless sector, we show that the higher-spatial-derivative correction preserves the conventional plus and cross polarizations and introduces neither polarization mixing, helicity splitting, nor gravitational birefringence. We construct the retarded Green function of the modified wave operator and derive the radiation-zone waveform to first order in $α$. The resulting signal exhibits a frequency-dependent amplitude renormalization together with a dispersive propagation phase that accumulates over the source-observer distance. We apply the formalism to a binary black hole system in a quasi-circular orbit and obtain the polarization waveforms for an arbitrary observation direction. We further derive the corresponding energy flux, total luminosity, and adiabatic chirp evolution. In terms of the observed gravitational wave frequency $f$, the leading corrections satisfy $Δh_{A}/h_{A}^{\mathrm{GR}}=-8π^{2}αf^{2}$ and $ΔP/P_{\mathrm{GR}} =Δ\dot{f}/\dot{f}_{\mathrm{GR}} =-16π^{2}αf^{2}$, while the accumulated generation phase has the frequency dependence of a relative third post-Newtonian contribution. By mapping the Hořava-Lifshitz coefficient to the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA modified-dispersion parametrization, we obtain $-6.2\times10^{2}\,\mathrm{eV}^{-2} <α< 1.9\times10^{2}\,\mathrm{eV}^{-2}$ at $90\%$ credibility from the GWTC-4.0 posterior.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gravitational wave generation and propagation in Hořava-Lifshitz gravity’s infrared limit, where the dispersion relation is modified to ω² = k² + αk⁴. It confirms standard polarizations are preserved, derives corrected waveforms and energy flux for binary black holes, identifies α-dependent amplitude, luminosity, and chirp corrections ∝ f², and constrains α using GWTC-4.0 data.
AI.motivation: To test Lorentz-violating quantum gravity models—specifically Hořava-Lifshitz gravity—via observable imprints on gravitational wave signals, particularly dispersion-induced modifications to waveform phase and amplitude.
AI.method: Analyzes linearized gravitational waves in the transverse-traceless gauge under the modified dispersion relation; constructs the retarded Green function; computes radiation-zone waveforms, polarization patterns, energy flux, and adiabatic orbital evolution for quasi-circular binaries; maps α to the standard LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA modified-dispersion parameterization (δ₁) for Bayesian constraint inference using GWTC-4.0 posteriors.
AI.result: The higher-derivative term preserves GR-like polarizations without birefringence; introduces frequency-dependent amplitude suppression Δh_A/h_A^GR = −8π²αf², luminosity correction ΔP/P_GR = −16π²αf², and a dispersive phase scaling as αf³; GWTC-4.0 yields 90% credible bound −6.2×10² eV⁻² < α < 1.9×10² eV⁻².
AI.conclusion: Hořava-Lifshitz gravity’s IR truncation produces distinctive, testable deviations in gravitational wave signals—primarily quadratic-in-frequency amplitude and luminosity corrections—and current LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data already place competitive constraints on its coupling parameter α.

title: Scrutinizing lepton flavor universality and transition form factor correlation from charmed meson semileptonic decay into light strange vector $K^*$ meson
summary: In this paper, we calculate the transition form factors (TFFs) $A_{1,2}(q^2)$ and $V(q^2)$ of $D_s^+ \to K^{*0}$ decays by using the QCD light-cone sum rule (QCD LCSR) and constructing a correlation function containing the usual current, in which the twist-2 transverse and longitudinal light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) $φ^λ_{2;K^{*0}}(x,μ_0)$ with $λ=(\bot,\|)$ of the $K^{*0}$ meson constitute the main source of theoretical uncertainty. Based on this, we construct these LCDAs using the light-cone harmonic oscillator model. Subsequently, the TFFs obtained in the large recoil region are $A_{1}(0)=0.579_{-0.028}^{+0.024}$, $A_{2}(0)=0.414_{-0.023}^{+0.021}$, and $V(0)=0.830_{-0.020}^{+0.020}$, and the corresponding ratios are obtained to be $r_V=1.433_{-0.090}^{+0.110}$ and $r_2=0.715_{-0.067}^{+0.075}$. Furthermore, we predict the correlation of TFFs and their corresponding ratios. Then, we extrapolate the TFFs over the whole physical $q^2$-region and calculate the decay widths and branching fractions for the semileptonic decays $D_s^+\to K^{*0}\ell^+ν_{\ell}$. The results are $\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to K^{*0}e^+ν_{e})=(2.05_{-0.16}^{+0.13})\times 10^{-3}$ and $\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to K^{*0}μ^+ν_μ)=(1.95_{-0.15}^{+0.13})\times 10^{-3}$. Meanwhile, we calculated the branching fraction ratio $\mathcal{R}_{μ/e}^{K^{*0}}$ to be $0.950_{-0.002}^{+0.004}$. In addition, we extract values of the CKM matrix element, obtaining $|V_{cd}|_{(e\text{-Channel})} = 0.225_{-0.005}^{+0.005}$ and $|V_{cd}|_{(μ\text{-Channel})} = 0.227_{-0.004}^{+0.011}$. Finally, we calculated the forward-backward asymmetry parameters for the $D_s^+\to K^{*0} \ell^+ν_{\ell}$ decay.

AI.tldr: This paper computes transition form factors for D_s^+ → K^{*0} decays using QCD light-cone sum rules with twist-2 LCDAs modeled via light-cone harmonic oscillator; predicts branching fractions, CKM element |V_cd|, and forward-backward asymmetries.
