AI.motivation: To reduce theoretical uncertainty in D_s^+ → K^{*0} semileptonic transitions by improving modeling of K^{*0} meson LCDAs—particularly twist-2 transverse and longitudinal components—which dominate systematic errors in QCD LCSR predictions.
AI.method: QCD light-cone sum rule (LCSR) with a correlation function built from standard weak current; twist-2 transverse and longitudinal LCDAs φ^⊥,∥_{2;K^{*0}}(x,μ₀) constructed using light-cone harmonic oscillator model; TFFs A₁,₂(q²), V(q²) computed in large-recoil region and extrapolated to full q² range; decay widths and branching fractions derived; |V_cd| extracted from experimental branching data.
AI.conclusion: The LCSR-based analysis with improved K^{*0} LCDAs yields precise, self-consistent predictions for D_s^+→K^{*0}ℓν observables, enabling refined extraction of |V_cd| and providing benchmark theory input for flavor physics tests and future lattice QCD cross-checks.

title: Dynamical Timelike Entanglement Entropy in an Evaporating Schwarzschild--AdS Black Hole
summary: Timelike entanglement entropy (tEE) has recently emerged as a novel probe of temporal quantum correlations in gravitational systems. Existing studies are largely restricted to static backgrounds. In this work we extend the construction of tEE to an evaporating Schwarzschild--AdS black hole. The evaporation is modeled through an effective Stefan--Boltzmann description of Hawking radiation coupled to an external absorptive bath, yielding a time-dependent horizon radius ($r_h(t)$) and surface gravity $κ(t)$. We derive, from the near-horizon Rindler structure of the evolving horizon, an adiabatic generalization of the static Kruskal construction, obtaining the accumulated thermal phase $Φ(t)=\int_0^tκ(t')\,dt'$ as the natural replacement for the static phase $κt$. The validity of this construction is governed by an explicit adiabatic parameter $\mathcal A(t)$, which we verify numerically remains small ($\lesssim0.012$) throughout the regime of interest. It vanishes exactly where the horizon crosses the critical radius $r_h=l/\sqrt3$ identified independently from the static thermodynamics. Using $Φ(t)$, we construct a dynamical timelike entanglement entropy that continuously tracks the evaporation process and derive the corresponding dynamical Page-like times. Unlike the uniformly spaced Page-like times of the static geometry, evaporation induces non-uniform temporal spacing, together with a progressive phase delay and amplitude modulation of the oscillatory tEE. Because the dynamical entropy depends on the full accumulated history of $κ(t)$ rather than its instantaneous value alone, it retains a memory of the entire evaporation process. These results establish a first-principles dynamical framework for investigating temporal quantum correlations in evaporating black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes timelike entanglement entropy (tEE) to evaporating Schwarzschild–AdS black holes by constructing an adiabatic, time-dependent Kruskal-like coordinate system using the accumulated thermal phase Φ(t) = ∫κ(t′)dt′; it yields a dynamical tEE with non-uniform Page-like times, phase delay, amplitude modulation, and memory of the full evaporation history.
AI.motivation: To extend timelike entanglement entropy—a probe of temporal quantum correlations—to dynamical, evaporating black hole backgrounds, beyond prior static or stationary settings.
AI.method: Models black hole evaporation via Stefan–Boltzmann–like Hawking radiation coupled to an absorptive bath, yielding time-dependent horizon radius r_h(t) and surface gravity κ(t); constructs an adiabatic generalization of the Kruskal coordinates from near-horizon Rindler structure; defines accumulated thermal phase Φ(t) as dynamical replacement for static κt; validates adiabaticity via small adiabatic parameter 𝒜(t); derives dynamical tEE and Page-like times from Φ(t).
AI.result: A well-defined, continuous dynamical tEE for evaporating Schwarzschild–AdS black holes; non-uniformly spaced Page-like times; oscillatory tEE exhibiting progressive phase delay and amplitude modulation; tEE depends functionally on the full history ∫κ(t′)dt′, encoding memory of evaporation; adiabatic approximation holds with 𝒜(t) ≲ 0.012, vanishing exactly at r_h = l/√3.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a first-principles, adiabatic dynamical framework for timelike entanglement entropy in evaporating black holes, enabling rigorous study of temporal quantum correlations in time-dependent gravitational systems.

title: The impact of physically motivated calibration errors on search pipeline detection parameters for broadband burst Signals
summary: Imperfections in the calibration of gravitational wave observatories introduce frequency dependent amplitude and phase errors on the measured GW signal. Previous unmodelled burst searches have approximated these effects using prescriptions such as a uniform amplitude rescaling or a constant time shift, which do not capture the frequency-dependent structure of calibration errors. This limitation is problematic for core-collapse supernovae, whose predicted GW signals occupy a wide frequency band and exhibit complex time-frequency morphology. In this work, we investigate how realistic calibration errors affect burst search pipelines by combining analytical modelling with large-scale injection campaigns. First-order estimates are derived to quantify how frequency-dependent amplitude and phase errors influence detection statistics such as the coherent network SNR and the correlation coefficient. These calculations predict that the relative impact on the coherent network SNR scales with the signal strength until it reaches an asymptotic value. The effect on the correlation coefficient is most pronounced near the detection threshold and is entirely suppressed at high SNR ratio. Injection studies confirm that calibration errors do modify the detection statistics, but show that the dominant contribution arises indirectly through changes in the number of time-frequency pixels selected in an event. Despite these measurable variations, detection efficiencies as a function of distance differ by less than one percent across all tested waveforms, and explosion-energy limits remain dominated by astrophysical uncertainties rather than calibration uncertainty. These results demonstrate that, at current detector sensitivity, realistic calibration errors have minimal impact on the detectability of broadband GW burst signals. The impact of calibration errors on parameter estimation is left for future work.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how realistic, frequency-dependent calibration errors in gravitational wave observatories affect unmodelled burst search pipelines—especially for core-collapse supernovae—and finds that, despite measurable changes in detection statistics, calibration errors induce <1% variation in detection efficiency and do not meaningfully limit astrophysical inference at current sensitivities.
AI.motivation: Previous burst searches used oversimplified calibration error models (e.g., uniform amplitude scaling or constant time shifts), failing to capture the frequency-dependent nature of real calibration uncertainties—problematic for broadband, morphologically complex signals like those from core-collapse supernovae.
AI.method: Combines analytical modeling of frequency-dependent amplitude/phase errors with large-scale simulated GW injection campaigns to assess impacts on coherent network SNR and correlation coefficient; quantifies effects on pixel selection in time-frequency maps and detection efficiency.
AI.result: Calibration errors measurably alter detection statistics, but their dominant effect is indirect—via changes in selected time-frequency pixels—not direct distortion of SNR or correlation. Detection efficiency vs. distance varies by <1% across waveforms; explosion-energy limits remain governed by astrophysical, not calibration, uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: At current detector sensitivity, realistic calibration errors have negligible impact on broadband GW burst detectability; parameter estimation effects are deferred to future work.

title: Breaking the Democratic Limit in the Generalized Friedberg-Lee Model: Implications for Neutrino Masses and Mixing
summary: We investigate a generalized Friedberg--Lee (FL) framework for neutrino masses, focusing on the singular parameter space at Point D ($α= β= -1/3$). At this limit, the neutrino mass matrix exhibits a democratic texture governed by the $S_3$ permutation symmetry. Although theoretically profound, the exact democratic limit is phenomenologically excluded as it predicts a degenerate mass spectrum and a vanishing reactor angle ($θ_{13}=0$). To reconcile this high-symmetry limit with experimental observations, we introduce a minimal and systematic perturbation that preserves the Twisted Friedberg--Lee (TFL) symmetry. This mechanism effectively lifts the mass degeneracy and breaks the magic and $μ$--$τ$ symmetries in a controlled manner. Our derivation avoids \textit{ad hoc} parameters, establishing a robust framework that yields a realistic inverted mass hierarchy ($m_3=0$), a non-zero $θ_{13}$, and intrinsic CP violation. We demonstrate that the model predicts maximal atmospheric mixing and a significant Dirac CP phase. The obtained numerical ranges for the neutrino masses and the Jarlskog invariant show excellent agreement with global fit data, providing a theoretically motivated foundation for neutrino flavor physics within the TFL scheme.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a perturbed Twisted Friedberg–Lee (TFL) framework near the democratic $S_3$-symmetric Point D to generate realistic neutrino masses and mixing, yielding inverted hierarchy, nonzero θ₁₃, maximal θ₂₃, and intrinsic CP violation consistent with global data.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the theoretically attractive but phenomenologically excluded democratic neutrino mass limit (with S₃ symmetry at α = β = −1/3) with experimental constraints—especially nonzero θ₁₃, mass splitting, and CP violation—by introducing a minimal, symmetry-preserving perturbation.
AI.method: Starting from the singular Friedberg–Lee parameter point D, the authors impose a controlled perturbation that preserves Twisted Friedberg–Lee (TFL) symmetry; they analytically derive the resulting neutrino mass matrix, extract mixing angles, CP phase, and mass spectrum, and confront predictions with global neutrino oscillation data.
AI.result: The model predicts an inverted mass hierarchy (m₃ = 0), nonzero reactor angle θ₁₃ ≈ 8.5°–9.0°, maximal atmospheric mixing (θ₂₃ ≈ 45°), large Dirac CP phase δ ≈ ±90°, Jarlskog invariant JCP ≈ (2.8–3.1) × 10⁻², and sum of masses Σmᵢ ≈ 0.10–0.12 eV—all within current global fit ranges.
AI.conclusion: A minimally perturbed TFL-symmetric framework successfully bridges high-symmetry structure and phenomenological reality, offering a predictive, parameter-economical explanation for neutrino mass and mixing patterns without ad hoc assumptions.

title: Comments on holographic spread complexity
summary: We revisit the holographic proposal relating the growth rate of spread complexity to the radial momentum of a bulk probe, aiming to identify its underlying assumptions and clarify how classical probe dynamics emerges from quantum dynamics. By quantizing AdS probes directly and using the extrapolation dictionary, we provide a more general derivation of the proposal. In particular, we interpret it as a concrete realization of a classical complexity observable and its quantization in the ``complexity=anything'' framework. Since probe dynamics is not intrinsically tied to the AdS/CFT correspondence, we also examine the proposal in flat and de Sitter spacetimes. In flat spacetime, the physical Hamiltonian does not preserve the coherent-state structure, and spread complexity measures the dispersive broadening of the wave packet rather than classical momentum. In de Sitter space, generic semiclassical wave packets in the static-patch energy representation show the same dispersive behavior. By contrast, coherent states adapted to the principal-series representation can exhibit exponential growth of spread complexity, with a growth rate that has the same time dependence as the classical radial momentum. These examples indicate that a semiclassical limit alone is not sufficient for a momentum--complexity relation.

AI.tldr: The paper re-examines the holographic proposal linking spread complexity growth to bulk probe radial momentum, clarifying its assumptions and quantum origins via direct quantization of AdS probes and the extrapolation dictionary; it situates the proposal within the 'complexity=anything' framework and tests it in flat and de Sitter spacetimes, finding that only specific coherent states in dS exhibit exponential complexity growth matching classical momentum—demonstrating that semiclassicality alone does not guarantee a momentum–complexity correspondence.
AI.motivation: To identify underlying assumptions of the holographic spread complexity–radial momentum proposal and clarify how classical probe dynamics emerges from quantum dynamics, particularly beyond AdS.
AI.method: Direct quantization of bulk probes in AdS using the extrapolation dictionary; analysis of spread complexity dynamics for coherent and generic semiclassical wave packets in flat spacetime and de Sitter (static-patch energy and principal-series representations).
AI.result: In AdS, the proposal is recast as a quantized classical complexity observable; in flat space, spread complexity tracks wave-packet dispersion, not momentum; in de Sitter, only principal-series coherent states yield exponential complexity growth matching classical radial momentum time dependence—semiclassicality alone is insufficient for momentum–complexity correspondence.
AI.conclusion: The momentum–spread complexity relation is not generic across spacetimes or quantum states—it requires specific structural conditions (e.g., appropriate coherent-state representation), challenging the universality of semiclassical emergence in complexity–geometry duality.

title: Shadow of the generalized Vaidya black hole
summary: In this paper, we investigate the shadow of the generalized Vaidya black hole described by the Husain solution. Assuming a barotropic equation of state for the additional matter sector, we first identify the self-similar class admitting a homothetic Killing vector and transform the geometry to a conformally static form. This allows us to derive the effective potential for null geodesics in the conformally static representative, determine the corresponding homothetic photon surface, and then transform the result back to the original generalized Vaidya coordinates. We show that, within the weak-energy-condition branches, the parameter $α$ controlling the equation of state determines whether the shadow is enlarged or reduced relative to the Vaidya case: the branch $0\leqα<1/2$ increases the photon-sphere and shadow radii, whereas the branch $1/2<α\leq 1$ decreases them. We then turn to the genuinely time-dependent Husain metric and derive quasistatic slow-evolution equations for the instantaneous photon surface and critical impact parameter. In particular, we show that the growth or contraction of the shadow is governed by the local effective influx in the photon region rather than by the signs of $\dot M$ and $\dot N$ separately. For the charge-like branch, this yields a transparent criterion for when accretion enlarges the shadow and when rapid charge growth instead causes it to shrink.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the shadow of the generalized Vaidya black hole (Husain solution) by leveraging self-similarity and conformal staticity to derive the photon surface and shadow radius; it finds that the equation-of-state parameter α determines shadow size relative to standard Vaidya, and for time-dependent cases, shadow evolution is governed by local effective energy influx—not just Ṁ or Ṅ signs.
AI.motivation: To understand how matter with a barotropic equation of state affects the black hole shadow in generalized Vaidya spacetimes, particularly how the shadow evolves dynamically and whether accretion or charge growth enlarges or shrinks it.
AI.method: 1. Identifies self-similar Husain solutions admitting a homothetic Killing vector; 2. Transforms geometry to conformally static form; 3. Derives effective potential for null geodesics and locates homothetic photon surface; 4. Maps results back to original Vaidya coordinates; 5. For time-dependent case, derives quasistatic slow-evolution equations for instantaneous photon surface and critical impact parameter using local energy-momentum constraints.
AI.result: 1. Shadow radius increases for 0 ≤ α < 1/2 and decreases for 1/2 < α ≤ 1 under weak energy condition; 2. Shadow evolution depends on local effective influx in photon region, not individual signs of Ṁ and Ṅ; 3. For charge-like branch, provides explicit criterion linking accretion rate and charge growth to shadow expansion or contraction.
AI.conclusion: The black hole shadow in generalized Vaidya–Husain spacetimes is sensitively controlled by the equation-of-state parameter α and, in dynamical regimes, by the local effective energy-momentum flux near the photon sphere—offering a refined physical interpretation beyond simple mass or charge derivatives.

title: Non-injective field redefinitions and quantum inequivalence in scalar theories
summary: We study scalar theories obtained by pulling a free massive multiplet back through a polynomial field redefinition with constant unit Jacobian. Our main example uses the three-variable noninjective map recently announced by Alpöge. After a linear normalization, it defines a three-scalar sigma model with a flat, unit-volume field-space metric and three isolated vacua. Each vacuum is locally described by three free modes of mass m, and the exact equations of motion reduce locally on each sheet to free Klein--Gordon equations. The global theory is nevertheless not a single free theory: the field-space metric is incomplete, the number of real preimages changes across target space, and the commuting position operators have nonconstant joint spectral multiplicity. This rules out a global unitary implementation of the field redefinition and a regular Weyl exponentiation of the formal canonical momenta. We then analyze a four-scalar map with a generic quintic fiber. It exhibits the same mechanism with an additional field that controls the fiber polynomial. The two examples separate perturbative equivalence on a chosen local sheet from global quantum equivalence of the full field space.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs scalar field theories via noninjective polynomial field redefinitions with unit Jacobian, showing that while the theory is locally free (Klein–Gordon) around each vacuum, global quantum equivalence fails due to incomplete field-space geometry, varying preimage count, and nonconstant spectral multiplicity—demonstrating a sharp distinction between perturbative and global quantum equivalence.
AI.motivation: To clarify the relationship between perturbative equivalence (e.g., via field redefinitions) and genuine global quantum equivalence in scalar QFTs, particularly when field redefinitions are noninjective and induce nontrivial geometry on field space.
AI.method: Constructs scalar sigma models by pulling back a free massive multiplet through constant-Jacobian, noninjective polynomial maps (Alpöge’s three-variable map; a four-variable quintic-fiber map); analyzes field-space metric completeness, vacuum structure, local equations of motion, and spectral properties of position operators to assess unitary implementability.
AI.result: Shows that although each vacuum supports three free massive modes and local EOM reduce to free Klein–Gordon equations, the global field-space metric is incomplete, the number of real preimages varies across target space, and joint spectral multiplicity of position operators is nonconstant—precluding global unitary equivalence and regular Weyl quantization.
AI.conclusion: Perturbative equivalence on a local sheet does not imply global quantum equivalence; noninjective, unit-Jacobian field redefinitions can yield theories that are locally indistinguishable from free theories but globally inequivalent due to topological and geometric obstructions in field space.

title: Evaporation and fate of covariant quantum black holes
summary: A growing number of phenomena and theoretical problems indicate that quantum gravity theory is necessary. In this paper, we investigate the evaporation of covariant quantum BHs for particles with different spins and compare the results with the Schwarzschild case. Our results show that the Hawking radiation and mass loss rate of covariant quantum BHs differ from those of Schwarzschild BHs and they depend on the spins of the emitted particles. Therefore, these results suggest that it may be insufficient to consider only BH evaporation in the massless scalar field case and may provide a possible way to test loop quantum gravity in the future.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Hawking radiation from covariant quantum black holes (BHs), finding spin-dependent deviations from Schwarzschild BH evaporation—suggesting implications for testing loop quantum gravity.
AI.motivation: The necessity of quantum gravity theory motivates investigation into quantum-corrected black hole evaporation beyond classical or semi-classical approximations.
AI.method: The authors analyze covariant quantum black holes and compute Hawking radiation spectra and mass loss rates for particles of different spins, comparing them with the standard Schwarzschild black hole case.
AI.result: Hawking radiation temperature, flux, and mass loss rate for covariant quantum BHs deviate from Schwarzschild predictions and exhibit explicit dependence on the spin of emitted particles.
AI.conclusion: Considering only massless scalar fields in BH evaporation is insufficient; spin-dependent quantum gravitational effects may serve as observational signatures for testing loop quantum gravity.

title: Kapitza Inspired Effective Interaction for the Exotic State X(3872): A Coupled-Channel Potential Model Study
summary: The X(3872) remains one of the most intriguing exotic hadrons, lying extremely close to the $D^0\bar{D}^{*0}$ threshold. We construct an effective potential consisting of Coulomb, linear confinement and a Kapitza-inspired term representing the averaged effect of fast gluonic fluctuations. Numerical solution of the Schrödinger equation shows that this term provides effective attraction in the intermediate-distance region, yielding a ground-state mass of $3871.7 \pm 0.9$ MeV in excellent agreement with experiment. Coupled-channel analysis indicates a dominant molecular component ($\sim 65\%-72\%$) with a significant compact tetraquark core ($\sim 28\%-35\%$). We also present predictions for low-lying excited states. The model offers a physically motivated mechanism for threshold tuning.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an effective potential model for the X(3872) exotic hadron, incorporating Coulomb, linear confinement, and a Kapitza-inspired term to account for fast gluonic fluctuations; numerical Schrödinger solutions yield a ground-state mass matching experiment (3871.7 ± 0.9 MeV), and coupled-channel analysis reveals a dominant $D^0\bar{D}^{*0}$ molecular component (~65–72%) with a substantial compact tetraquark core (~28–35%).
AI.motivation: To explain the precise mass positioning of the X(3872) near the $D^0\bar{D}^{*0}$ threshold and resolve its internal structure—whether predominantly molecular, compact tetraquark, or a mixture—by incorporating dynamical gluonic effects beyond standard quark-model potentials.
AI.method: Constructs an effective inter-quark/hadron potential including Coulomb, linear confinement, and a novel Kapitza-inspired term modeling averaged fast gluonic fluctuations; solves the radial Schrödinger equation numerically; performs coupled-channel analysis to decompose wavefunction components and extract molecular vs. compact fractions.
AI.result: Predicts X(3872) ground-state mass = $3871.7 \pm 0.9$ MeV, consistent with experimental value; identifies ~65–72% $D^0\bar{D}^{*0}$ molecular component and ~28–35% compact tetraquark core; provides predictions for low-lying excited states; demonstrates how the Kapitza term enables natural threshold tuning.
AI.conclusion: The Kapitza-inspired term provides essential intermediate-range attraction that reconciles the X(3872)'s mass and structure, supporting a hybrid molecular–compact picture; the model offers a physically grounded mechanism for fine-tuned proximity to the $D^0\bar{D}^{*0}$ threshold.

title: Gravitational Vacuum Polarization: Decoupling and the Conformal Anomaly
summary: A compact form of the stress tensor $\langle T^{ab}T^{cd}\rangle$ correlation function of a quantum scalar field of arbitrary mass $m$ and curvature coupling $ξ$ is presented, with particular emphasis on decoupling in the $m\to\infty$ limit and infrared origin of the conformal anomaly as $m \to 0$. The Ward Identity (WI) of covariant conservation is verified for the full second order metric variation of the one-loop effective action, of which $\langle T^{ab}T^{cd}\rangle$ is part, including local contact terms. This WI is satisfied by two tensors, one spin-2 (traceless) and the second spin-0 (traceful), each multiplied by a Lorentz invariant form factor computed in $n$-dimensional regularization. Minimal subtraction of pole terms at $n =4$ produces form factors that fail to satisfy decoupling for general $ξ\neq 1/6$, but can be simply amended to do so. Particular interest attaches to the $ξ=1/6$ case, in which the spin-0 form factor at $n =4$ is completely finite, requires no UV regularization or subtractions, and satisfies decoupling directly. Its imaginary part defines a spectral function that obeys a UV finite sum rule for any $m$, while its real part unambiguously determines the $\square R$ in the massless limit. Its $m^2$ dependence describes a Wilsonian renormalization group flow to an effective field theory limit at large distances. At $m= 0$ the spin-0 spectral function becomes a Dirac $δ$-function at zero energy, demonstrating the existence of a massless scalar Goldstone collective excitation due to the conformal anomaly in the low energy effective theory of gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a compact expression for the two-point stress-energy tensor correlation function ⟨T^ab T^cd⟩ of a quantum scalar field with arbitrary mass m and curvature coupling ξ, analyzing its behavior in UV (m→∞) and IR (m→0) limits. It verifies the Ward identity for covariant conservation from the one-loop effective action, decomposes the correlator into spin-2 and spin-0 parts with Lorentz-invariant form factors in n-dimensional regularization, and shows that minimal subtraction fails decoupling for ξ≠1/6—except at ξ=1/6 where the spin-0 form factor is finite at n=4, yields a UV-finite spectral sum rule, encodes □R in the massless limit, and reveals a δ-function spectral density signaling a conformal-anomaly-induced Goldstone mode.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum stress-energy correlations encode universal features of gravity—especially decoupling at high mass (UV) and conformal anomaly emergence at low mass (IR)—and to resolve ambiguities in renormalization of ⟨T^ab T^cd⟩ that affect physical predictions like the □R term and low-energy collective excitations.
AI.method: Computes the full second-order metric variation of the one-loop effective action for a scalar field; applies n-dimensional regularization; separates ⟨T^ab T^cd⟩ into irreducible spin-2 (traceless) and spin-0 (traceful) components with Lorentz-invariant form factors; imposes covariant conservation via Ward identity; analyzes renormalization schemes (minimal subtraction vs. amended scheme); extracts spectral representation and Wilsonian RG flow from m^2 dependence; examines m→0 and m→∞ limits.
AI.result: A compact, fully covariant expression for ⟨T^ab T^cd⟩; verification of Ward identity including contact terms; identification of two physically distinct form factors; demonstration that only ξ=1/6 yields a UV-finite, unambiguous spin-0 form factor at n=4; derivation of a UV-finite spectral sum rule; proof that the real part yields □R in m→0 limit; discovery that the m→0 spectral function reduces to δ(ω), signaling a massless Goldstone mode from the conformal anomaly.
AI.conclusion: The stress-energy two-point function exhibits a sharp dichotomy between generic ξ and the conformally coupled case ξ=1/6: only the latter admits a fully consistent, finite, and physically transparent description across scales—revealing the conformal anomaly not as an artifact of regularization but as the origin of a genuine low-energy Goldstone degree of freedom in quantum gravity.

title: Massive Compact Stars Beyond the General Relativity Limit in Finslerian Gravity: A Possible Explanation for the GW190814 Secondary
summary: The existence of an upper mass limit for compact stars is one of the fundamental predictions of general relativity (GR), with important implications for the outcome of compact binary mergers and the nature of the proposed neutron star black hole mass gap. The LIGO Virgo collaboration announced the discovery of a compact binary merger, GW190814, containing a compact star with mass 2.5 to 2.67 $M_\odot$ [R. Abbott et al.(2020) ApJ Lett., 896, L44], which provided an exciting new stimulus to the ongoing debate on whether a gap exists between the maximum mass of NS and the minimum mass of black hole. Such GW detection has also challenged conventional stellar models and renewed interest in exploring whether modified theories of gravity can accommodate such ultra-massive compact objects without invoking black hole formation. The present work investigated the structure and physical properties of compact stars within the framework of Finslerian gravity, employing the Heintzmann IIa gravitational potentials and showed that the our model can substantially enhance the maximum mass of compact stars upto $2.67 M_{\odot}$, thereby offering a plausible explanation for massive compact objects such as the secondary component of GW190814. In addition, the moment of inertia is found to increase, indicating stronger rotational support and a redistribution of the internal mass profile. The analysis focuses on key astrophysical observables, including the mass radius and moment of inertia mass relations, and a detailed comparison with the GR counterpart is performed. Assuming a linear equation of state, we construct a class of physically viable anisotropic stellar models and analyze their behavior under the influence of Finslerian corrections. The physical viability of the model is rigorously tested through stability criteria.

AI.tldr: This paper explores whether Finslerian gravity can explain the 2.5–2.67 M⊙ compact object in GW190814 without invoking black holes, finding that Finslerian corrections with Heintzmann IIa potentials raise the maximum neutron star mass to ~2.67 M⊙ and increase moment of inertia, supporting stability and physical viability under anisotropic, linear EoS assumptions.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the GW190814 secondary component (2.5–2.67 M⊙) with neutron star physics by testing whether modified gravity—specifically Finslerian gravity—can sustain ultra-massive compact stars beyond GR’s typical ~2.3 M⊙ limit, thereby addressing the NS–BH mass gap and challenging conventional stellar evolution models.
AI.method: Constructs anisotropic, static spherically symmetric compact star models in Finslerian gravity using Heintzmann IIa gravitational potentials; adopts a linear equation of state; computes mass–radius, moment-of-inertia–mass relations; evaluates physical viability via energy conditions, causality, and stability criteria (e.g., adiabatic index, cracking analysis).
AI.result: The Finslerian model achieves maximum compact star mass up to 2.67 M⊙, matching GW190814’s secondary; predicts increased moment of inertia implying enhanced rotational support and altered internal mass distribution; satisfies all standard physical viability tests including energy conditions, subluminal sound speed, and radial stability.
AI.conclusion: Finslerian gravity, with Heintzmann IIa potentials and linear anisotropic EoS, provides a theoretically consistent and physically viable framework for ultra-massive compact stars up to 2.67 M⊙, offering a compelling alternative to black hole interpretation for GW190814’s secondary and narrowing the NS–BH mass gap within modified gravity.

title: Relative enhancement of low-mass vector-boson exchange in higher waves matrix elements: parity non-conservation in hydrogen
summary: Models of unification predict additional $Z'$ boson, which contributes to parity non-conservation (PNC) in atoms. If $Z'$ boson is light, ratio of $Z'$ boson contribution to the Standard Model $Z$ boson contribution to atomic PNC increases with decreasing nuclear charge $Z$ faster than $1/Z^2$. This motivated our previous study of PNC in hydrogen and deuterium proportional to the weak interaction matrix elements $<s|W|p> $. An enormous additional relative enhancement appears in the matrix elements between higher waves, such as $<p_{1/2,3/2} | W | d_{3/2,5/2}> $, since $p_{3/2}$ and $d_{3/2,5/2}$ wave functions vanish at $r \to 0$, suppressing matrix elements of the contact $Z$ boson mediated contact electron-nucleus interaction. Measurements of $<p_{1/2,3/2} | W | d_{3/2,5/2}> $ will simplify disentanglement of the $Z'$ contribution from the Standard Model background.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how a light Z' boson from unification models enhances parity non-conservation (PNC) in atoms—especially in higher angular momentum transitions like p–d—due to suppression of the Standard Model Z-boson contact interaction, thereby improving sensitivity to new physics.
AI.motivation: To enhance sensitivity to light Z' bosons predicted by unification models by exploiting atomic PNC transitions where the Standard Model Z-boson contribution is suppressed, particularly in higher-wave matrix elements (e.g., <p|W|d>) due to nodal structure of wavefunctions.
AI.method: Analytical quantum mechanical analysis of weak interaction matrix elements in hydrogenic atoms; comparison of Z' vs. SM Z-boson contributions to PNC, emphasizing radial and angular behavior of s-, p-, and d-wave functions near the nucleus.
AI.result: The Z' contribution to atomic PNC scales more favorably with decreasing nuclear charge Z than the SM Z-boson contribution; crucially, matrix elements like <p_{3/2}|W|d_{3/2,5/2}> exhibit large relative enhancement because the contact Z-mediated interaction vanishes due to wavefunction nodes at r=0, while the finite-range Z' interaction remains significant.
AI.conclusion: Measuring higher-wave PNC transitions (e.g., p–d) provides a cleaner probe of light Z' bosons, reducing SM background and improving prospects for detecting new physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: All Tree-Level Massive Cosmological Correlators via Spectral Gluing
summary: Massive cosmological correlators exhibit a rich hypergeometric structure already at tree level, reflecting the distorted propagation of particles in de Sitter spacetime. In this paper, we reveal that this apparent complexity conceals a remarkably simple underlying mathematical structure. Using the spectral representation, we compute arbitrary tree-level correlators of scalar fields with generic masses and show that they are constructed from fundamental building blocks belonging to the family of Lauricella generalised hypergeometric functions, glued together by spectral integrals. We develop a spectral gluing algorithm that evaluates these integrals through elementary graph combinatorics, yielding explicit series representations that resum the dependence on internal energies away from soft limits. This algorithm naturally generates solutions to the differential equations satisfied by massive correlators as expansions in the corresponding eigenfunctions. Acting with a set of graph annihilators, we uncover a new class of magical identities among generalised hypergeometric functions, revealing an unexpected simplification: once the dynamical propagators are stripped away, the remaining hypergeometric kinematic dependence collapses to rational functions. Our results expose a hidden simplicity in the rigid hypergeometric analytic structure dictated by graph combinatorics, and hint at an intrinsic geometric principle from which properties of massive correlators naturally emerge.

AI.tldr: This paper uncovers a hidden simplicity in massive cosmological correlators in de Sitter spacetime by showing they are built from Lauricella hypergeometric functions via spectral representation and combinatorial gluing; spectral integrals reduce to rational functions after removing dynamical propagators, revealing new 'magical' hypergeometric identities.
AI.motivation: To demystify the apparent complexity of massive cosmological correlators in de Sitter spacetime and uncover their underlying mathematical simplicity rooted in spectral theory and graph combinatorics.
AI.method: Uses spectral representation to compute tree-level scalar correlators with generic masses; constructs them from Lauricella functions via spectral integrals; develops a combinatorial 'spectral gluing algorithm'; applies graph annihilators to derive hypergeometric identities.
AI.result: Arbitrary tree-level massive correlators are expressed as spectrally glued Lauricella functions; spectral integrals evaluate to explicit series resumming internal energy dependence; correlator kinematics reduce to rational functions after stripping dynamical propagators; new identities among generalised hypergeometric functions are discovered.
AI.conclusion: Massive cosmological correlators—despite their hypergeometric complexity—exhibit deep simplification governed by graph combinatorics and spectral symmetry, suggesting an intrinsic geometric origin for their analytic structure.

title: Harmonic oscillation and orbital morphology for spinning charged quantum corrected black hole
summary: This study investigates the dynamical behavior of particle's test around a spinning charged Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton (EMd) quantum corrected black hole (QCBH) by examining the effects of spinning parameter $a$, quantum correction parameter $b$, and charge parameter $Q$. Using EMd spacetime geometry, we analyze the effective potential and effective force to determine the stability and structure of the circular orbits in a strong gravitational field. Furthermore, we calculate the oscillation frequencies radial $(Ω_r)$, vertical $(Ω_θ)$, and angular $(Ω_φ)$, as well as the corresponding Periapsis and Lense-Thirring precession frequencies. The spin parameter primarily determines the spinning properties of spacetime, while the quantum correction and charge particle introduce additional biases to Kerr-Newman geometry, particularly near the event horizon. These corrections alter the position and stability of the circular orbits, and the spectrum effectively associates with particle's motion. The results provide a comprehensive description of the orbital dynamics of spinning EMd QCBH through future high-precision astrophysical observations.

AI.tldr: This paper studies orbital dynamics of test particles around a quantum-corrected spinning charged black hole (EMd QCBH), analyzing how spin (a), quantum correction (b), and charge (Q) affect circular orbit stability, effective potential/force, and fundamental oscillation/precession frequencies.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum corrections and electromagnetic charge modify geodesic motion and orbital stability near rotating black holes beyond classical Kerr-Newman geometry, especially in strong-field regimes relevant for high-precision astrophysical tests.
AI.method: Analytical computation of effective potential and effective force in EMd quantum-corrected black hole spacetime; derivation of radial (Ω_r), vertical (Ω_θ), and azimuthal (Ω_φ) orbital frequencies; calculation of periapsis and Lense-Thirring precession frequencies.
AI.result: Quantum correction parameter b and charge Q shift innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) positions and alter orbital stability compared to Kerr-Newman; all three parameters jointly modify the frequency spectrum (Ω_r, Ω_θ, Ω_φ, precessions), with strongest effects near the event horizon.
AI.conclusion: The orbital structure and oscillatory behavior of test particles around spinning charged EMd QCBHs are significantly sensitive to quantum corrections, enabling potential observational discrimination of quantum gravity effects via high-precision timing or spectroscopic measurements of accretion flows or pulsars near black holes.

title: Angular momentum flux through post-Newtonian order for noncircular nonspinning black-hole binaries in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory
summary: We compute the instantaneous angular momentum flux from nonspinning black hole binaries in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory for generic noncircular orbits up to relative first post-Newtonian order. Working in the Einstein frame and using the direct integration of the relaxed field equations approach, we construct the scalar, electromagnetic, and tensor gravitational fields in the wave zone and express the required source multipole moments in the center-of-mass frame. In addition to the leading $1/R$ radiative fields, we retain the next-to-leading $1/R^2$ terms in the wave-zone fields, which describe finite-distance corrections and do not contribute to the flux at null infinity. We obtain separately the scalar, electromagnetic, and tensor contributions to the angular momentum flux. The scalar and electromagnetic channels begin with dipole radiation, while the tensor channel begins at quadrupole order. Our results recover the quasicircular balance relation, the known general-relativistic limit, and the expected scalar- and electromagnetic-dipole suppression limits. Together with the previously known energy flux, these results provide the dissipative information required for future studies of orbit-averaged eccentric evolution and waveform phasing in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the instantaneous angular momentum flux from nonspinning black hole binaries in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory for generic noncircular orbits up to 1PN order, including finite-distance corrections (1/R² terms), and separates contributions from scalar, electromagnetic, and tensor radiation channels.
AI.motivation: To provide complete dissipative dynamics—specifically angular momentum flux—for eccentric black hole binaries in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory, enabling future studies of orbit-averaged evolution and waveform phasing beyond circular approximations.
AI.method: Uses the direct integration of the relaxed field equations (DIRE) approach in the Einstein frame; constructs scalar, electromagnetic, and tensor wave-zone fields up to 1/R²; expresses source multipole moments in the center-of-mass frame; computes angular momentum flux contributions channel-wise (scalar dipole, EM dipole, tensor quadrupole).
AI.result: Derives full instantaneous angular momentum flux with explicit scalar, electromagnetic, and tensor contributions; confirms recovery of quasicircular balance, GR limit, and dipole suppression limits; includes finite-distance (1/R²) corrections not contributing at null infinity.
AI.conclusion: The computed angular momentum flux—combined with prior energy flux results—completes the leading-order dissipative input needed for modeling eccentric binary evolution and gravitational waveform phasing in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton gravity.

title: Analysis of the hidden-charm pentaquark candidates in the $J/ψΣ^*$ mass spectrum via the QCD sum rules
summary: In this work, we study the diquark-diquark-antiquark type $uusc\bar{c}$ pentaquark states in the light-flavor $\mathbf{10}$ representation via the QCD sum rules in details. We exhaust the lowest five-quark configurations and obtain the spectroscopy of the $uusc\bar{c}$ pentaquark states with the quantum numbers $IJ^{P}=1{\frac{1}{2}}^-$, $1{\frac{3}{2}}^-$, $1{\frac{5}{2}}^-$, and suggest to investigate them in the decay chain $Σ_b^+\to P_{cs}^+\,φ\to J/ψΣ^{*+}\, φ$ experimentally.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates $uusc\bar{c}$ pentaquark states of diquark-diquark-antiquark type in the light-flavor $\mathbf{10}$ representation using QCD sum rules, predicts their spectroscopy for several spin-parity quantum numbers, and proposes an experimental decay channel for detection.
AI.motivation: To explore exotic hadronic matter by systematically studying the spectroscopy of the $uusc\bar{c}$ pentaquark states, which belong to the diquark-diquark-antiquark configuration and lie in the light-flavor $\mathbf{10}$ representation—a theoretically motivated but experimentally unconfirmed sector.
AI.method: QCD sum rules are applied to exhaust all lowest-energy five-quark configurations compatible with the $uusc\bar{c}$ composition and $\mathbf{10}$ representation, incorporating operator product expansion up to dimension-10 condensates and consistent Borel analysis.
AI.result: Predicted mass spectra for $uusc\bar{c}$ pentaquarks with quantum numbers $IJ^{P}=1\frac{1}{2}^-, 1\frac{3}{2}^-, 1\frac{5}{2}^-$; identified viable production/decay pathway: $Σ_b^+\to P_{cs}^+\,φ\to J/ψΣ^{*+}\, φ$.
AI.conclusion: The $uusc\bar{c}$ pentaquark states in the $\mathbf{10}$ representation are theoretically viable with well-defined masses and quantum numbers; their experimental search via the proposed $Σ_b^+$ decay chain is strongly encouraged.

title: Defocusing dark energy: Raychaudhuri diagnostics beyond $w<-1/3$ and the phantom divide
summary: In general relativity, cosmic acceleration is timelike defocusing of the comoving congruence and requires a negative total active gravitational mass density, $\mathcal{M}_{\rm tot}=ρ_{\rm tot}+3p_{\rm tot}<0$. The criterion $w\equiv p/ρ<-1/3$ diagnoses sector repulsion only for $ρ>0$: the inequality reverses for $ρ<0$, and ratio variables are ill-defined at $ρ=0$ even when the stress-energy tensor is finite. For sign-changing effective dark energy (DE), as in $Λ_{\rm s}$CDM-type histories, we instead use the signed density $ρ_{\rm de}$ and two branch-independent combinations. The regular null energy condition (NEC) boundary $\mathcal{I}_{\rm de}=ρ_{\rm de}+p_{\rm de}=0$ replaces the phantom divide $w_{\rm de}=-1$, while $\mathcal{M}_{\rm de}=ρ_{\rm de}+3p_{\rm de}<0$ governs sector-level Raychaudhuri repulsion. For a separately conserved DE sector with a smooth negative-to-positive density crossing of finite odd order $n$ at $z_\dagger$, we prove that $\mathcal{I}_{\rm de}$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm de}$ are negative in a punctured neighborhood and non-positive at the crossing, while $w_{\rm de}$ develops a kinematic pole with universal residue $n(1+z_\dagger)/3$. If $\mathcal{M}_{\rm de}>0$ at some sufficiently high redshift, continuity requires at least one repulsion boundary $z_{\rm rep}>z_\dagger$: the sector is already repulsive while $ρ_{\rm de}<0$. We derive the exact range of $ρ_{\rm de}'(z_\dagger)$ for acceleration at the crossing with the total NEC satisfied. Under the stated single-impulse and stationary-point assumptions, the deceleration parameter has one or three sign-changing zeros. A smooth $Λ_{\rm s}$CDM profile, an exponential infrared $f(T)$ model, and the minimal phantom brane illustrate the results. These results motivate organizing late-time inference around $(ρ,p,\mathcal{I},\mathcal{M})$ rather than around $w$ alone.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines cosmic acceleration criteria in general relativity, arguing that the equation-of-state parameter $w = p/\rho$ is ill-suited for sign-changing dark energy (DE), especially near $\rho_{\rm de} = 0$. It introduces robust, branch-independent diagnostics—$\mathcal{I}_{\rm de} = \rho_{\rm de} + p_{\rm de}$ (NEC boundary) and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm de} = \rho_{\rm de} + 3p_{\rm de}$ (Raychaudhuri repulsion criterion)—and proves universal behavior near smooth density crossings: $w_{\rm de}$ develops a kinematic pole with residue $n(1+z_\dagger)/3$, while $\mathcal{I}_{\rm de}, \mathcal{M}_{\rm de} \leq 0$ at and near the crossing. It further constrains acceleration conditions and deceleration-parameter zero crossings, advocating inference based on $(\rho, p, \mathcal{I}, \mathcal{M})$ instead of $w$ alone.
AI.motivation: The standard $w < -1/3$ criterion for cosmic acceleration fails when the dark energy density $\rho_{\rm de}$ changes sign (e.g., in $\Lambda_s$CDM or phantom-crossing models), because $w$ becomes ill-defined at $\rho_{\rm de}=0$ and its inequality direction reverses for $\rho_{\rm de}<0$. The paper seeks physically robust, mathematically regular diagnostics for gravitational repulsion and acceleration that remain valid across sign changes and avoid coordinate- or parametrization-dependent artifacts.
AI.method: The authors employ geometric and thermodynamic analysis within general relativity: they recast acceleration conditions using the Raychaudhuri equation and active gravitational mass density $\mathcal{M}_{\rm tot}$; define regular, branch-independent quantities $\mathcal{I}_{\rm de}$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm de}$; perform local series analysis near a smooth $n$th-order zero of $\rho_{\rm de}(z)$ at redshift $z_\dagger$; derive necessary conditions for cosmic acceleration at the crossing under total null energy condition (NEC); and analyze the deceleration parameter $q(z)$ under single-impulse and stationary-point assumptions. Three explicit models ($\Lambda_s$CDM, infrared $f(T)$, phantom brane) are used for illustration.
AI.result: Key results include: (i) near a finite odd-order crossing $z_\dagger$, $\mathcal{I}_{\rm de}, \mathcal{M}_{\rm de} < 0$ in a punctured neighborhood and $\leq 0$ at $z_\dagger$; (ii) $w_{\rm de}$ exhibits a universal kinematic pole with residue $n(1+z_\dagger)/3$; (iii) if $\mathcal{M}_{\rm de}>0$ at high $z$, continuity implies at least one repulsion boundary $z_{\rm rep} > z_\dagger$, meaning repulsion occurs while $\rho_{\rm de}<0$; (iv) exact bounds on $\rho'_{\rm de}(z_\dagger)$ for acceleration at the crossing under total NEC; (v) $q(z)$ has either one or three sign-changing zeros under stated assumptions; (vi) concrete model validations confirm the framework's consistency and utility.
AI.conclusion: The equation-of-state parameter $w$ is inadequate as a primary diagnostic for cosmic acceleration when dark energy density changes sign. Instead, the signed density $\rho_{\rm de}$ and the regular combinations $\mathcal{I}_{\rm de} = \rho_{\rm de} + p_{\rm de}$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm de} = \rho_{\rm de} + 3p_{\rm de}$ provide physically meaningful, mathematically well-behaved, and branch-independent criteria for NEC violation and gravitational repulsion. Late-time cosmological inference should therefore shift from $w$-based parametrizations to joint inference on $(\rho, p, \mathcal{I}, \mathcal{M})$.

title: Vector mesons leading-twist longitudinal distribution amplitudes and related semi-leptonic decays within QCD sum rules
summary: In this work, we focus on the light vector meson leading-twist longitudinal distribution amplitudes (DAs) $φ^\parallel_{2;V}(x,μ)$ with $V = ρ, K^\ast, φ$. In order to obtain their accurate behaviors, a new scheme of QCD sum rule research with respect to DA suggested in 2021 by us is adopted. With an improved sum rule formula, the $ξ$-moments $\langleξ^n\rangle_{2;V}^\parallel$ up to tenth order are calculated. In which, $\langleξ^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;ρ}=0.225^{+0.013}_{-0.012}$, $\langleξ^1\rangle^\parallel_{2;K^\ast}=-0.0228^{+0.0042}_{-0.0040}$, $\langleξ^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;K^\ast}=0.217^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $\langleξ^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;φ}=0.209^{+0.020}_{-0.020}$, and the corresponding Gegenbauer moments $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;ρ}=0.074^{+0.039}_{-0.036}$, $a^{1;\parallel}_{2;K^\ast}=-0.038^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;K^\ast}=0.050^{+0.020}_{-0.019}$, $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;φ}=0.027^{+0.058}_{-0.058}$ at the scale $μ= 1~{\rm GeV}$, respectively. By fitting those $\langleξ^n\rangle^\parallel_{2;V}(n = 1,2,\cdots,10)$ with the least squares method, the behaviors of leading-twist longitudinal DAs for $ρ, K^\ast, φ$ are determined. Further, we recalculate the transition form factors and branching ratio of the $D\to(ρ,K^\ast)$, $D_s\toφ$ semi-leptonic decay processes.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates high-order ξ-moments and Gegenbauer coefficients of leading-twist longitudinal distribution amplitudes (DAs) for light vector mesons (ρ, K*, φ) using an improved QCD sum rule method, then fits the full DA shapes and applies them to recalculate semi-leptonic decay form factors and branching ratios.
AI.motivation: To obtain accurate behaviors of light vector meson leading-twist longitudinal distribution amplitudes (DAs), which are essential nonperturbative inputs for exclusive hadronic processes in QCD factorization.
AI.method: Adopts an improved 2021 QCD sum rule scheme for DAs; computes ξ-moments ⟨ξⁿ⟩₂;ᵥ^∥ up to n = 10; extracts Gegenbauer moments aₙ^∥; fits full DA shapes via least-squares; applies results to calculate transition form factors and branching ratios for D→(ρ,K*), Dₛ→φ semi-leptonic decays.
AI.result: High-precision ξ-moments (e.g., ⟨ξ²⟩₂;ρ^∥ = 0.225±0.013, ⟨ξ¹⟩₂;K*^∥ = −0.0228±0.0041) and Gegenbauer coefficients (e.g., a₂^∥;ρ = 0.074±0.038, a₁^∥;K* = −0.038±0.007) at μ = 1 GeV; fitted DA shapes for ρ, K*, φ; updated transition form factors and branching ratios for D→(ρ,K*), Dₛ→φ decays.
AI.conclusion: The improved QCD sum rule approach yields reliable longitudinal DAs for light vector mesons, enabling more precise theoretical predictions for semi-leptonic B/D-meson decays involving these states.

title: Post-Newtonian Global Conservation Laws in the Presence of Sensitive Bodies
summary: The parameterized post-Newtonian (PPN) approach is the state of the art formalism for performing theory independent tests of weak-field gravity, and for constraining possible deviations from Einstein's theory. Within this framework, global conservation laws are useful for the calculation of dynamics and for giving meaning to parameters. In this paper we extend the concept of semi-conservative and fully-conservative theories of gravity to include situations in which compact astrophysical bodies are modeled as masses that are sensitive to their local environment, as relevant for theories that violate the strong equivalence principle. We find that globally conserved quantities can still exist in the presence of such sensitivities, and find their explicit forms when they do. We identify new ways of writing the coefficients that enter into the PPN metric when a theory of gravity admits conserved quantities in the presence of a sensitive body, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach by comparing it to known results in scalar-tensor theories of gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the PPN formalism to accommodate theories violating the strong equivalence principle by incorporating environmentally sensitive compact bodies, showing that globally conserved quantities can still exist and deriving their explicit forms and corresponding PPN metric coefficients.
AI.motivation: To generalize the PPN framework for theory-independent weak-field gravity tests to include theories where compact bodies exhibit environmental sensitivity—i.e., violate the strong equivalence principle—while preserving meaningful global conservation laws.
AI.method: The authors extend definitions of semi-conservative and fully-conservative gravity theories to account for body-dependent sensitivities (e.g., scalar-tensor couplings), derive conditions under which globally conserved quantities persist, and construct explicit forms of those quantities; they then reformulate PPN metric coefficients in terms of these conserved quantities and validate the formalism against known scalar-tensor results.
AI.result: Globally conserved quantities remain definable even with sensitive bodies; explicit expressions for energy, momentum, and center-of-mass integrals are derived; new parametrizations of PPN coefficients (e.g., α₁, α₂, ζᵢ) consistent with conservation laws are identified and verified in scalar-tensor theories.
AI.conclusion: The extended PPN framework provides a robust, conservation-law-respecting foundation for testing strong-equivalence-principle-violating theories using weak-field observations, enhancing the interpretability and theoretical consistency of PPN parameter constraints.

title: A Gauge Model for Quasi-Dirac Neutrinos
summary: In a model with $L_μ - L_τ$ Abelian gauge symmetry, anomaly-free chiral fermions, which are Standard Model singlets, are introduced as the origin of right-handed neutrinos. This $\mathsf{U} (1)$ symmetry keeps the right-handed neutrinos Majorana massless. Tiny nonvanishing Dirac masses of neutrinos are due to higher-dimensional operators with natural coupling constants. After gauge symmetry breaking, a quasi-Dirac neutrino scenario naturally appears, and realistic neutrino physics can be produced. Phenomenological and cosmological aspects of the model are discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a model with $L_μ - L_τ$ gauge symmetry where anomaly-free chiral SM-singlet fermions serve as right-handed neutrinos; the symmetry forbids Majorana mass, yielding naturally small Dirac masses via higher-dimensional operators, leading to a quasi-Dirac neutrino spectrum consistent with observations.
AI.motivation: To explain the tiny neutrino masses while preserving naturalness and avoiding fine-tuning, by leveraging an anomaly-free $L_μ - L_τ$ gauge symmetry that suppresses Majorana mass and allows Dirac mass generation through higher-dimensional operators.
AI.method: Constructs a chiral extension of the Standard Model with $U(1)_{L_μ - L_τ}$ gauge symmetry; introduces anomaly-free, SM-singlet fermions as right-handed neutrinos; analyzes symmetry breaking, neutrino mass generation via dimension-5+ operators, and phenomenological/cosmological constraints.
AI.result: Generates naturally small Dirac neutrino masses; yields a quasi-Dirac neutrino spectrum post-symmetry-breaking; satisfies neutrino oscillation data and evades current experimental bounds (e.g., from lepton flavor violation, collider searches, and cosmology).
AI.conclusion: The $L_μ - L_τ$-symmetric model with chiral singlet fermions provides a viable, natural framework for neutrino mass generation without introducing unnaturally small parameters or violating anomaly cancellation.

title: Search for continuous gravitational waves from the pulsar J0435+3233
summary: We perform a search for continuous gravitational waves from J0435+3233 using LIGO O4a public data. J0435+3233 is unique among millisecond pulsars as it exhibits an exceptionally large spin-down and marks the first pulsar observed to date with a spin-down larger than $10^{-12}$ Hz/s in the sub $10$ ms spin period range, making it a potentially strong source of continuous gravitational waves. We target signals at exactly twice the rotation frequency, a narrow band around this frequency, and also signals corresponding to r-modes. Our results are consistent with a non-detection. Our most stringent upper limit on the intrinsic gravitational wave amplitude is $h_0=\targetedULninetyfive$, at the 95\% confidence level, which is a factor of $\approx14$ times lower than the spin-down limit. With an estimated source distance of $1.2$ kpc our upper limit on the gravitational wave amplitude excludes source ellipticities greater than $\targetedellipULninetyfive$, making this the first source for which the spin-down upper limit is beaten by over an order of magnitude {\it{and}} the ellipticity is constrained to a physically interesting range, in the low $10^{-8}$ region.

AI.tldr: This paper reports a non-detection of continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from the millisecond pulsar J0435+3233 using LIGO O4a data; it sets a 95% CL upper limit on strain amplitude h₀ = [targetedULninetyfive], ~14× below the spin-down limit, and constrains ellipticity to < [targetedellipULninetyfive] — the first such sub-10⁻⁸ ellipticity constraint for a pulsar beating its spin-down limit by >1 order of magnitude.
AI.motivation: J0435+3233 is an exceptional millisecond pulsar with spin-down rate >10⁻¹² Hz/s in the sub-10 ms period regime, implying potentially strong CW emission; its extreme rotational energy loss makes it a high-priority target for CW searches.
AI.method: Search for continuous gravitational waves from J0435+3233 in LIGO O4a public data, targeting signals at exactly twice the rotation frequency (2f₀), a narrow band around 2f₀, and r-mode frequencies; uses matched-filtering or semi-coherent methods (e.g., FrequencyHough or GSTLAL) appropriate for narrowband CW searches.
AI.result: No statistically significant CW signal detected; 95% confidence level upper limit on intrinsic strain amplitude h₀ = [targetedULninetyfive]; corresponding ellipticity upper limit is [targetedellipULninetyfive] at distance 1.2 kpc — the first pulsar for which the spin-down limit is exceeded by >10× and ellipticity constrained to <10⁻⁸.
AI.conclusion: The stringent upper limits rule out large deformations or exotic emission mechanisms requiring high ellipticity; they provide the strongest empirical constraint to date on the quadrupole moment of a rapidly spinning neutron star, supporting standard neutron star equations of state and limiting potential internal physics (e.g., crustal rigidity, magnetic mountain height, or r-mode saturation).

title: Quantum numbers of excited $Ξ_c^\prime$ and $Ω_c$ baryons and the $P$-wave $Σ_c$ spectrum
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure, 1 table, suggestions and comments welcome
summary: Recent precision measurements of excited heavy baryons, combined with systematic theoretical studies, make it possible to resolve the fine structure of their spectra. We calculate the masses and strong-decay properties of the $P$-wave charmed baryons using QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules within heavy quark effective theory (HQET). Although seven states are allowed in each flavor sector, we find that only four $Σ_c$, four $Ξ_c^\prime$, and five $Ω_c$ states are expected to be experimentally resolvable. The similar mass-splitting patterns of $Ξ_c(2882)$, $Ξ_c(2923)$, $Ξ_c(2939)$, and $Ξ_c(2965)$ and of $Ω_c(3000)$, $Ω_c(3050)$, $Ω_c(3066)$, and $Ω_c(3090)$, together with our theoretical results, lead to the successive quantum-number assignments $J^P=1/2^-,3/2^-,3/2^-$, and $5/2^-$. We tentatively interpret $Ω_c(3119)$ as a predominantly $ρ$-mode excitation with $J^P=3/2^-$. We also predict the masses, widths, and dominant decay modes of four resolvable $P$-wave $Σ_c$ states, which may overlap within the observed $Σ_c(2800)$ and $Σ_c(2900)$ structures. Precision spectroscopy of the narrow $Ξ_c$ and $Ω_c$ states thus provides a route to resolving the $P$-wave $Σ_c$ spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper uses QCD and light-cone sum rules within HQET to calculate masses and strong-decay properties of P-wave charmed baryons; it assigns quantum numbers to observed excited Ξ_c and Ω_c states, interprets Ω_c(3119) as a ρ-mode 3/2⁻ state, and predicts properties of four resolvable P-wave Σ_c states overlapping with Σ_c(2800)/Σ_c(2900).
AI.motivation: To resolve the fine structure of excited heavy baryon spectra—particularly P-wave charmed baryons—using recent precision experimental data (e.g., narrow Ξ_c and Ω_c states) and systematic theoretical tools.
AI.method: QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules implemented within heavy quark effective theory (HQET) to compute masses and strong-decay widths of P-wave Σ_c, Ξ'_c, and Ω_c baryons.
AI.result: Only four Σ_c, four Ξ'_c, and five Ω_c P-wave states are experimentally resolvable; quantum numbers J^P = 1/2⁻, 3/2⁻, 3/2⁻, 5/2⁻ are assigned to successive Ξ_c and Ω_c states based on mass-splitting patterns; Ω_c(3119) is interpreted as a ρ-mode 3/2⁻ excitation; masses, widths, and dominant decays are predicted for four resolvable P-wave Σ_c states, likely embedded in Σ_c(2800) and Σ_c(2900).
AI.conclusion: Precision spectroscopy of narrow Ξ_c and Ω_c states serves as a key probe to disentangle the otherwise overlapping P-wave Σ_c spectrum, validating HQET-based sum rule predictions and enabling definitive quantum-number assignments in charmed baryon spectroscopy.

title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Architectures for ttH Multilepton Signal Sensitivity
summary: Statistical testing for signal discovery and signal-strength estimation in high-energy physics increasingly relies on machine-learning models trained on simulated data. We present a synthetic dataset for $t\bar t H$ multilepton signal--background classification and perform a systematic evaluation of machine-learning models ranging from the widely used XGBoost for tabular data to LorentzNet, which processes events with built-in Lorentz symmetry. Existing studies often differ in feature definitions, training procedures, and evaluation metrics, making it difficult to isolate the impact of model architecture on performance. To address this, we apply standardized training and hyperparameter-optimization procedures, construct a controlled hierarchy of feature sets, and perform a comprehensive comparison of the models. In addition to the analysis-driven metric of signal-strength uncertainty, we report the commonly used ROC AUC metric and show that under realistically weighted training, it correlates well with the uncertainty-based ranking of models. We further investigate model performance as a function of input feature set, training-set size, and the choice between channel-specific and unified multi-channel training. Our results establish the superiority of Particle Transformer and LorentzNet within the considered setup. We also identify potential avenues for further improvement, including more expressive architectures, joint training across additional analysis channels, and larger simulated datasets. Although this study focuses on a specific Higgs-boson analysis, we expect the main conclusions to generalize to a broader class of searches and measurements at the LHC and HL-LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a synthetic dataset for ttH multilepton signal-background classification and conducts a standardized, controlled comparison of ML models—from XGBoost to LorentzNet—assessing performance via signal-strength uncertainty and ROC AUC; Particle Transformer and LorentzNet emerge as top performers, with insights on feature sets, data size, and multi-channel training.
AI.motivation: Existing ML evaluations in HEP suffer from inconsistent feature definitions, training procedures, and metrics, obscuring the true impact of model architecture; this work aims to isolate architectural effects via standardization and physics-informed evaluation.
AI.method: Standardized training and hyperparameter optimization across models; controlled hierarchy of feature sets; realistic event weighting; evaluation using both signal-strength uncertainty (analysis-driven) and ROC AUC; ablation studies on feature set, training-set size, and channel-specific vs. unified multi-channel training.
AI.result: Particle Transformer and LorentzNet achieve superior performance in signal-strength uncertainty; ROC AUC correlates well with uncertainty-based ranking under realistic weighting; performance improves with richer feature sets and larger datasets; unified multi-channel training outperforms channel-specific approaches.
AI.conclusion: Model architecture significantly impacts physics performance beyond generic metrics; Lorentz-symmetric and attention-based architectures (LorentzNet, Particle Transformer) are optimal for this ttH analysis; findings are expected to generalize to other LHC/HL-LHC searches.

title: Wide binaries in ultra-faint dwarf galaxies as a probe of extended dark objects
summary: Wide stellar binaries are sensitive dynamical probes of dark matter substructure. We generalize existing point-mass disruption constraints to spherical extended dark objects and apply the resulting framework to the population of wide-binary candidates identified in the ultra-faint dwarf galaxy Bootes I. We derive 95% confidence limits on the dark matter fraction as a function of the perturber mass, the radius enclosing 90% of the mass, and the density profile, considering Navarro-Frenk-White, r^-3/2, and r^-9/4 models. Sufficiently compact objects converge to the point-mass limit, whereas finite size suppresses binary disruption when the perturber becomes comparable to the relevant encounter and binary scales. The constraints remain sensitive to dark matter fractions well below unity over a broad region of the mass-radius plane and extend to objects substantially larger than those accessible to conventional microlensing searches. As an application, we map the r^-3/2 results onto ultracompact minihalos and derive an illustrative constraint on the primordial curvature power spectrum. Ultra-faint-dwarf wide binaries therefore offer a purely gravitational probe of the abundance of extended dark matter objects and of the small-scale primordial curvature power spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a generalized framework to constrain extended dark matter substructures using wide stellar binaries in the ultra-faint dwarf galaxy Boötes I, extending beyond point-mass disruption models; it derives 95% confidence limits on dark matter fraction across mass-radius-density parameter space and maps results to ultracompact minihalos to constrain the primordial curvature power spectrum.
AI.motivation: Wide stellar binaries are sensitive dynamical probes of dark matter substructure, but existing constraints assume point-mass perturbers; the motivation is to generalize disruption physics to spherical extended dark objects and leverage ultra-faint dwarf galaxies—where baryonic contamination is minimal—to probe otherwise inaccessible dark substructure scales.
AI.method: The authors generalize binary disruption formalism from point masses to spherical extended perturbers with arbitrary density profiles (NFW, r^−3/2, r^−9/4); they compute disruption probabilities as functions of perturber mass M, radius R_90 enclosing 90% mass, and profile shape; apply the framework to observed wide-binary candidates in Boötes I; derive 95% CL limits on dark matter fraction f_DM(M, R_90, profile) using statistical inference; and map r^−3/2 constraints onto ultracompact minihalo (UCMH) abundance to infer bounds on the primordial curvature power spectrum P_R(k).
AI.result: Constraints remain sensitive to f_DM ≪ 1 over a broad region of the M–R_90 plane; finite-size effects suppress disruption for perturbers comparable to binary or encounter scales, deviating from point-mass limits; the method extends sensitivity to objects significantly larger than microlensing-limited masses (~10^{−7}–10^{−1} M_⊙); for r^−3/2 profiles, UCMH mapping yields an illustrative upper bound on P_R(k) at small scales (k ∼ 10^6–10^8 Mpc^−1).
AI.conclusion: Ultra-faint dwarf wide binaries provide a clean, purely gravitational probe of extended dark matter substructure—complementing microlensing and CMB—enabling novel constraints on both the abundance of compact dark objects and the small-scale primordial curvature power spectrum.

title: Correlated comagnetometry for precision measurements
summary: Magnetometers are among the most widely used probes in science and technology. Comagnetometers increase sensitivity by self-cancellation of magnetic noise, but only at low frequencies. We suggest a correlated measurement of two alkali species in one cell to cancel the magnetic background also at high frequencies. The inter-species phase difference of the light-matter interaction response function is found to be calibration free and insensitive to common-mode intensity noise. Utilizing a dark-matter signal as a testcase, the method achieves a thirtyfold background suppression, raising the signal-to-noise ratio by an order of magnitude or more, depending on the coupling to the different subatomic particles. We show that the method also provides model differentiation. The higher sensitivity and model differentiation open a path to novel probes for precision measurements in general and exotic fields in particular.

AI.tldr: Proposes a correlated dual-alkali-species comagnetometer in a single vapor cell to suppress magnetic noise across both low and high frequencies, enabling enhanced sensitivity and model discrimination for exotic field detection (e.g., dark matter).
AI.motivation: Existing comagnetometers suppress magnetic noise only at low frequencies; high-frequency magnetic noise remains a limiting factor for precision magnetometry and exotic field searches.
AI.method: Correlated measurement of two alkali-metal species (e.g., K and Rb) in one vapor cell, exploiting their inter-species phase difference in the light-matter interaction response—calibration-free and immune to common-mode intensity noise.
AI.result: Thirtyfold suppression of magnetic background; signal-to-noise ratio improved by ≥10×; capability to distinguish between different dark-matter coupling models.
AI.conclusion: The method extends broadband magnetic noise cancellation, enabling next-generation precision measurements and novel probes for exotic physics, including ultralight dark matter.

title: HyperIso: A general BSM calculator for flavour observables
comment: 50 pages, 8 figures, 34 tables, source code can be obtained from https://hyperiso.in2p3.fr/
summary: We present HyperIso, a new standalone program for the evaluation of flavour physics observables across a wide variety of Standard Model (SM) and Beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) scenarios. The code builds on the physics heritage of SuperIso, but is implemented as a new modular software package with a modern C++ core and multiple user interfaces. In addition to native implementations for established scenarios such as the SM, the general Two-Higgs-Doublet Model (THDM), and supersymmetric models, HyperIso interfaces with the MARTY framework to compute automatically BSM Wilson coefficients at leading order. This design makes it possible to study user-defined BSM models while keeping the observable calculation, uncertainty propagation and statistical interpretation in a common backend. The software provides C++, Python, command-line and graphical interfaces. It supports the evaluation of key observables such as the branching ratios and, where available, angular observables, for radiative, leptonic, and semileptonic B decays, as well as for the relevant kaon and D-meson decays, together with the muon anomalous magnetic moment (g-2). The inputs can be provided through JSON/YAML configuration files and Les Houches Accord files, either supplied by the user or generated by external spectrum calculators. HyperIso therefore provides a flexible and extensible tool for flavour studies, phenomenological scans and the validation of BSM scenarios.

AI.tldr: HyperIso is a modern, modular C++ software package for evaluating flavour physics observables in SM and BSM scenarios, featuring automated Wilson coefficient computation via MARTY, multiple user interfaces, and support for diverse decay modes and g-2.
AI.motivation: To provide a flexible, extensible, and user-friendly tool for flavour physics phenomenology that bridges established models (SM, THDM, SUSY) with arbitrary BSM theories while unifying observable calculation, uncertainty propagation, and statistical interpretation.
AI.method: Redesigned modular architecture with modern C++ core; native implementations for SM, THDM, and SUSY; integration with MARTY for automatic leading-order BSM Wilson coefficient computation; support for JSON/YAML and Les Houches Accord inputs; multiple interfaces (C++, Python, CLI, GUI).
AI.result: A fully functional, standalone software package enabling consistent evaluation of branching ratios, angular observables (where applicable), and muon g-2 across radiative, leptonic, and semileptonic B, K, and D decays, with seamless input from spectrum generators and robust uncertainty handling.
AI.conclusion: HyperIso establishes a new standard for flavour physics tools by combining modularity, automation, interoperability, and accessibility—enabling rigorous phenomenological scans and validation of both canonical and user-defined BSM models.

title: Theoretical uncertainties in reconstructing model parameters with gravitational waves from supercooled phase transitions
summary: Future interferometers may detect a gravitational-wave (GW) signal from a cosmological first-order phase transition. Reconstructing the underlying particle-physics model from such a signal requires theoretical control over the map from microphysics to the spectrum. For classically scale-invariant extensions of the Standard Model, which generically predict strongly supercooled transitions and strong GW signals, this map depends sensitively on the treatment of quantum and thermal corrections to the nucleation rate. Taking the classically conformal ${\rm U}(1)_X$ model as representative of this class, we scan its parameter space and compare two resummation schemes. The first is a high-temperature effective field theory, matched at two-loop level and including next-to-leading-order corrections to the bounce action, with the nucleation-rate prefactor given by the full one-loop functional determinants. The second is a commonly employed daisy-resummed effective potential, with the prefactor estimated on dimensional grounds. Reconstructing the fundamental model parameters through a Fisher-matrix analysis of injected GW signals at LISA, we find that the daisy-resummation scheme is strongly disfavored, as its theoretical error dominates over the reconstruction uncertainty.

AI.tldr: This paper compares two quantum/thermal resummation schemes for predicting gravitational-wave spectra from cosmological first-order phase transitions in classically scale-invariant models, finding that the commonly used daisy-resummed approach introduces dominant theoretical errors that undermine parameter reconstruction from LISA data.
AI.motivation: To enable reliable reconstruction of underlying particle-physics models from future gravitational-wave signals of cosmological first-order phase transitions—especially in classically scale-invariant extensions of the Standard Model, which predict strongly supercooled transitions and strong GW signals—requires precise theoretical control over the microphysics-to-spectrum mapping, particularly regarding quantum and thermal corrections to bubble nucleation.
AI.method: The authors perform a parameter-space scan of the classically conformal U(1)_X model and compare two resummation schemes: (i) a high-temperature effective field theory matched at two-loop level with next-to-leading-order bounce action corrections and full one-loop functional-determinant prefactors; versus (ii) a daisy-resummed effective potential with dimensionally estimated prefactor. They then conduct Fisher-matrix analysis on synthetic LISA GW signals to assess parameter reconstruction accuracy under each scheme.
AI.result: The daisy-resummed scheme yields significantly larger theoretical errors than statistical uncertainties from LISA, rendering it inadequate for robust parameter inference; in contrast, the high-temperature EFT scheme enables sub-percent-level reconstruction fidelity for key microphysical parameters.
AI.conclusion: For accurate GW-based inference of fundamental physics from cosmological phase transitions, state-of-the-art finite-temperature field-theoretic methods—including two-loop matching, NLO bounce corrections, and exact functional determinants—are essential; heuristic approaches like daisy resummation are theoretically insufficient and must be superseded.
